> **Note:** A minimized window fails with `WindowMinimized`, unless `restoreIfMinimized: true`: then the window (or the minimized window it is inside) is restored without being activated, the call waits until two frames in a row are equal (at most 1.5 s, else a `WindowStillPainting` warning), captures it and minimizes it again with SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE, which activates no other window; the warning `WindowRestored` says so. The result's `captureId` is refused with `StaleCapture` while the window is minimized again; to click a point of the image, restore the window and capture it again. While the window is restored the call holds the input gate, like a window tool: it fails with `PausedByUser` while input is paused and with `InputBusy` when another input or window call holds the gate, and it is refused with `TargetDeniedByPolicy` when the [target policy](#target-policy) denies a window the restore would show (a dialog the minimized window owns). A window that was maximized before it was minimized is shown at its normal size for the capture, and the user's next restore may bring it back un-maximized (SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE clears its restore-to-maximized flag; the `WindowRestored` warning says so). A hidden window fails with `WindowHidden` and a cloaked one (on another virtual desktop) with `Cloaked`, also when it is minimized and `restoreIfMinimized` is true: it is never restored, so an app minimized to the notification area stays hidden. The window can be behind other windows.

> **Note:** The window is asked to draw itself (PrintWindow) with a 5-second deadline. A window whose application Windows reports as hung, or that misses the deadline, is taken from the desktop compositor instead (`captureMethod: "WindowsGraphicsCapture"`, warning `WindowNotResponding` with the reason): the window as it was last drawn, which may be out of date, without the windows that cover it. Where Windows.Graphics.Capture is not available it is copied from the screen (`captureMethod: "ScreenBitBlt"`), so windows that cover it show in the image. The same happens, at once, while too many earlier calls to other applications are still waiting for an answer.

> **Note:** `captureMethod` (roadmap M7.1) chooses how the pixels are read. `auto` (the default) uses PrintWindow, and when its image is one solid color (as GPU-drawn, DirectComposition, WinUI and UWP windows often print: black) asks the desktop compositor through Windows.Graphics.Capture, and keeps that frame when it is not one color too; a window that really is one color keeps its PrintWindow image and the `ImageBlank` warning. `printwindow` is PrintWindow only (and the screen copy for a window that does not answer), as before. `wgc` reads only the compositor's frame (`captureMethod: "WindowsGraphicsCapture"`), and fails with `CaptureFailed` saying why when it cannot (Windows before 10 1903, no Direct3D 11 device, a window without frames), or that it cannot be asked right now and to try again in a few seconds (an earlier capture is stuck in the graphics driver, or the check whether this Windows supports it did not answer in time). `screen` copies the screen over the window, covering windows included (`ScreenBitBlt`). Windows.Graphics.Capture needs no answer from the window and leaves the mouse pointer out; on Windows 10, and where Windows does not let the server turn it off, Windows draws a yellow border around the window for the moment of the capture.

> **Note:** `capturedRegion` is the window's real screen rectangle: with the default `includeFrame: true` the visible frame (DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS), without the invisible resize borders that the window rectangle and `bounds` from find_windows include (about 7 pixels left, right and bottom at 100%), or the client area with `includeFrame: false`. A window without a DWM frame (a child window) keeps its window rectangle. So a frame capture's image does not start at the corner the mouse tools' `window` space counts from: pass a point of the image with this capture's `captureId` (space `image`), never as a `window` or `client` point. Convert image points with `imageToScreen`; see [Image coordinates](#image-coordinates). `captureMethod` is `PrintWindow`, `BitBltFallback` when the window refused to draw itself and its visible pixels were copied instead, `WindowsGraphicsCapture` when the compositor's frame was used, or `ScreenBitBlt` for a screen copy.

**Example with a ref:**
> "Show me the Save button up close" (its ref came from capture_with_elements or find_ui_elements)

```json
{
  "name": "capture_window",
  "arguments": {
    "ref": "w4120035e17",
    "padding": 12
  }
}
```

> **Note:** With `ref`, the window is captured as without it (covering windows do not show) and the image is cut to the element plus `padding` (default 8 pixels), clipped to what the window capture shows (the visible frame, or the client area with `includeFrame: false`): a small, sharp image of one control at full resolution. The element is found again through its ref and its bounds are read at the time of the call, so the crop follows a control that moved inside the window. `handle` and `window` may be left out: the ref names its window (an element of an open menu or dialog belongs to that popup's window). A `handle` or `window` that names another window fails with `InvalidArguments`, since the element is not in that window's image. `capturedRegion` and `imageToScreen` start at the crop's corner, and the `captureId` keeps the crop's origin and the window, so a mouse tool given a point of the crop and the `captureId` clicks the right screen point and refuses once the window moved (`StaleCapture`). The metadata's `ref` is the ref the element resolved to: the one passed, or the element's own ref when it was found again under another. When the ref was moved to a re-created element that alone fits its description (see [Element refs](#ui-automation)), the crop shows that element, and the metadata has `refMoved: true` and a `RefMoved` warning. A value that is not a ref is an `InvalidArguments` tool error. A ref that is unknown or whose element is gone fails with `ElementStale` (`AmbiguousElement` when several elements now fit it), and an element that is offscreen, has no bounds or lies outside the captured window with `ElementOffscreen`; a window that does not answer UI Automation with `NotResponding` or `OperationTimedOut`, one that UI Automation cannot read with `WindowNotFound`, and an unexpected UI Automation error with `OperationException`. Nothing is captured then. The window is checked first, as without a ref (`TargetDeniedByPolicy`, `WindowMinimized`, `WindowHidden`, `Cloaked`), before the element is read.

---

### capture_with_elements

Capture a window with its UI elements drawn on it as numbered marks (Set-of-Marks). Each mark is a box around an element and a filled tag with the element's [ref](#ui-automation), such as `w4120035e17`: the same ref every UI Automation tool takes. When every mark's ref has the same window part, as a window's refs do, the tags show only the element part (`e17`) and `markPrefix` gives the window part (`w4120035`): tag `e17` is ref `w4120035e17`, as its legend line says. Pick a target in the image, then act on it with [element_action](#element_action) (`ref`), with no coordinates at all; or click the mark's `center` from the legend with this capture's `captureId`. There is no separate click-by-mark tool.

<!-- tools:begin params:capture_with_elements -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| handle | integer | No | - | Window handle from find_windows |
| window | object | No | - | Alternative to handle: the window as a selector, resolved to exactly one window or refused (WindowNotFound; AmbiguousWindow with candidates). Filters as in find_windows (processName is the whole name); index picks a match in z-order; foreground is the window in front; handle plus filters must still match (HandleMismatch). |
| includeFrame | boolean | No | true | Include window frame/decoration |
| format | string (one of: `"auto"`, `"png"`, `"jpeg"`, `"jpg"`) | No | "auto" | "auto" (JPEG, or PNG up to a 512-pixel long edge), "png" or "jpeg" |
| quality | integer | No | 80 | JPEG quality (1-100) |
| maxDepth | integer | No | 5 | How many levels below the window to read (1-10). 1 reads only the window's direct children |
| controlTypes | string | No | - | Comma-separated control types to include (e.g., "Button,Edit"); matches inside other containers are kept. Unknown names fail |
| interactableOnly | boolean | No | false | Only include interactable elements: enabled, and keyboard-focusable or with an action pattern |
| actionableOnly | boolean | No | true without controlTypes | Mark only elements with an action pattern (Invoke, Toggle, Value, SelectionItem, ExpandCollapse, RangeValue), enabled or not; containers are left out, the elements inside them kept. false with `controlTypes` |
| visibleOnly | boolean | No | true | Only include visible (on-screen) elements; leaves out everything inside an offscreen element |
| highlightInteractable | boolean | No | true | Use brighter colors for enabled elements (dimmer boxes for disabled ones) |
| timeoutMs | integer | No | 5000 | Timeout for UI element retrieval in ms (1000-30000). When it passes, the elements found so far are drawn (`truncated: true`); with none found, the image comes without overlays (`elementsErrorCode: "OperationTimedOut"`) |
| maxElements | integer | No | 80 | The most elements the walk finds (1-5000); it stops there (`truncated: true`, `truncationReason: "MaxElements"`), keeping the levels nearest the window. An element without bounds or outside the image gets no mark, so there can be fewer marks |
| labels | boolean | No | true | Draw each mark's ref in a filled tag at its box (without `markPrefix`, the window part the refs share); false draws the boxes only |
| drawOverlays | boolean | No | true | false returns the clean image, with the marks only in `legend` (and `elements`) |
| detail | string (one of: `"legend"`, `"full"`) | No | "legend" | `legend`: one line per mark in `legend`. `full`: also the `elements` list with `imageBounds`, `screenBounds` and `overlayColor` |
| maxDimension | integer | No | 1568 px | Longest image edge in pixels; 0 keeps full resolution. `imageBounds` are scaled with the image; `screenBounds` stay in screen pixels |
| output | string (one of: `"image"`, `"file"`, `"both"`, `"metadata"`) | No | "image" | "image", "file", "both" or "metadata" |
| outputPath | string | No | temp file | Absolute file path on a drive letter (no network paths) for output "file" or "both"; the folder must exist |
| overwrite | boolean | No | false | Allow `outputPath` to replace an existing file |
| saveToFile | boolean | No | false | Deprecated: the same as output "file" |
| maxWidth | integer | No | - | Deprecated: maximum image width in pixels |
| restoreIfMinimized | boolean | No | false | Restore a minimized window without activating it for the capture, then minimize it again; holds the input gate meanwhile (`PausedByUser` while paused). Without it a minimized window fails with `WindowMinimized` |
| captureMethod | string (one of: `"auto"`, `"printwindow"`, `"wgc"`, `"screen"`) | No | "auto" | How the pixels are read: 'auto' (default: PrintWindow, falling back to the compositor), 'printwindow', 'wgc' (Windows.Graphics.Capture, for windows that print black) or 'screen' (covering windows included) |
<!-- tools:end params:capture_with_elements -->

**Color Coding:**
| Control Type | Color |
|--------------|-------|
| Button, SplitButton | Green |
| Edit, Document | Blue |
| CheckBox, RadioButton | Orange |
| ComboBox, List, ListItem | Purple |
| Hyperlink | Cyan |
| MenuItem, Menu, MenuBar | Red |
| Tab, TabItem | Yellow |
| Image | Gray |
| Text | Light Gray |
| Other | Light Blue |

**Example:**
> "Capture Notepad with UI element overlays"

```json
{
  "name": "capture_with_elements",
  "arguments": {
    "handle": 12345
  }
}
```

**Example with filters:**
> "Mark only the buttons and text inputs in VS Code, with the full element list"

```json
{
  "name": "capture_with_elements",
  "arguments": {
    "handle": 330390,
    "controlTypes": "Button,Edit",
    "maxDepth": 3,
    "detail": "full"
  }
}
```

**Response** (metadata text; the marked image block comes first):
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "imageFormat": "jpeg",
  "mimeType": "image/jpeg",
  "width": 1200,
  "height": 800,
  "windowHandle": 12345,
  "windowTitle": "Untitled - Notepad",
  "capturedRegion": { "x": 100, "y": 100, "width": 1200, "height": 800 },
  "imageToScreen": { "offsetX": 100, "offsetY": 100, "scaleX": 1, "scaleY": 1 },
  "elementCount": 24,
  "captureElapsedMs": 45.2,
  "annotationElapsedMs": 127.8,
  "monitorScaleFactor": 1.5,
  "byteSize": 152884,
  "captureMethod": "PrintWindow",
  "coordinateSpace": "physical-virtual-screen",
  "captureId": "c7-3fa91c",
  "legend": "[w4120035e1] MenuItem 'File' center=(35,41)\n[w4120035e2] MenuItem 'Edit' center=(85,41)\n[w4120035e3] Document 'Text Editor' #15 center=(600,426)\n...",
  "markPrefix": "w4120035"
}
```

With `detail: "full"` the metadata also has `elements`, one entry per mark in the legend's order:

```json
  "elements": [
    {
      "ref": "w4120035e1",
      "name": "File",
      "controlType": "MenuItem",
      "imageBounds": { "x": 10, "y": 30, "width": 50, "height": 22 },
      "screenBounds": { "x": 110, "y": 130, "width": 50, "height": 22 },
      "isEnabled": true,
      "overlayColor": "red"
    }
  ]
```

**The marks.** Each mark is a 2-pixel box in its type's color and a filled tag in the same color showing the element's ref in black or white, whichever contrasts more. When every mark's ref has the same window part (`w4120035`, as the refs of one window's walk do), the tags leave it out and show the element part alone (`e17`), and `markPrefix` gives the window part: put it before a tag to get the exact ref (`w4120035` and `e17` make `w4120035e17`), which the tag's legend line also gives whole. When the refs are of more than one window, the tags show whole refs and `markPrefix` is left out; it is left out too when no tags are drawn (`labels: false`, `drawOverlays: false`). A tag goes outside its element where there is room, so it does not cover the element's own text: above the box's top-left corner, left of the box at its top, or below the box, the first of these that lies in the image and covers no earlier tag and no other mark's box (a box that holds the element, such as a list around its item, does not count). With no room outside (a list's rows stacked on each other) it goes inside the box: at its top-right corner when the box is at least three tags wide (an element's icon and text start at its left), else at its top-left corner, then at the bottom; never over an earlier tag while one of those places is free. Marks are placed in reading order, so the first marks get the first choice. Marks are drawn on the returned image after it was scaled, so lines and the 11-pixel tags keep their size at any `maxDimension`. An element without a ref (no UI Automation runtime id, rare) gets a box without a tag. `labels: false` draws the boxes only; `drawOverlays: false` returns the image as captured, with the marks only in the metadata, for a model that reads the clean image better.

**The legend.** `legend` has one line per mark, in reading order (an element before the elements inside it): `[ref] Type 'Name' #automationId center=(x,y)`, with the whole ref also when the tags leave out `markPrefix`, with `[disabled]` at the end for a disabled element and `[-]` for an element without a ref. The name is cut at 60 characters; a quote or backslash in it is escaped with a backslash, and an automation id with a space, quote, backslash, `@`, `[` or `]` is quoted. `center` is the middle of the element's part inside the image, in pixels of the returned (scaled) image: click it with this capture's `captureId` (for example `click` with `x`, `y` and `captureId`) and the server converts it back to the element's middle on the screen, and refuses with `StaleCapture` once the window moved. Better still, act on the ref with [element_action](#element_action), which needs no point and works on covered windows. `elementCount` is the number of marks. `legend` is left out when there are none. `detail: "full"` adds the `elements` list with each mark's `imageBounds` (pixels of the returned image), `screenBounds` (screen pixels) and `overlayColor`; it costs about three times the legend's tokens.

**Which elements.** By default, without `controlTypes`, only the elements an agent can act on are marked (`actionableOnly`): those with an Invoke, Toggle, Value, SelectionItem, ExpandCollapse or RangeValue pattern (buttons, edits, check boxes, list and tree items, menu items, tabs, links, sliders), enabled or not (a disabled one has a dimmed box with `highlightInteractable`). Labels, panes and groups are left out, and the elements inside them are still marked. With `controlTypes`, every element of those types is marked; pass `actionableOnly` to choose either way. The walk stops once it has found `maxElements` elements (default 80) with `truncated: true` and `truncationReason: "MaxElements"`; an element without bounds, smaller than 2 pixels or outside the image (a frame element with `includeFrame: false`) gets no mark, so `elementCount` can be lower. It reads breadth first, so the levels nearest the window are kept. Narrow the walk with `controlTypes` or `maxDepth` rather than raising it: 80 tags already crowd a dense window.

> **Note:** `imageBounds` are pixels of the returned image (scaled with it), measured from its top-left corner, which is `capturedRegion`. `screenBounds` are absolute screen coordinates. The marks, `imageBounds` and `center` line up with the image with or without the frame. The elements are read before the pixels: when the window moved or resized in between (more than 2 pixels on an edge), the marks are offset from the controls the image shows, so the result has no `captureId` and carries a `WindowMoved` warning; capture it again, or act on the ref with element_action.

> **Note:** The handle only has to be a window, so untitled popups and menus work; their title comes from UI Automation. A minimized, hidden or cloaked window is refused before the UI element walk, as in [capture_window](#capture_window) (`WindowMinimized`, `WindowHidden`, `Cloaked`); `restoreIfMinimized` works as there, and the window stays restored for the walk and the capture. A window whose app the user's [target policy](#target-policy) denies, or whose process cannot be named while the policy denies anything, is refused with `TargetDeniedByPolicy` before any pixel or element is read.

Each mark's ref is the same one get_ui_elements and find_ui_elements give the element, so [element_action](#element_action), [read_element_text](#read_element_text), [wait_for_element](#wait_for_element) and [capture_window](#capture_window)'s `ref` crop all take it.

> **Note:** The pixels do not depend on the UI element walk. When the walk fails, the image is still returned, without overlays and with `success: true`: `elementsError` says why, `elementsErrorCode` is the [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements) code (for example `OperationTimedOut`: raise `timeoutMs` or lower `maxDepth`; or `OperationException` when the app's UI Automation provider failed) and `truncated` is `true`. A walk that the timeout cut off after it found matching elements returns the elements read so far, with `truncated: true` and `truncationReason: "Timeout"`. Only an unknown `controlTypes` name fails the call (`InvalidControlType`).

> **Note:** The filters work as in [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements): `controlTypes`, `interactableOnly` and `actionableOnly` leave out only the elements that fail them, so a Button inside a Pane is still marked, while `visibleOnly` leaves out everything inside an offscreen element. An unknown control type name fails the call, and the error lists the valid names.

> **Note:** `truncated` is `true` whenever the element list is incomplete, and `truncationReason` says why, as in [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements): `Timeout`, `MaxElements` (the walk stopped once it found `maxElements` elements), or `ElementsSkipped` when elements disappeared or their UI Automation provider failed during the walk. Both fields are left out for a complete walk.

> **Note:** A window with a web page (Chromium, Electron, WebView2) is warmed up before the walk, and the metadata carries `accessibilityWarmup` as in [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements) (see [Web content](#ui-automation)). With `status: "NotReady"`, the overlays show the app's frame, not its page.

> **Note:** The walk's `warnings` (see [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements)) are added to the capture's `warnings`: a window that runs at a higher integrity level than the server, for example as administrator, is `TargetElevated`, since UI Automation cannot read it and the image has few or no marks. A minimized window is refused before the walk (`WindowMinimized`), so it has no walk warning.

> **Note:** A dialog or popup the window owns (a Save As dialog, a message box, a menu) is a window of its own. UI Automation shows it inside the window's tree, but the walk leaves it out, as in [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements), so it gets no marks here (with `captureMethod: "PrintWindow"` the image does not show it either). `ownedWindows` lists the handles of the windows left out, and is left out when there are none: capture one by its own handle to mark its controls.

> **Note:** Element names and the window title come from the application and are untrusted (see [Untrusted content](#untrusted-content)).

---

### read_screen_text

Read the text of a window, a screen region or a monitor with Windows OCR (`Windows.Media.Ocr`, roadmap M6.3), for what UI Automation cannot read: canvas apps, games, remote desktops and Citrix, rendered PDFs, text in images. Where UI Automation works, [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements), [find_ui_elements](#find_ui_elements) and [read_element_text](#read_element_text) are faster, exact and give refs. In the opt-in `ocr` toolset: `WAM_TOOLSETS=+ocr` (see [Toolsets](#toolsets)). It returns no image and writes no file, so it is read-only.

<!-- tools:begin params:read_screen_text -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| handle | integer | No | - | Window handle (as integer) from find_windows. Pass handle or window, or another target. |
| window | object | No | - | Alternative to handle: a window selector with find_windows' filters (processName is the whole name; plus foreground, index), resolved to exactly one window or refused (AmbiguousWindow lists candidates). |
| x | integer | No | - | With x, y, width and height: the region's left edge |
| y | integer | No | - | With x, y, width and height: the region's top edge |
| width | integer | No | - | With x, y, width and height: the region's width in pixels |
| height | integer | No | - | With x, y, width and height: the region's height in pixels |
| includeFrame | boolean | No | true | For a window: read its frame (title bar) too. Default: true |
| language | string | No | the user's | An installed OCR language tag such as 'en-US', or 'en' for the first English one. Default: the user's. |
| detail | string (one of: `"lines"`, `"words"`) | No | "lines" | 'lines' (default: each line's text and bounds) or 'words' (also each word's text and bounds). |
| maxLines | integer | No | 150 | The most lines to return (default: 150, min: 1, max: 500). |
| monitor | integer or string | No | primary (no other target) | A monitor (see [Monitor selectors](#monitor-selectors)), or `"all"` (or -1) for every monitor in one image |
<!-- tools:end params:read_screen_text -->

**Example:**
> "What does the drawing app's canvas say?"

```json
{
  "name": "read_screen_text",
  "arguments": { "window": { "processName": "mspaint" } }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "source": "ocr",
  "language": "en-US",
  "captureId": "c7-3fa91c",
  "capturedRegion": { "x": 100, "y": 200, "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
  "ocrScale": 2,
  "lineCount": 2,
  "lines": [
    { "text": "Quarterly planning - Canvas board", "bounds": { "x": 124, "y": 236, "width": 318, "height": 21 } },
    { "text": "Ship the beta by Friday", "bounds": { "x": 124, "y": 270, "width": 205, "height": 17 } }
  ],
  "truncated": false,
  "windowHandle": 1706796
}
```

**The target.** One of: a window (`handle` or `window`), a region (`x`, `y`, `width` and `height` together, physical virtual-screen pixels as in [capture_region](#capture_region)) or a monitor (`monitor`, `"all"` or `-1` for every monitor in one image). With none, the primary monitor is read, as [take_screenshot](#take_screenshot) does. Two targets, or part of a region, are `InvalidArguments` and nothing is read. A window is read as [capture_window](#capture_window) captures it (`includeFrame`; PrintWindow, so a covered window still reads; a window that does not answer is copied from the screen with a `WindowNotResponding` warning, and then what covers it is read too), and is refused the same way: `WindowMinimized` (nothing is restored: the tool only reads, so it takes no input lock), `WindowHidden`, `Cloaked`. A region or monitor is copied from the screen: what is on screen there is read.

**The user's target policy.** A window of an app the user's [target policy](#target-policy) denies is refused with `TargetDeniedByPolicy`, as capture_window refuses it. In a region, a monitor, or a window whose pixels can show other windows (copied from the screen, `ScreenBitBlt`, or from its device context because it refused PrintWindow, `BitBltFallback`; not a window that drew itself, `PrintWindow`, or the compositor's frame of it, `WindowsGraphicsCapture`), the visible parts of the top-level windows the policy denies are blacked out before OCR (each window's rectangle less what opaque windows above it cover, read just before and just after the capture), and `maskedWindows` says how many were; it is left out when none were. While the policy denies anything, a window whose process cannot be named is masked too. OCR turns pixels into text an agent can log and search, so it is held to more than a screenshot, which shows a denied window that happens to be on screen. A denied window on screen whose rectangle cannot be read refuses the read (`CaptureFailed`) rather than go unmasked. Masking by rectangle cannot hide denied content that another app draws (a remote desktop, a screen share), a denied app's child window inside another app's window, or what a blurred (blur-behind or acrylic) window above a denied one shows of it. Layered, click-through, DirectComposition and region-shaped windows count as see-through, so a denied window under them stays masked.

**Boxes and clicks.** `bounds` are screen pixels (physical virtual-screen coordinates, as everywhere), rounded outward to whole pixels and kept inside `capturedRegion`. The capture is registered under `captureId` 1:1 from `capturedRegion`'s top-left corner: a screen point minus that corner is a point of the capture, which [mouse_click](#mouse_click) takes with `captureId` (and refuses with `StaleCapture` once the window moved, or for a region or monitor once the monitors changed, as for any capture). [find_text_on_screen](#find_text_on_screen) does that subtraction for you (`imagePoint`).

**Small text.** On a monitor below 150% scale, text is small in pixels and Windows OCR reads it much better at twice the size: the pixels are enlarged 2x (bilinear) before OCR and the boxes mapped back, and `ocrScale` is `2`. It is `1` at 150% and above, when the scale is not known (the virtual screen with `monitor: "all"`, or a region whose centre is on no monitor), and for a capture over 5 megapixels (the 2x copy would take too much memory). There is no parameter for it.

**Large images.** Windows OCR reads at most `OcrEngine.MaxImageDimension` pixels on an edge (about 10,000). A larger image (a virtual screen wider than that with `monitor: "all"`; an image is enlarged 2x only when the result fits) is read in tiles that overlap by 512 pixels, each word kept once (by the tile whose middle part holds its centre; a word up to 512 pixels wide lies whole in that tile), with an `OcrTiled` warning: a line across a tile's edge can come back as two lines. The lines of several tiles are returned top to bottom, then left to right. Progress is reported per tile, and the call can be cancelled between tiles.

**Languages.** `language` is a BCP-47 tag of an installed OCR language (`en-US`, `nb`), in any case, or a language alone (`en` takes the first installed English one). Without it, Windows picks the first of the user's profile languages it has a recognizer for; when it has none, the first installed language is used, with an `OcrLanguageFallback` warning. A language that is not installed is `OcrLanguageNotInstalled`, and no OCR language at all (or a system without Windows OCR) is `OcrUnavailable`; both are checked before anything is captured, list `installedLanguages` (left out when Windows OCR itself is missing) and say how the user adds one: Settings > Time & language > Language & region (a language with its optical character recognition feature), or as an administrator `Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name 'Language.OCR~~~en-US~0.0.1.0'`. The server never installs a language.

**What OCR cannot tell.** Windows OCR gives no confidence values. It misreads look-alike characters (`l`, `I` and `1`; `O` and `0`), splits and joins words its own way, and reads nothing on a black image: a GPU, DirectComposition or protected window that PrintWindow cannot draw comes back with an `ImageBlank` warning and no lines. `textAngle` (degrees) is set when OCR found the text skewed. Check the outcome of anything you do with what it read.

`detail: "words"` adds each line's `words`, each with `text` and `bounds`; it costs about three times the tokens. `maxLines` (default 150, at most 500) keeps the first lines in reading order; `lineCount` counts them all, and `truncated` says some were left out. The text comes from the screen and is untrusted (see [Untrusted content](#untrusted-content)).

> **Note:** Other errors are the capture tools' codes: `InvalidRegion`, `RegionOffScreen`, `InvalidMonitorIndex`, `CaptureFailed` (see the [Error code reference](#error-code-reference)). A failed read has `success: false`, `error` and `errorCode`, and `windowHandle` for a window target.

---

### find_text_on_screen

Find text in a window, region or monitor with Windows OCR and get click points for it: the OCR counterpart of [find_ui_elements](#find_ui_elements), for what UI Automation cannot find. It reads as [read_screen_text](#read_screen_text) does (the same targets, policy, masking, 2x enlargement, tiles, languages and errors), then matches `text` against each line. In the opt-in `ocr` toolset (`WAM_TOOLSETS=+ocr`); read-only.

<!-- tools:begin params:find_text_on_screen -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| text | string | Yes | - | The text to find. |
| match | string (one of: `"contains"`, `"exact"`, `"regex"`) | No | "contains" | 'contains' (default: anywhere in a line), 'exact' (whole words) or 'regex' (.NET, on each line). contains and exact treat runs of whitespace as one space. |
| caseSensitive | boolean | No | false | Compare case. Default: false |
| handle | integer | No | - | Window handle (as integer) from find_windows. Pass handle or window, or another target. |
| window | object | No | - | Alternative to handle: a window selector with find_windows' filters (processName is the whole name; plus foreground, index), resolved to exactly one window or refused (AmbiguousWindow lists candidates). |
| x | integer | No | - | With x, y, width and height: the region's left edge |
| y | integer | No | - | With x, y, width and height: the region's top edge |
| width | integer | No | - | With x, y, width and height: the region's width in pixels |
| height | integer | No | - | With x, y, width and height: the region's height in pixels |
| includeFrame | boolean | No | true | For a window: read its frame (title bar) too. Default: true |
| language | string | No | the user's | An installed OCR language tag such as 'en-US', or 'en' for the first English one. Default: the user's. |
| maxResults | integer | No | 20 | The most matches to return (default: 20, min: 1, max: 100). |
| monitor | integer or string | No | primary (no other target) | A monitor (see [Monitor selectors](#monitor-selectors)), or `"all"` (or -1) for every monitor in one image |
<!-- tools:end params:find_text_on_screen -->

**Example:**
> "Click 'Canvas board' in the drawing app"

```json
{
  "name": "find_text_on_screen",
  "arguments": { "text": "Canvas board", "window": { "processName": "mspaint" } }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "source": "ocr",
  "language": "en-US",
  "captureId": "c8-3fa91c",
  "capturedRegion": { "x": 100, "y": 200, "width": 1280, "height": 800 },
  "ocrScale": 2,
  "matchCount": 1,
  "matches": [
    {
      "text": "Canvas board",
      "line": "Quarterly planning - Canvas board",
      "bounds": { "x": 336, "y": 236, "width": 106, "height": 21 },
      "clickPoint": { "x": 389, "y": 246 },
      "imagePoint": { "x": 289, "y": 46 }
    }
  ],
  "truncated": false,
  "windowHandle": 1706796
}
```

Then click it through the capture, so the click is refused if the window moved since:

```json
{
  "name": "mouse_click",
  "arguments": { "x": 289, "y": 46, "captureId": "c8-3fa91c" }
}
```

**Matching.** `match: "contains"` (default) finds `text` anywhere in a line, even inside a word; `"exact"` only as whole words (one word, or a run of words: `save as` matches `Save As` but not `Autosave Assets`; punctuation OCR reads as part of a word, as in `(OK)` or `OK.`, is ignored at its edges). Both ignore case unless `caseSensitive`, and treat every run of whitespace as one space, since OCR spaces words its own way; they ignore it inside a number and between a number and its unit, which Windows OCR often splits (`4711km` finds `471 1 km`, and `4711 km` finds `4711km`), and between the words of Chinese, Japanese and Thai, which it joins with spaces. `"regex"` runs a .NET regular expression on each line as OCR read it (culture-invariant, ignoring case unless `caseSensitive`, at most 100 ms per line); an invalid pattern, or one that runs too long, is `InvalidArguments`. Empty text, or only whitespace for contains and exact, is `InvalidArguments` too; text that is invalid is refused before anything is read.

**Matches.** Each match has the matched `text` as OCR read it, the `line` it is in, its `bounds` in screen pixels (the words it covers; part of a word is boxed by its share of the word's width, since OCR gives no box per character), `clickPoint` (the centre on the screen) and `imagePoint` (the same point in the capture: pass it as `x`, `y` to [mouse_click](#mouse_click) with `captureId`). Matches are ordered top to bottom, then left to right; `maxResults` (default 20, at most 100) keeps the first, `matchCount` counts them all and `truncated` says some were left out. No match is a success with `matches: []` and a `hint`: OCR may have read the text differently (try `contains` with a shorter part, or read the window with [read_screen_text](#read_screen_text) to see what OCR read).

> **Note:** A click point from OCR is only as good as OCR's box: prefer an element ref ([find_ui_elements](#find_ui_elements), [element_action](#element_action)) whenever UI Automation shows the element, and check the outcome of the click.

---

### wait_for_visual

> In the `visual` toolset, off by default (roadmap M6.4): `WAM_TOOLSETS=+visual` serves it.

Wait on the server until a window, a screen region or a monitor changes on screen, or stops changing, for when UI Automation has nothing to wait on: a canvas app, a game, a remote desktop, a chart that renders, a page that settles. It costs no image tokens: the server compares the frames itself and returns rectangles of where they changed, never an image or a file. Read-only: it runs outside the input gate (input and window calls go ahead while it waits), and it keeps working while input is paused. When there is an element or a window to wait on, [wait_for_element](#wait_for_element) and [wait_for_window](#wait_for_window) say more, and say it exactly.

<!-- tools:begin params:wait_for_visual -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| condition | string (one of: `"changed"`, `"stable"`) | No | "changed" | changed (default) or stable |
| handle | integer | No | - | Window handle (as integer) from find_windows. Pass handle or window, not both |
| window | object | No | - | Alternative to handle: a window selector with find_windows' filters (processName is the whole name; plus foreground, index), resolved to exactly one window or refused (AmbiguousWindow lists candidates). |
| includeFrame | boolean | No | - | With a window: whether the frame (title bar, borders) is watched too. Default: true |
| x | integer | No | - | Region: X of its left edge in screen pixels; with y, width and height |
| y | integer | No | - | Region: Y of its top edge |
| width | integer | No | - | Region: width in pixels |
| height | integer | No | - | Region: height in pixels |
| since | string | No | - | A captureId from a capture taken before you acted (output 'metadata' costs no image): the baseline, and the target (its window, region or monitor). Alone, not with another target |
| timeoutMs | integer | No | 10000 | How long to wait in milliseconds (default: 10000, min: 0, max: 60000); 0 compares once, with since |
| pollMs | integer | No | 200 | Milliseconds from one frame to the next (default: 200, min: 100, max: 2000) |
| stableMs | integer | No | - | stable only: how long nothing may change, in milliseconds (default: 500, min: 0, max: 10000; at most timeoutMs) |
| minChangedPercent | number | No | 0 | A frame counts as changed only when more than this share of its tiles changed, in percent (default: 0, any tile; min: 0, below 100): raise it a little to ignore a clock or a spinner |
| monitor | integer or string | No | - | A monitor (see [Monitor selectors](#monitor-selectors)), or `"all"` (or -1) for all of them (at most 32 megapixels) |
<!-- tools:end params:wait_for_visual -->

**One target.** Pass exactly one of these, or the call is `InvalidArguments`:

| Target | Read as | Refused with |
|--------|---------|--------------|
| `handle` or `window` (with `includeFrame`) | As [capture_window](#capture_window) reads it: the window draws itself (PrintWindow), so windows that cover it do not count, cut to its visible frame (or its client area with `includeFrame: false`). A window that stops answering is copied from the screen for the rest of the wait (`captureMethod: "ScreenBitBlt"`, warning `WindowNotResponding`) | `TargetDeniedByPolicy` (the user's [target policy](#target-policy) denies its app), `InvalidHandle`, `WindowMinimized`, `WindowHidden`, `Cloaked` (at the start; later, see the reasons below) |
| `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` | As [capture_region](#capture_region) reads it: copied from the screen, cut to the screen (warning `RegionClipped`) | `InvalidRegion`, `RegionOffScreen` |
| `monitor` | As [take_screenshot](#take_screenshot) reads it ([Monitor selectors](#monitor-selectors)); `"all"` (or -1) is every monitor | `InvalidMonitorIndex`, `MonitorNotFound`, `AmbiguousMonitor` |
| `since` alone | The target of the capture with that `captureId`: its window (with the capture's `includeFrame`), or its screen rectangle for a monitor or region capture. The capture is also the baseline (see below) | `CaptureNotFound`; `TargetDeniedByPolicy` for a window |

A region or monitor (also through `since`) is at most 32 megapixels (one 8K monitor; `InvalidRegion` otherwise), since every check reads all of it: watch a monitor, a window or a part of the screen rather than a large virtual screen.

**Windows the policy denies, over a region or monitor** (owner decision D8). A screen read shows whatever is there, so every window the user's [target policy](#target-policy) denies (or whose process cannot be named while the policy denies anything) that lies over the area during the wait is left out of the comparison, with its whole window rectangle, and listed in `maskedWindows` (`handle`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`). Nothing it shows counts as a change, and a rectangle it had once stays left out for the rest of the wait, so a denied window that moves shows at neither place. Windows that cover a denied one lose that part too. A capture's signature keeps the rectangles it left out, so a `since` on a region or monitor capture (or on a wait's last frame) leaves them out too, even after the denied window closed or moved. A window target of a denied app is refused instead; a window target that stops answering, and so is copied from the screen, leaves out the denied windows over it in the same way, as does one that refuses PrintWindow, whose device context is copied instead (`captureMethod` `BitBltFallback`, which can show the windows that cover it).

**How frames compare.** Each check keeps a hash of every 16 x 16 tile of the frame (its blue, green and red), not the pixels, and two frames of the same size compare tile by tile, so any changed pixel counts: a hover color of the same brightness, or one word replaced by another. `changedPercent` is the share of the tiles compared that changed, and `changedRegions` the changed tiles merged into at most 8 rectangles of touching tiles, in screen pixels, largest first (the last one joins the smallest when there are more). A frame counts as changed when more than `minChangedPercent` of its tiles changed (default 0: any tile); raise it a little to ignore a clock or a spinner in a corner. The text caret the window's thread reports (the target window's, or for a region or monitor the window in front's) is left out with a 2-pixel margin where it is in both frames compared, so a blinking caret is no change, but text typed at it, which moves it, is; WPF and Chromium report theirs too, though they draw it themselves. Against a capture (`since`), whose caret is unknown, the caret is left out where it is now. In a window that Windows scales for its DPI the reported caret can be off its drawn place (warning `DpiScaledWindow`). A window that moved without resizing compares by content.

| `condition` | Satisfied when | `reason` |
|-------------|----------------|----------|
| `changed` (default) | A frame differs from the baseline by more than `minChangedPercent`: from `since`'s capture, or without `since` from the wait's first frame. A window that resized (or an area whose size changed) is a change of 100 %; a window that closed, was minimized, hidden or cloaked counts as a change too: a visible effect of the action (a frame of one color that would count as a change is checked against the window first, so a minimize right before a read reads as `minimized`) | `pixels`, `resized`, `closed`, `minimized` or `hidden` |
| `stable` | No frame differed from the one before it (by more than `minChangedPercent`) for `stableMs` (default 500), counted from the wait's first frame, which is compared with the next; with `since`, its capture is that first frame, so `stableMs: 0` needs one frame. A resize starts the time again; a window that closes, is minimized, hidden or cloaked ends the wait with its code (`InvalidHandle`, `WindowMinimized`, `WindowHidden`, `Cloaked`) | - (`stableForMs` says how long) |

**Catching the change your action makes.** Without `since`, the baseline is the wait's first frame, taken after your action: a change that is already on the screen is part of the baseline, and the wait times out. Capture the target before you act with `output: "metadata"` (no image, no image tokens) and pass its `captureId` as `since`:

1. `capture_window` with `handle` and `output: "metadata"`: `captureId` `c7-3fa91c`.
2. Act: `mouse_click`, `press_keys`, ...
3. `wait_for_visual` with `since: "c7-3fa91c"`.

A capture keeps what `since` compares with (its visual signature) only when it was taken while wait_for_visual is served (owner decision D9), of a whole window, region or monitor (not a [capture_window](#capture_window) crop to a `ref`, nor a capture of a window that `restoreIfMinimized` restored, which is minimized again after it), for as long as its `captureId` lives (10 minutes, the 32 most recent). The signatures together take at most 16 MB: past that, the least recently used captures lose their signatures but keep their `captureId` for the mouse tools. A `since` without a signature is `CaptureNotFound`, and `error` says why. `timeoutMs: 0` with `since` compares once, as a comparison of two captures would; `timeoutMs: 0` without `since` is `InvalidArguments`.

**The last frame.** The result's `captureId` is the wait's last frame, registered as a capture without an image (`capturedRegion`, a 1:1 transform): pass it as the next wait's `since` to wait for the next change, or to [mouse_click](#mouse_click) with an image point of the frame (the point in screen pixels less `capturedRegion`'s corner). It counts as one of the 32 captures kept, so many waits can push out a capture you meant to click on; a wait whose last frame shows what `since`'s capture showed returns `since`'s `captureId` instead and registers nothing. A window that closed, was minimized or hidden has none, and neither has a screen frame whose monitors could not be read.

**Timing.** A frame is read every `pollMs` (default 200, 100 to 2000) until the condition holds or `timeoutMs` (default 10000, at most 60000) has passed; a frame that takes longer to read than `pollMs` is followed by the next at once. `stableMs` is 0 to 10000 and at most `timeoutMs`, and only for `stable`; a `stable` wait counts `timeoutMs` from its first frame, so a `stableMs` as long as `timeoutMs` can be met. Out-of-range values are refused (`InvalidArguments`), never clamped. A client that sends a progress token gets a progress notification about once a second (`progress` is the milliseconds waited, `total` is `timeoutMs`), and a cancelled call stops before its next frame (see [Cancellation and progress](#cancellation-and-progress)).

**Warnings** (each starts with its code): `WindowNotResponding` (the window is copied from the screen from then on, so a window that covers it shows), `DpiScaledWindow` (Windows scales the window, so the frames can show it at its unscaled size and `changedRegions` can be offset from the screen; watch its region instead), `RegionClipped`, and `ImageBlank` when every pixel of the last frame has one color: GPU or protected content this read cannot see, or a window that has not painted yet. Such a target never changes, so `stable` is satisfied as soon as `stableMs` has passed and means little. `BaselineReset` when the wait starts again from a frame because it was read another way than its baseline (a window that stopped answering is copied from the screen, or `since`'s capture was, and the two reads differ where nothing changed): a change made before that frame is missed.

**Outcomes.** A wait that is not satisfied is a failure (`success: false`, so the call goes out with `isError: true`, see [Tool errors](#tool-errors)); the result still says what was seen.

| Outcome | errorCode | Result |
|---------|-----------|--------|
| Satisfied | - | `success` and `satisfied` `true`, `condition`, `elapsedMs`, `checks`; for `changed` `reason`, and for `pixels` and `resized` `changedPercent` and `changedRegions` (the window's last place for `closed`, `minimized` and `hidden`); for `stable` `stableForMs`; `captureId`, `capturedRegion` and `captureMethod` of the last frame; `maskedWindows` and `warnings` when there are any |
| Timed out | `WaitTimedOut` | `timedOut` `true`. `changed`: `changedPercent` of the last frame (0 when nothing changed) and the `changedRegions` of a change too small to count. `stable`: the `changedPercent` and `changedRegions` of the last change, what kept moving. `captureId` of the last frame. `error` says what was seen and, for `changed`, how to catch a change made before the wait |
| The target cannot be watched | `TargetDeniedByPolicy`, `InvalidHandle`, `WindowMinimized`, `WindowHidden`, `Cloaked`, `InvalidRegion`, `RegionOffScreen`, `InvalidMonitorIndex`, `CaptureNotFound`, `StaleCapture` (`since`'s region or monitor is no longer all on the screen) | At the start; nothing was waited for. During a `stable` wait the window codes end it |
| The pixels cannot be read | `CaptureFailed` | Windows could not read the window or the screen (a secure desktop, a window over the capture budget); `error` has the reason |
| An argument that cannot be used | `InvalidArguments` (tool error) | No target or two, half a region, `includeFrame` without a window, an empty `since`, `timeoutMs` outside 0-60000, `pollMs` outside 100-2000, `stableMs` outside 0-10000, over `timeoutMs` or with `changed`, `minChangedPercent` outside 0 to below 100, or `timeoutMs: 0` without `since`. A window selector that names no single window: `WindowNotFound`, `AmbiguousWindow` |

**Example:**
> "Click Render, then wait until the chart has changed."

```json
{
  "name": "wait_for_visual",
  "arguments": { "since": "c7-3fa91c" }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "satisfied": true,
  "timedOut": false,
  "condition": "changed",
  "elapsedMs": 412,
  "checks": 3,
  "reason": "pixels",
  "changedPercent": 0.42,
  "changedRegions": [
    { "x": 288, "y": 116, "width": 64, "height": 48 },
    { "x": 1040, "y": 948, "width": 192, "height": 16 }
  ],
  "captureId": "c9-3fa91c",
  "capturedRegion": { "x": 0, "y": 100, "width": 1600, "height": 900 },
  "captureMethod": "PrintWindow"
}
```

A `stable` wait that timed out on a spinner (`isError: true`):

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "satisfied": false,
  "timedOut": true,
  "condition": "stable",
  "elapsedMs": 3000,
  "checks": 16,
  "changedPercent": 0.21,
  "changedRegions": [ { "x": 784, "y": 532, "width": 32, "height": 32 } ],
  "captureId": "c10-3fa91c",
  "capturedRegion": { "x": 0, "y": 100, "width": 1600, "height": 900 },
  "captureMethod": "PrintWindow",
  "error": "The target kept changing for 3000 ms (16 checks); changedRegions shows the last change. Raise minChangedPercent to ignore a small animation, or watch a smaller region.",
  "errorCode": "WaitTimedOut"
}
```

---

## UI Automation

Tools for reading UI elements through Windows UI Automation: one observation of the desktop with the elements of a window ([get_desktop_state](#get_desktop_state), the first call to make), the element tree of a window, a search for elements by name, automation id, control type and class (also in the window's open menus, dropdowns and dialogs), the element that has keyboard focus, the element at a screen point, an app's open popups, an element's text and a table's cells, and a wait for an element's state. They only read; none of them clicks, types or changes focus. [element_action](#element_action) acts on an element they found, through its UI Automation patterns (also along a menu path), and [respond_to_dialog](#respond_to_dialog) and [file_dialog](#file_dialog) answer a dialog and complete an Open or Save As dialog through it. Every read runs under a timeout, because an application that hangs can block UI Automation indefinitely.

**Element refs.** Every element these tools return (and every element of [capture_with_elements](#capture_with_elements)) carries a `ref`, such as `w4120035e17`: a short name for that element that later calls use instead of coordinates or a repeated search ([element_action](#element_action), [wait_for_element](#wait_for_element), [read_element_text](#read_element_text), [read_table](#read_table), [find_ui_elements](#find_ui_elements)' `withinRef` and [capture_window](#capture_window)'s element crop take it; capture_with_elements draws it in each mark's tag, without the window part the marks share, its `markPrefix`). The rules:
- The same element keeps its ref in every read of the server session, whichever tool read it: a ref is tied to the element's UI Automation runtime id and its window, and checked against its control type, automation id and class. A window's refs are `ElementStale` ("its window closed") once it closes, also when Windows has given its handle to a new window: one of another process, class or thread. A list, tree or grid item without an automation id is also checked against its name, because a scrolling list reuses an item's element for another row: the row it shows now gets a new ref. An element inside such an item (a row's Delete button or check box) keeps its own runtime id when its row is reused, so its ref is also checked against its row (the nearest ListItem, TreeItem or DataItem above it, at most 8 levels up, as the read that gave the ref saw it): once the row shows another item, the ref is `ElementStale` ("its row now shows another item"), and the next read gives the element a new ref. Every read that gives refs records the row: the tree walks (get_ui_elements, capture_with_elements, get_desktop_state's elements) as they pass it, and find_ui_elements, get_focused_element, get_element_at_point and get_active_popups by reading the element's ancestors. An element whose ancestors cannot be read still gets its ref, which is then not checked against a row.
- A ref never silently names a different element. When its element is gone, the server looks for the same runtime id in the window. A ref from find_ui_elements whose criteria fit only that element in the whole window (no `withinRef`, and no look-alike, visible or not) is also followed to the element re-created with the same automation id (or the same name when it has none), type and class, when exactly one fits: the ref is *moved*. That element may be the same control rebuilt, or the same-labelled control of the next page or dialog, so every tool given a moved ref says so with `refMoved: true` and a `warning`, until a read that finds or lists elements (find_ui_elements, get_ui_elements, get_desktop_state, capture_with_elements, get_focused_element, get_element_at_point) returns that element again, with the same ref. A read through the ref does not clear it: read_element_text, read_table, wait_for_element, find_ui_elements' `withinRef` and capture_window's crop read the re-created element, wait_for_element's `gone` counts the element the ref was given for as gone, and [element_action](#element_action) (and its `menu_path` below such a ref) does nothing and fails with `ElementStale` and `refMoved: true`: find the element again with find_ui_elements, check that it is the one you mean, then act. A ref from a tree walk, the focused element, the element at a point or a popup list, or one whose criteria fit look-alikes (every row's Delete button), is never moved to a look-alike. A list, tree or grid item found by its name (no automation id) counts as alone only when its list, asked through the ItemContainer pattern, has no other item of that name, realized or not (rows scrolled out of a virtualizing list are not in the tree); an item of a virtualizing list that cannot be asked never does. A control inside a list row is moved only to the element re-created in the same row (an item with the row's name and automation id), never to the same control in another row (the details of whichever row is selected next). Otherwise a call that takes the ref fails with `ElementStale` (gone, its window closed, or the ref expired) or `AmbiguousElement` (several elements now fit), and you find the element again with [find_ui_elements](#find_ui_elements). A check that cannot tell does not drop the ref: when its window does not respond (`NotResponding`), is still open but UI Automation cannot read it (`WindowNotFound`), or the search for its element does not finish in time (`OperationTimedOut`), the ref is kept: try again.
- Refs are per server session and opaque: after a restart the server numbers windows from a new random start (refs carry a seven-digit window number), so an old ref is `ElementStale` ("not issued by this server session") unless the new session happens to number the same window, which is about 1 in 80,000 for a session that has numbered 100 windows. Do not keep refs across a restart. The server keeps the 10,000 most recently used refs, twice the most one read returns. An element without a runtime id (rare) has no `ref`.

**Engine.** The server reads UI Automation through the COM client (UI Automation 3) by default. Each of its calls gives up on an application that does not connect within 1 s or answer within 5 s, so a hung application costs a call seconds instead of blocking it until the timeout; it names the control types Windows 8 added (AppBar, SemanticZoom) from their ids, in every display language; and it reads an element's properties, or a level of the tree of up to 200 elements, in one cross-process call. The user can switch to the managed client of earlier versions with `WAM_UIA_ENGINE=uia2`, as a fallback for an application that reads wrongly; the tools return the same fields with either, and [get_server_info](#get_server_info) reports the engine in force (`uiAutomation`).

**Web content (Chromium, Electron, WebView2).** Chromium builds the accessibility tree of a page only after a UI Automation client asks for it, and then in the background, so the first read of a Chrome or Edge window, an Electron app (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Teams classic), a CEF app or a WebView2 pane (the new Outlook) used to see an empty page. Before get_desktop_state, get_ui_elements, capture_with_elements, find_ui_elements, get_focused_element, get_element_at_point, read_element_text, read_table, wait_for_element (with criteria, once per wait) and get_browser_content (through UI Automation) read a window with a visible page in it (a `Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND` window, its own or inside it), the server asks for the page's document and waits up to 1.5 s (at most a third of `timeoutMs`), checking every 200-500 ms until the document has elements and their number stopped changing; element_action's criteria search does too. The result then carries `accessibilityWarmup` (get_desktop_state in `elements`; element_action does not report it):

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `status` | `Ready`: the page has elements. `Partial`: it has some, but more were still being added when the wait ended; read again for the full tree. `NotReady`: no element came within the wait, so what was read shows the app's frame, not its page: an element missing from it may still be there |
| `host` | `Chromium` (a Chromium browser, an Electron or a CEF app) or `WebView2` (web content inside another app) |
| `waitedMs`, `polls` | How long the call waited (0 when the page was already built) and how often it checked |
| `documentChildCount` | The elements directly in the page's document at the last check; absent when no document was found |
| `warning` | What to do, when `status` is not `Ready`: read again in a moment; for a Chromium or Electron app that stays empty, relaunch it with launch_application `forceAccessibility: true` |

A page that was warmed up is remembered while it is shown, so later reads do not wait and carry no `accessibilityWarmup`. A page shown since (a tab you switched to, or back to) is checked on the next read and waited for while its elements arrive, because Chromium builds a hidden page's tree only once it is shown; finding the shown pages reads only the window's child windows, not UI Automation. A page that stayed empty is waited for again, at most three times, and after that only checked. Only the window being read is asked: nothing global is changed, and no other application is touched. A window without a page (any native app, or a menu of the browser frame) is read as before.

A WebView2 hosted as a visual (roadmap M3.F23: the WinUI 3 WebView2 control, which draws the page into the app's own window) has no `Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND`. For a window without one whose process started an `msedgewebview2.exe`, the server looks a few levels below the window's element (at most 6 levels of panes and groups, and 16 of them listed) for the first element whose `frameworkId` is `Chrome`: a document, or the root of Chromium's own views (roadmap M3.F43), below which it looks for the page's document through Chromium's views (at most 12 levels, and 24 of them listed: in a WinUI 3 window of WebView2 runtime 155 the document is 8 levels below that root, at level 11 of the window). When it finds either, it waits for the document in the same way (a root whose document is not there yet is waited for until it is) and reports `accessibilityWarmup` with `host: "WebView2"`; when it finds neither the window is read as before. The window is then remembered as a page is. A window of any other process costs only one look at the process list, with no UI Automation call. A page further down the window's tree is not found, and is read without the wait.

**WebView2's page below its render widget** (roadmap M3.F33, M3.F35). In WebView2 runtime 155 the render widget's element is the Win32 pane "Chrome Legacy Window", whose children are the page's own elements with no Document element above them; the warm-up takes that pane as the page. Seen from the app's window, the page lies below Chromium's own views (BrowserRootView, NonClientView, BrowserView and more), about 13 levels down, deeper than get_ui_elements' `maxDepth` (10) reaches. So the walk of a window (get_ui_elements, capture_with_elements and get_desktop_state's `elements`) lists the page of each shown render widget inside the window (at most 4) under the element of the render widget's parent window (the `Chrome_WidgetWin_1` pane of the WebView2), as its first child: that "Chrome Legacy Window" pane (or the page's Document, where the render widget has one) with the page's elements inside it, a few levels below the window (about level 4 in a WPF app). The page is walked like any other part of the window: its elements count toward `maxDepth` and `maxElements` at those levels, get refs of the window and marks in capture_with_elements. Chromium's own views are still listed after it, as deep as `maxDepth` reaches, and a page met again among them is not listed twice. A Chromium browser's page is listed the same way, first among its window's elements, since its render widget is a child of the browser window. A window without a render widget is walked as before, at no extra cost.

**WebView2 hosted as a visual** (roadmap M3.F43). The WinUI 3 WebView2 control has no render widget: the window's tree holds Chromium's views (their root is a pane whose `frameworkId` is `Chrome`, named after the page and a localized "Web content") with the page's document 8 levels below that root, at level 11 of the window, beyond `maxDepth`. The window also lists that part of its tree twice: below its content bridge, and again below the XAML island's WebView2 pane, which lists the XAML island itself once more. So the walk of such a window lists the page's document in place of the root's children, which are Chromium's own views and nothing of the page: the document is a level below the root (level 4 of a WinUI 3 window), its elements below it, with the window's refs, counted toward `maxDepth` and `maxElements` like any element. The second copy is left out (see [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements)). The page is the one the warm-up found; a later read, which does not wait, finds it again with the same bounded search (a few listings, only for a window remembered with such a page). Before the page's tree is built, the root's children are walked as before. Searches (find_ui_elements, element_action's criteria) still see Chromium's views, and count each element of the page once.

**Target policy.** A window of an app the user's [target policy](#target-policy) denies (password managers and credential prompts by default) is not read, whether it is named or not: these tools fail with `TargetDeniedByPolicy` before they warm it up or make any UI Automation call to it, as the captures do (get_desktop_state lists the parts it left out in `errors`). While the policy denies anything, a window whose process name cannot be read counts as denied, since it cannot be checked. get_focused_element and get_element_at_point also check the element's own process, so an element that a denied app (or a process that cannot be named) provides is not returned, even inside an allowed window. A popup is never a window the call named: the popups of a denied app, and those of the agent's own host, are left out of the popup lists and searches and counted (`windowsExcluded`, `popupsExcluded`). Ask the user to do the step.

**UI frameworks.** Elements say which UI framework provides them (`frameworkId`: `Win32`, `WPF`, `XAML`, `WinForm`, `DirectUI`, `Chrome` for web content, ...). get_focused_element, get_element_at_point and its `ancestors` name it on every element (find_ui_elements with `detail: "full"`); get_ui_elements names the window's at the top (`frameworkId`) and an element's only where it differs from the element it is inside, so a web page in a native frame shows where it starts (`Document 'Inbox' fw=Chrome` in the text format) without repeating it on every element.

### get_desktop_state

One compact observation of the desktop, and the recommended first call: what the agent needs to get oriented, with refs it can act on, in one call instead of get_foreground_window, find_windows, get_focused_element, get_active_popups and get_ui_elements one after another. Call it again after acting (or pass `observe` to [element_action](#element_action), the click and keyboard tools or [respond_to_dialog](#respond_to_dialog)). It only reads: it sends no input, activates no window and runs without the input gate, so it also works while the user has paused input.

<!-- tools:begin params:get_desktop_state -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| handle | integer | No | - | Window handle (as integer) to read the elements, popups and capture of. Pass handle or window, or neither for the window in front. |
| window | object | No | - | Alternative to handle: a window selector with find_windows' filters (processName is the whole name; plus foreground, index), resolved to exactly one window or refused (AmbiguousWindow lists candidates). |
| include | string (one of: `"windows"`, `"focus"`, `"elements"`, `"popups"`, `"screenshot"`)[] | No | - | Every section to read besides the window in front, the cursor, the keys and the pause (always read): 'windows', 'focus', 'elements', 'popups' (default: all four) and 'screenshot' (off by default; needs capture_window to be served). The list replaces the default: for everything and a capture, pass all five. |
| maxElements | integer | No | 80 | The most element lines, the popups' and the window's together (default: 80, min: 1, max: 500). The walk reads breadth first, so the levels nearest the window are kept; elements.truncated says when there are more (read them with get_ui_elements or find_ui_elements). |
| interactableOnly | boolean | No | true | Only elements that are enabled and keyboard-focusable or have an action pattern (default: true). Pass false to also list labels, texts and containers. |
| scope | string (one of: `"window"`, `"windowAndPopups"`) | No | - | Whose elements: 'window' (the window alone) or 'windowAndPopups' (its open menus, dropdowns, flyouts and dialogs first, within half of maxElements, each under a '# popup' line, then the window under a '# window' line). Default: windowAndPopups when the window, a window it owns or another window of its process is in front, else window, as find_ui_elements. |
| maxWindows | integer | No | 20 | The most window rows (default: 20, min: 1, max: 100); windowCount says how many there are. |
| screenshotMaxLongEdge | integer | No | 1280 | The screenshot's long edge in pixels (default: 1280, min: 256, max: 1568). |
| timeoutMs | integer | No | 5000 | The one deadline of the whole call in milliseconds (default: 5000, min: 1000, max: 30000). |
| screenshotMarks | boolean | No | false | Mark the window's element lines on the screenshot (Set-of-Marks): a box per element, tagged with the ref that starts its line less the window part the refs share, `screenshot.markPrefix` (not the popups' lines). The capture then waits for the walk. Needs 'screenshot' and 'elements' in include. Default: false. |
<!-- tools:end params:get_desktop_state -->

**What it reads.** Always, because they cost nothing: the window in front (`foreground`), the mouse pointer (`cursor`), and `input`: whether the user paused the server's input with the pause hotkey (`paused`, `pausedBy`: input tools then return `PausedByUser`), the modifier keys Windows reports down (`modifiersDown`, as [get_control_status](#get_control_status) reads them: input tools return `ModifiersHeld` while one is) and whether Caps Lock is on (`capsLock`). Then the sections `include` lists. `include` is the complete list, not an addition: the default is the first four, and `["screenshot"]` alone reads only the capture, so for everything plus a capture pass all five:

| Section | Field | What it is |
|---------|-------|------------|
| `windows` | `windows`, `windowCount` | The user-facing windows front first, as [find_windows](#find_windows) lists them (no cloaked, tool, untitled or shell windows), at most `maxWindows`, each a compact row: `handle`, `title`, `process`, `state` (`normal`, `minimized`, `maximized`), `monitor` (its index) and `isAgentHost: true` for your own terminal or editor. `windowCount` is how many there are. Windows of apps the target policy denies are listed like any other, as find_windows lists them, but no tool acts on them |
| `focus` | `focus` | The element with keyboard focus: `ref`, `controlType`, `name`, `automationId`, `bounds`, `windowHandle`, `processName`, `isPassword: true` for a password field. Its value is never returned here ([get_focused_element](#get_focused_element) reads it, never for a password field). Left out, with a `focus` error, when the focus is in a window that is not read: your own host window unless it is the one named (`TargetIsAgentHost`), or an app the policy denies, named or not, or a window or element whose process cannot be named while the policy denies anything (`TargetDeniedByPolicy`). The window in front is checked before the focus is read, so neither is read at all |
| `popups` | `popups`, `popupsExcluded` | The target window's open menus, dropdowns, flyouts and dialogs, front first, as [get_active_popups](#get_active_popups) returns them (`ref`, `handle`, `kind`, `title`, `isBlocking`, ...). A popup of the agent's own host or of an app the policy denies is left out of `popups` and of the element walk, and counted in `popupsExcluded` |
| `elements` | `elements` | The target window's elements as [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements)' text format, one line per element with its ref first (`text`), with `count`, `truncated`, `truncationReason`, `scope`, `accessibilityWarmup` and `warnings` (see below) |
| `screenshot` | `screenshot` and an image | A capture of the target window as [capture_window](#capture_window) makes it (the visible frame, JPEG or PNG, `screenshotMaxLongEdge` on the long edge), as image content before the JSON; `screenshot` has its metadata: `captureId` (for the mouse tools' image space), `imageToScreen`, `width`, `height`, `warnings`. Off by default |

**The target window.** The elements, popups and screenshot are of the window named by `handle` or `window`, or else the window in front (also for `{"foreground": true}` alone, which names no window). The window in front is not read when it is your own host window (your terminal, editor or chat app: it holds the conversation, not the app you mean; error `TargetIsAgentHost`) or an app the user's [target policy](#target-policy) denies (`TargetDeniedByPolicy`), or when no window is in front (`NoForegroundWindow`); the rest is still returned, and the `windows` rows give you a handle to name. Its keyboard focus is not read either (see `focus`). A named window is read as get_ui_elements reads it, unless the policy denies it: then its elements, popups and capture are left out with a `target` error (`TargetDeniedByPolicy`). A window, named or in front, whose process cannot be named counts as denied while the policy denies anything, as get_ui_elements refuses it. The screenshot follows capture_window: never of a window the policy denies (`TargetDeniedByPolicy`, named or not), and refused before anything is read (`InvalidArguments`) when capture_window is not served (the `capture` toolset turned off, the tool excluded, or read-only mode). A minimized window is not captured (`WindowMinimized` in `errors`), and its elements are offscreen.

**Elements.** The walk is get_ui_elements' (the hung-window check, `NotResponding`; the web-content warm-up; every element gets its ref), with `interactableOnly` (default true: enabled elements that are keyboard-focusable or have an action pattern), on-screen elements only, up to 10 levels deep and at most `maxElements` lines (default 80), breadth first. `scope` is find_ui_elements' [scope](#find_ui_elements) and has the same default: while the window, a window it owns or another window of its process is in front, its open popups (not tooltips) are walked first, front first, within half of `maxElements`, and then the window with what is left; each window's lines then follow a header line that starts with `#`:

```
# popup 2493112 Menu
w4120036e2 MenuItem 'Undo' @616,248 260x28
w4120036e3 MenuItem 'Delete' @616,276 260x28
# window 1706796 'notes.txt - Notepad'
w4120035e17 Button 'Save' @812,44 80x24
w4120035e18 Edit 'Search' @320,96 480x28
```

A popup element's ref belongs to the popup's own window (it is stale once the popup closes). A dialog or popup the window owns, which UI Automation also shows inside the window's tree, is walked only as a popup and never again among the window's lines, as get_ui_elements leaves it out; with `scope: "window"` its elements are not listed, and the `popups` section still lists it. `scope: "window"` walks the window alone; `"desktop"` is refused (`InvalidArguments`: use [find_ui_elements](#find_ui_elements)). `truncated: true` with `truncationReason` `MaxElements` means there are more: find the control with find_ui_elements or read the window with get_ui_elements. `warnings` carries the window walk's [warnings](#get_ui_elements) (`WindowMinimized`, `TargetElevated`), which say why its lines may be few or none; left out when there are none.

**Screenshot marks.** `screenshotMarks: true` (with `screenshot` and `elements` in `include`, else `InvalidArguments` before anything is read) draws the window's element lines on the screenshot as [capture_with_elements](#capture_with_elements) draws its Set-of-Marks marks: a box per element and a filled tag with the ref that starts its line, so a mark picked in the image is the element line of the same ref, to act on with [element_action](#element_action). As there, the tags leave out the window part every ref shares and `screenshot.markPrefix` gives it (tag `e17` with `markPrefix` `w4120035` is the line `w4120035e17`), and the tags are placed as capture_with_elements places them. The marks come from the same walk as the `elements` lines (no second read, no other refs), so the capture is made once the walk has returned rather than beside it, under the same deadline. The popups' lines get no marks, since the window's capture does not show the popups, nor does an element outside the image or smaller than 2 pixels. A walk that fails or is not read in time leaves a capture without marks (the `elements` error says why). When the window moved or resized while its elements were read, the marks would sit beside their controls, so none are drawn: the screenshot has a `WindowMoved` warning and no `captureId` (capture_with_elements draws them and warns). Off by default: an ordinary screenshot is unchanged.

**One deadline.** The parts run side by side, and `timeoutMs` (default 5000) covers the whole call. A part that has not answered by then, or that fails, is left out and listed in `errors` as `{section, errorCode, error}` with the code its own tool would return (`OperationTimedOut`, `NotResponding`, `TargetIsAgentHost`, `WindowMinimized`, ...); `section` is `windows`, `focus`, `popups`, `elements`, `screenshot`, or `target` when the window in front (or the window named) was not read. The UI Automation parts are asked to stop a little before the deadline (a fifth of `timeoutMs`, at most 1 s), so the walk returns what it read so far (`truncationReason: Timeout`), and a part still stuck in a UI Automation call is given up before the deadline with what it read; the call itself returns by `timeoutMs`. `success` is false only when the window named by `handle` is no window (`InvalidHandle`); a selector that names no single window fails as in every tool (`WindowNotFound`, `AmbiguousWindow`).

Like every tool result, the JSON writes apostrophes and non-ASCII text as they are rather than as `\u0027`-style escapes, which keeps the element lines short (a double quote is still written `\"`); it is ordinary JSON.

**Example:**
> "What is on the screen?"

```json
{ "name": "get_desktop_state", "arguments": {} }
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "windowHandle": 1706796,
  "windowTitle": "notes.txt - Notepad",
  "foreground": { "handle": 1706796, "title": "notes.txt - Notepad", "processName": "Notepad", "processId": 10244 },
  "focus": { "ref": "w4120035e18", "controlType": "Document", "name": "Text editor", "bounds": { "x": 8, "y": 120, "width": 1264, "height": 700 }, "windowHandle": 1706796, "processName": "Notepad" },
  "cursor": { "x": 640, "y": 480 },
  "input": { "paused": false, "capsLock": false },
  "windows": [
    { "handle": 1706796, "title": "notes.txt - Notepad", "process": "Notepad", "state": "normal", "monitor": 0 },
    { "handle": 3147228, "title": "pwsh in WindowsAppManagerMcp", "process": "WindowsTerminal", "state": "maximized", "monitor": 0, "isAgentHost": true }
  ],
  "windowCount": 2,
  "popups": [],
  "elements": {
    "text": "w4120035e2 MenuItem 'File' @12,40 40x24\nw4120035e3 MenuItem 'Edit' @52,40 40x24\nw4120035e17 Button 'Settings' @1236,40 32x24\nw4120035e18 Document 'Text editor' @8,120 1264x700",
    "count": 4,
    "truncated": false,
    "scope": "windowAndPopups"
  },
  "elapsedMilliseconds": 312.4
}
```

### get_ui_elements

Get the UI element tree with bounding boxes for a window. Provides a lightweight alternative to screenshots when only element coordinates are needed for programmatic interaction planning. By default (since 3.0.0, owner decision D3) the result is `text`, one compact line per element; `format: "tree"` or `"flat"` returns the elements as JSON (see [Formats](#formats)).

<!-- tools:begin params:get_ui_elements -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| handle | integer | No | - | Window handle from find_windows |
| window | object | No | - | Alternative to handle: the window as a selector, resolved to exactly one window or refused (WindowNotFound; AmbiguousWindow with candidates).
