### type_text

Type text by simulating keyboard input, using Unicode characters, so any language works; or paste it through the clipboard (`method`, see [Typing or pasting](#typing-or-pasting)). By default (`auto`) text of up to 200 characters is typed and longer text is pasted when the clipboard can be lent. Pass `windowHandle`: the server brings that window to the front first, and checks the foreground window again every 64 characters, and right before a paste ([Input guard](#input-guard)). Without `windowHandle` the text goes to whatever window is in the foreground; confirm it with `get_foreground_window` first. Typed text with a line break or a tab needs `controlChars` (see [Line breaks and tabs](#line-breaks-and-tabs)). At most 5,000 characters are typed and 1,000,000 pasted (`TextTooLong`). The result reports the text's `length`, never the text.

<!-- tools:begin params:type_text -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| text | string | Yes | - | The text to type |
| delayMs | integer | No | 0 | Delay between keystrokes in milliseconds (0-100). Use for visible typing effect. |
| controlChars | string (one of: `"unicode"`, `"keys"`, `"shiftEnter"`) | No | none | What line breaks and tabs do when typed; required when typed text has any (`InvalidArguments` otherwise, nothing typed). A paste pastes them as they are. See [Line breaks and tabs](#line-breaks-and-tabs) |
| method | string (one of: `"auto"`, `"unicode"`, `"keys"`, `"paste"`) | No | "auto" | `unicode`: type Unicode characters. `keys`: type with the keys of the window's keyboard layout, for remote desktops and virtual machines that drop Unicode keystrokes. `paste`: lend the clipboard, press Ctrl+V and put the clipboard's text back. `auto`: paste text over 200 characters when it can, else type it as `unicode`. See [Typing or pasting](#typing-or-pasting) |
| windowHandle | integer | No | none | The window the keys are for. The server brings it to the front first and sends only while it, or a dialog it owns, is in front (see [Input guard](#input-guard)) |
| window | object | No | - | Alternative to windowHandle: the window as a selector, resolved to exactly one window or refused (WindowNotFound; AmbiguousWindow with candidates), then used as windowHandle. Filters as in find_windows (processName is the whole name); index picks a match in z-order; foreground is the window in front, and alone counts as no windowHandle; handle plus filters must still match (HandleMismatch). |
| allowHostTarget | boolean | No | false | Allow the agent's own host window, only when it is `windowHandle` (or `window.handle`; refused beside a selector without a handle). Set it only when the user explicitly asked |
| releaseHeldModifiers | boolean | No | false | Send modifier keys that are down (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Windows) up first, instead of refusing with `ModifiersHeld`. Only when nobody is pressing them (a stuck key) or the user asked (see [Input guard](#input-guard)) |
| observe | string (one of: `"none"`, `"state"`, `"screenshot"`) | No | "none" | What to return after the action: 'none' (default), 'state' (get_desktop_state's default observation of the window acted on, or of the window in front once that closed, as observed; needs get_desktop_state to be served) or 'screenshot' (as state, plus a capture of that window as image content; needs capture_window too). |
<!-- tools:end params:type_text -->

**Example:**
> "Type 'Hello World' into Notepad"

```json
{
  "name": "type_text",
  "arguments": {
    "text": "Hello World",
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

**Example with delay:**
> "Type text slowly with 50ms between each keystroke"

```json
{
  "name": "type_text",
  "arguments": {
    "text": "Typing slowly...",
    "delayMs": 50,
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "length": 11,
  "charactersTyped": 11,
  "errorCode": "None",
  "method": "unicode",
  "receivingWindow": { "handle": 12345, "title": "Untitled - Notepad", "processName": "Notepad", "processId": 4120 },
  "foregroundAfter": { "handle": 12345, "title": "*Untitled - Notepad", "processName": "Notepad", "processId": 4120 }
}
```

**Error Response:** no `windowHandle`, and the agent's own terminal is in front, so nothing was typed.
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "length": 11,
  "charactersTyped": 0,
  "error": "The input would reach 'pwsh' (WindowsTerminal, handle 34567), the agent's own host: the terminal, editor or chat app this server was started from, or a window it owns. Nothing was typed. Pass windowHandle with the window you mean; ...",
  "errorCode": "TargetIsAgentHost",
  "method": "unicode",
  "receivingWindow": { "handle": 34567, "title": "pwsh", "processName": "WindowsTerminal", "processId": 7788 },
  "foregroundAfter": { "handle": 34567, "title": "pwsh", "processName": "WindowsTerminal", "processId": 7788 }
}
```

#### Line breaks and tabs

A Windows line break (`\r\n`) and a lone `\r` count as one `\n`, and `length` and `charactersTyped` count the text that way. Text that is typed and contains a `\n` or a tab needs `controlChars`; without it the call is refused with `InvalidArguments` and nothing is typed (roadmap M4.1). A paste needs none: it pastes line breaks (as `\r\n`) and tabs as they are, so `auto` pastes long text with line breaks without `controlChars`, but types it (and then needs `controlChars`) when it cannot paste. There is no default because each choice does something different in a different app: Enter sends a chat message or submits a form, and Tab moves to the next field or Excel cell.

| controlChars | A line break (`\n`) | A tab |
|--------------|----------------------|-------|
| `unicode` | The character U+000A, typed like any other character: no Enter key is pressed. Most editors insert a line break; a dialog's default button, a form and a chat box's send do not react to it, and some single-line fields ignore it | The character U+0009: no Tab key, so the focus does not move; editors insert a tab |
| `keys` | The Enter key, as a person typing presses it: it can send a chat message, submit a form, or move down a column in Excel | The Tab key: it moves to the next field or cell |
| `shiftEnter` | Shift+Enter: a new line without sending in chat apps (Teams, Slack, Discord) and in browser text areas. Excel moves up a cell on it, so do not use it there | The character U+0009, as with `unicode` |

**Example with line breaks:**
> "Write a two-line message in the chat box without sending it"

```json
{
  "name": "type_text",
  "arguments": {
    "text": "Hi team,\nthe build is green.",
    "controlChars": "shiftEnter",
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

When another window comes to the front while typing, the call stops with `TargetLostFocus`; when a modal dialog of the target opens (such as a "Save changes?" prompt), it stops with `BlockedByModal` and the dialog in `blockingWindow`. `charactersTyped` says how many characters were typed (into the window that was in front) before it stopped. The user's [pause hotkey](#pause-hotkey) stops typing between batches (`PausedByUser`), and so does a modifier key going down (`ModifiersHeld`); cancelling the request stops it too. With [takeover detection](#takeover-detection) set to `stop`, the user's keyboard or mouse input stops typing between batches (`UserInterrupted`, with `charactersTyped`); with `warn` the typing goes on and the result has a `warning`. A paste is one batch and is not watched. An empty `text` returns `EmptyText`, and typed text with a line break or tab but no `controlChars` returns `InvalidArguments`.

#### Typing or pasting

`method` says how the text goes in (roadmap M4.4). The result's `method` says which one was used (`unicode`, `keys` or `paste`), `length` how many characters the text has and `charactersTyped` how many went in: characters are code points, so an emoji is one, and a Windows line break is one. The text itself is never echoed, and the [audit log](#audit-log) keeps only these numbers and the method.

| method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `auto` (default) | Text of up to 200 characters is typed as `unicode`. Longer text is pasted, unless `delayMs` is set, `controlChars` is `keys` or `shiftEnter` and the text has a line break or tab (a paste would not press Enter or Tab), the window in front is a terminal, or the text has a line break and the window is VS Code or an editor built on it (its focus may be in its terminal panel, where a pasted line break runs a command). When the paste cannot be made (the clipboard cannot be lent, or changed right before Ctrl+V), the text is typed instead, and `warning` says why. Typing has its limits then too: more than 5,000 characters is `TextTooLong`, and a line break or tab without `controlChars` is `InvalidArguments` |
| `unicode` | Every character as a Unicode keystroke (`KEYEVENTF_UNICODE`): any language, whatever the keyboard layout. At most 5,000 characters |
| `keys` | Every character with the key of the window's keyboard layout, with the Shift or AltGr it needs and the key's scan code, as [send_keys](#send_keys) types characters (VkKeyScanEx, allowing for Caps Lock). For remote desktop and virtual machine windows, which drop Unicode keystrokes. A character the layout has no key for (an accent on a layout without it, an emoji, a character only a dead key types) is sent as Unicode, like `unicode` would: check the window afterwards. At most 5,000 characters |
| `paste` | Lends the clipboard: puts the text there, presses Ctrl+V and puts the clipboard's earlier text back. Fast, and free of autocomplete, auto-indent and auto-closing brackets. At most 1,000,000 characters. Refused with `delayMs` (`InvalidArguments`) |

Typed text goes out in batches of 64 characters (one character per batch with `delayMs`), each checked by the [input guard](#input-guard) right before it and stopped by the user's pause or a cancelled request; `charactersTyped` says how far it got. A runaway call cannot type for minutes: more than 5,000 characters are refused before anything is checked (`TextTooLong`); paste them.

**The paste, step by step.** The guard checks the window as for typing. Then:

1. **Never into a terminal.** A paste is refused (`PasteNotAllowed`; `auto` types instead) when the window in front is a terminal: the console, Windows Terminal, PuTTY, KiTTY, mintty, ConEmu, WezTerm, Alacritty, Hyper or Tabby. Ctrl+V does not paste in every terminal (PuTTY sends it on as a control character), and a pasted line break runs the line as a command, which is what `controlChars` exists to make a deliberate choice. Type into a terminal, with `controlChars: "keys"` only when each line is meant to run.
2. **The clipboard is lent only when it can be put back exactly.** The server reads the clipboard: it must be empty, or hold plain text only, at most 4,000,000 characters, not marked private. Formatted text (a copy from a browser, Word or an editor that adds HTML or rich text), an image, copied files or an application's own data could not be put back, and content a password manager marked private is never read (the formats OLE adds to a copy, and the empty `EnterpriseDataProtectionId` label Windows 11 puts on every copy, do not count; a label that names an enterprise identity does, so protected content is never stripped of it); the clipboard is then left alone, and the call fails with `ClipboardUnavailable` (`auto` types instead). The saved text stays in the server's memory for the call only, and is never returned or logged.
3. **The text goes on the clipboard** as [set_clipboard](#set_clipboard) puts it there: kept out of Win+V clipboard history and cloud clipboard sync, with a Windows line break (`\r\n`) for each line break, and only if nobody changed the clipboard since it was read (otherwise `ClipboardUnavailable`: try again).
4. **Right before Ctrl+V** the guard checks the window again, no modifier key may be down, and the [paste rule](#clipboard) checks the clipboard as for any Ctrl+V: it must still hold the agent's text (another application can replace it any time; then `PasteNotAllowed`, or `auto` types), and copy keys the agent sent moments ago must have copied. The paste never goes around the paste rule: it pastes only the text of the call.
5. **Ctrl+V** goes out as one batch with the scan codes of the window's layout (the key Windows calls V, on every layout).
6. **The clipboard goes back** 500 ms later: the earlier text, or an empty clipboard. It also goes back when the call stopped before Ctrl+V (`TargetLostFocus`, `ModifiersHeld`, `PausedByUser`): the pasted text never stays on the clipboard on purpose. A pause or a cancelled request does not shorten the wait once Ctrl+V went out, since a clipboard put back too early would be pasted instead.

`clipboardRestored` says how it ended: `true` when the clipboard holds what it held before again; `false`, with `warning`, when another application put something on the clipboard during the paste (its content is left alone, and the earlier text is not put back) or when the clipboard could not be opened (the pasted text is then still on it, kept out of history: tell the user that their clipboard was replaced).

The restore is best effort, and lossy:

- An application that reads the clipboard more than 500 ms after Ctrl+V (a busy or hung window) pastes the earlier text instead of the call's. Check the window after a paste.
- The text put back carries the same privacy markers as the pasted text, so it adds no entry to clipboard history; [get_clipboard](#get_clipboard) then refuses it as private, unless it was the agent's own text before, which stays the agent's. Its sequence number is new, so a yes the user gave get_clipboard for that content does not carry over. The next paste lends the text put back again: the server knows the content it restored, by its sequence number, so the markers do not make it refuse the user's text as private.
- An application that ignores the paste (some web forms refuse a paste into a field) leaves the field as it was, and the call still reports success: read the field afterwards when it matters.
- The paste goes to the control that has the keyboard focus, as typing does. Do not paste passwords or other secrets: while the paste runs, any application can read the clipboard, and one that ignores the privacy markers can keep a copy; `auto` never pastes text of 200 characters or less, so it types them. The server cannot tell a password field from another field before it pastes ([element_action](#element_action)'s paste mode can, and refuses one).

**Example of a paste:**
> "Paste this script into the editor"

```json
{
  "name": "type_text",
  "arguments": {
    "text": "def main():\n    print('hello')\n",
    "method": "paste",
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "length": 31,
  "charactersTyped": 31,
  "errorCode": "None",
  "method": "paste",
  "clipboardRestored": true,
  "receivingWindow": { "handle": 12345, "title": "script.py - Notepad", "processName": "Notepad", "processId": 4120 },
  "foregroundAfter": { "handle": 12345, "title": "*script.py - Notepad", "processName": "Notepad", "processId": 4120 }
}
```

---

### send_keys

Send keys and key combinations. Pass `windowHandle`: the server brings that window to the front first and sends the keys only while it, or a dialog it owns, is in front ([Input guard](#input-guard)). Without `windowHandle` the keys go to whatever window is in the foreground; confirm it with `get_foreground_window` first. Chords that close, quit or lock (such as Alt+F4) are refused without `windowHandle` (`DestructiveChordNeedsTarget`). A chord that hands the keyboard to another window (Alt+Tab, Alt+Esc, Ctrl+Esc, `{WIN}` or any Windows-key chord, Alt+Space, or a closing chord) must be the last key of the call (`KeysAfterFocusChange`).

**The keyboard layout** (roadmap M4.1). Every character is typed with the key that types it on the keyboard layout of the target window (of the window in front without `windowHandle`), with the Shift or AltGr it needs and the key's scan code, as a keyboard sends it. So `Hello` keeps its capital, `^-` and `%.` reach the application as Ctrl and Alt chords of the real key (a shortcut does not fire on a Unicode character), `@` is AltGr+2 on a Norwegian keyboard and `1` is Shift+& on a French one, and applications that read keys rather than characters (Office KeyTips, games, remote desktop and virtual machine clients) get them. Caps Lock is allowed for: with it on, `Hello` still comes out as written (Shift is added or dropped wherever the layout lets Caps Lock flip the key; never in a chord), and a `{CAPSLOCK}` in the keys counts for the characters after it. A character the layout has no key for, or only a dead key (an accent key that waits for the next key, such as `~` and `^` on a Norwegian keyboard), is sent as Unicode. In a chord with Ctrl, Alt or Win, a letter or digit the layout has no key for is its Latin A-Z or 0-9 key, so `^c` copies on a Russian or Greek layout too. AltGr is sent as the left Ctrl and the right Alt key, and the chord checks read that pair as a character, not as Ctrl+Alt: `user@example.de` on a German keyboard (where `@` is AltGr+Q) is not Ctrl+Q. An explicit `^` or `%` still counts (`^@` is a chord), and so do the left Ctrl and the right Alt pressed as keys: `{LCTRL down}{RALT down}` (or [press_keys](#press_keys)' `lctrl+ralt`) is Ctrl+Alt, as Windows reads it, so `{LCTRL down}{RALT down}{TAB}` is Ctrl+Alt+Tab for every check (`KeysAfterFocusChange` when keys follow it), and with Shift and Pause it is the default pause chord (`PauseChordNotAllowed`). The pause chord check reads even an AltGr character as Ctrl+Alt, because the hotkey reads the keys, not the character: with a pause chord of Ctrl+Alt+Q, `@` on a German keyboard is refused.

<!-- tools:begin params:send_keys -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| keys | string | Yes | - | Keys to send (see the syntax below) |
| windowHandle | integer | No | none | The window the keys are for. The server brings it to the front first and sends only while it, or a dialog it owns, is in front (see [Input guard](#input-guard)) |
| window | object | No | - | Alternative to windowHandle: the window as a selector, resolved to exactly one window or refused (WindowNotFound; AmbiguousWindow with candidates), then used as windowHandle. Filters as in find_windows (processName is the whole name); index picks a match in z-order; foreground is the window in front, and alone counts as no windowHandle; handle plus filters must still match (HandleMismatch). |
| allowHostTarget | boolean | No | false | Allow the agent's own host window, only when it is `windowHandle` (or `window.handle`; refused beside a selector without a handle). Set it only when the user explicitly asked |
| releaseHeldModifiers | boolean | No | false | Send modifier keys that are down (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Windows) up first, instead of refusing with `ModifiersHeld`. Only when nobody is pressing them (a stuck key) or the user asked (see [Input guard](#input-guard)) |
| observe | string (one of: `"none"`, `"state"`, `"screenshot"`) | No | "none" | What to return after the action: 'none' (default), 'state' (get_desktop_state's default observation of the window acted on, or of the window in front once that closed, as observed; needs get_desktop_state to be served) or 'screenshot' (as state, plus a capture of that window as image content; needs capture_window too). |
| delayMs | integer | No | 0 | Milliseconds to wait between keys, 0-500 (more is clamped to 500), at most 10,000 ms in all (`InvalidArguments`). 0 sends the keys in batches of up to 64; see [Pacing](#pacing-and-progress) |
<!-- tools:end params:send_keys -->

**Syntax:**

| Syntax | Meaning | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| A character | Types itself, with the key of the layout (see above) | `abc`, `Hello, world!` |
| `^` `%` `+` `#` | Ctrl, Alt, Shift and the Windows key: held down for the next key or group | `^c` Ctrl+C, `+{HOME}`, `^+{END}`, `#e` Win+E |
| `(...)` | A group: the modifiers before it stay down for every key in it | `+(abc)` types ABC, `^(ac)` |
| `{NAME}` | A named key (table below); names are case-insensitive, and `VK_` and underscores are optional | `{ENTER}`, `{F5}`, `{numpad7}`, `{VK_OEM_1}` |
| `{NAME n}` | The key pressed n times, 1 to 100 | `{DOWN 3}`, `{BACKSPACE 10}`, `{a 3}` |
| `{NAME down}`, `{NAME up}` | Press and release a key apart, within the call; a key still down at the end of the call is released there | `{SHIFT down}{RIGHT 5}{SHIFT up}` |
| `~` | Enter | `abc~` |
| `{c}` (one character) | The character itself: the way to type the characters the grammar uses | `{+}` `{^}` `{%}` `{#}` `{~}` `{(}` `{)}` `{{}` `{}}`; `100{%}` types 100% |
| A tab, a line break | The Tab and Enter keys (a Windows line break is one Enter) | |

`%` is always Alt and `#` always the Windows key: `100%{ENTER}` is "100" and Alt+Enter, so write `100{%}{ENTER}`. A syntax error is `InvalidKeySpecification` and an unknown name `UnknownKey`, both before anything is checked or sent. Syntax errors: a `{` without its `}`, a modifier with no key after it (`abc^`, `100%`), a `(` without its `)`, a `)` or `}` that closes nothing (write them `{)}` and `{}}`), an empty group, a count outside 1-100, `down` or `up` after a single character or with a modifier before it (hold modifiers with their own `{CTRL down}`), `{NAME up}` without `{NAME down}` before it in the call, and `{NAME down}` twice.

**Key names:**

| Key Name | Aliases | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `{ENTER}` | `{RETURN}`, `~` | Enter key |
| `{TAB}` | - | Tab key |
| `{ESC}` | `{ESCAPE}` | Escape key |
| `{BACKSPACE}` | `{BS}`, `{BKSP}`, `{BACK}` | Backspace |
| `{DELETE}` | `{DEL}` | Delete key |
| `{INSERT}` | `{INS}` | Insert key |
| `{UP}`, `{DOWN}`, `{LEFT}`, `{RIGHT}` | - | Arrow keys |
| `{HOME}`, `{END}` | - | Home and End |
| `{PGUP}` | `{PAGEUP}`, `{PRIOR}` | Page Up |
| `{PGDN}` | `{PAGEDOWN}`, `{NEXT}` | Page Down |
| `{SPACE}` | - | Space bar |
| `{F1}` - `{F24}` | - | Function keys |
| `{CAPSLOCK}` | `{CAPS}`, `{CAPITAL}` | Caps Lock (it toggles the user's Caps Lock) |
| `{NUMLOCK}` | - | Num Lock |
| `{SCROLLLOCK}` | `{SCROLL}` | Scroll Lock |
| `{PRTSC}` | `{PRINTSCREEN}`, `{PRTSCN}`, `{SNAPSHOT}` | Print Screen |
| `{PAUSE}` | `{BREAK}` | Pause/Break |
| `{CLEAR}` | - | Clear (numeric keypad 5 with Num Lock off) |
| `{APPS}` | `{CONTEXTMENU}` | The context-menu key |
| `{WIN}` | `{LWIN}` | Windows key (left); `{RWIN}` the right one |
| `{CTRL}`, `{ALT}`, `{SHIFT}` | `{CONTROL}`, `{MENU}` | A modifier pressed and released on its own; `{LCTRL}`, `{RCTRL}`, `{LALT}`, `{RALT}`, `{LSHIFT}`, `{RSHIFT}` for one side. Hold one with `{CTRL down}` |
| `{NUMPAD0}` - `{NUMPAD9}` | - | Numeric keypad digits |
| `{ADD}`, `{SUBTRACT}`, `{MULTIPLY}`, `{DIVIDE}`, `{DECIMAL}`, `{SEPARATOR}` | - | Numeric keypad operators |
| `{OEM_1}` - `{OEM_8}`, `{OEM_102}`, `{OEM_PLUS}`, `{OEM_COMMA}`, `{OEM_MINUS}`, `{OEM_PERIOD}` | - | Punctuation keys by position: what they type depends on the layout (`{OEM_1}` is `;` on a US keyboard). Prefer the character itself |
| `{VOLUME_MUTE}`, `{VOLUME_DOWN}`, `{VOLUME_UP}` | - | Volume keys (they change the user's volume) |
| `{MEDIA_PLAY_PAUSE}`, `{MEDIA_STOP}`, `{MEDIA_NEXT_TRACK}`, `{MEDIA_PREV_TRACK}` | `{MEDIA_NEXT}`, `{MEDIA_PREV}` | Media keys |
| `{BROWSER_BACK}`, `{BROWSER_FORWARD}`, `{BROWSER_REFRESH}`, `{BROWSER_STOP}`, `{BROWSER_SEARCH}`, `{BROWSER_FAVORITES}`, `{BROWSER_HOME}` | - | Browser keys |
| `{LAUNCH_MAIL}`, `{LAUNCH_MEDIA_SELECT}`, `{LAUNCH_APP1}`, `{LAUNCH_APP2}` | - | Launch keys (they start the user's mail or media app, or the apps the keyboard assigns) |

The Sleep key has no name. Win+L (lock) and Ctrl+Alt+Del cannot be injected: Windows ignores them.

#### Pacing and progress

Each top-level character, chord or group is one key, and so is each press of `{NAME n}`. Without `delayMs`, the keys go in SendInput batches of up to 64 key presses (whole keys: a group with more goes alone), which no other input can come between; a call of up to 64 keys is one batch. With `delayMs` (1-500 ms; more is clamped to 500), the keys go one at a time with that wait between them, for applications that drop keys that come too fast. Before each batch, the window is checked again as before the first (`TargetLostFocus`, `BlockedByModal`), a modifier the user presses meanwhile stops the call (`ModifiersHeld`), the paste rule is applied to the batch (`PasteNotAllowed`), and the user's pause (`PausedByUser`) and cancelling the request stop it too; a modifier the call itself holds with `{NAME down}` stays down between batches. A batch SendInput has inserted cannot be stopped, so a long call stops within 64 keys.

A call presses at most 5,000 keys, as type_text types at most 5,000 characters: every character, named key, press of `{NAME n}` and modifier pressed on its own (`{ALT}`) counts, the modifiers held for a key do not. More is refused with `TextTooLong` before anything is checked or sent; send the keys in parts, or put long text in with [type_text](#type_text). The waits add up to at most 10,000 ms ((keys - 1) × `delayMs`), as for [press_keys](#press_keys), because the input gate is held throughout and every other input and window call waits for it; more is refused with `InvalidArguments`, and nothing is sent. The result's `keysSent` says how many keys were sent completely: all of them on success, how far it got when it stopped. When SendInput inserts only part of the keys (`SendInputFailed`), the keys it had pressed are released again, so nothing stays down, and `keysSent` counts the keys that went in whole. Whatever the call holds down is released when it ends, however it ends.

**Example 1:** Press Enter
> "Press Enter to confirm"

```json
{
  "name": "send_keys",
  "arguments": {
    "keys": "{ENTER}",
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

**Example 2:** Copy (Ctrl+C)
> "Copy selected text"

```json
{
  "name": "send_keys",
  "arguments": {
    "keys": "^c",
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

**Example 3:** Select all and delete (Ctrl+A, Delete)
> "Clear all text in the field"

This deletes everything in the focused control. Pass `windowHandle`, and check with `get_focused_element` that the right field has focus first.

```json
{
  "name": "send_keys",
  "arguments": {
    "keys": "^a{DELETE}",
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

> **Closing a window:** do not send Alt+F4 (`%{F4}`). Without `windowHandle` it is refused with `DestructiveChordNeedsTarget`; with it, it still closes whatever the window does on Alt+F4. Use [close_window](#close_window) with the window's handle instead.

> **Switching windows:** keys after Alt+Tab (`%{TAB}`), Alt+Esc, Ctrl+Esc, `{WIN}`, Alt+Space or a closing chord would go to whatever window comes to the front, so `send_keys` refuses them (`KeysAfterFocusChange`): `"%{TAB}{ENTER}"` is refused, `"%{TAB}"` alone is sent. To work in another window, pass that window's handle as `windowHandle` in the next call instead of switching with keys.

**Example 4:** Select to beginning (Shift+Home)
> "Select text from cursor to beginning of line"

```json
{
  "name": "send_keys",
  "arguments": {
    "keys": "+{HOME}",
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

**Example 5:** Multiple modifiers (Ctrl+Shift+End)
> "Select from cursor to end of document"

```json
{
  "name": "send_keys",
  "arguments": {
    "keys": "^+{END}",
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

**Example 6:** Repeat a key, slowly
> "Move down three rows in a list that drops fast keys, then open the item"

```json
{
  "name": "send_keys",
  "arguments": {
    "keys": "{DOWN 3}{ENTER}",
    "delayMs": 100,
    "windowHandle": 12345
  }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "keys": "^c",
  "errorCode": "None",
  "keysSent": 1,
  "receivingWindow": { "handle": 12345, "title": "Untitled - Notepad", "processName": "Notepad", "processId": 4120 },
  "foregroundAfter": { "handle": 12345, "title": "Untitled - Notepad", "processName": "Notepad", "processId": 4120 }
}
```

**Error Response:**
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "keys": "{UNKNOWNKEY}",
  "error": "Unknown key: UNKNOWNKEY",
  "errorCode": "UnknownKey"
}
```

**Error Response:** a modifier with no key after it.
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "keys": "100%",
  "error": "'%' at position 3 has no key after it to hold down. Write the characters + ^ % # as {+} {^} {%} {#}.",
  "errorCode": "InvalidKeySpecification"
}
```

`UnknownKey`, `InvalidKeySpecification` and `EmptyText` are reported before anything is checked or sent; the guard's codes are listed under [Input guard](#input-guard). For key chords by name (`ctrl+shift+t`, `tab*3`), [press_keys](#press_keys) takes the same keys with the same checks. `#` is the Windows key (roadmap M4.1; it was an ordinary character before): type the character as `{#}`. A Windows-key chord opens a part of Windows (Run, Search, Explorer, the clipboard history), so it must be the last key of the call: `#hashtag` is Win+H followed by more keys and is refused with `KeysAfterFocusChange`, while `{#}hashtag` types it. Keys that press the user's [pause hotkey](#pause-hotkey) (`^%+{PAUSE}` for the default chord, also written with `{BREAK}` or with more modifiers) are refused with `PauseChordNotAllowed` and nothing is sent: they would reach the hotkey like the user's own key press, so the agent could pause or resume itself.

### press_keys

Press keys by name (roadmap M4.3): a chord such as `ctrl+shift+t`, or a sequence such as `tab*3 enter` or `ctrl+a delete`. Structured chords are easier to get right than [send_keys](#send_keys)' `^+t` punctuation, and they go through exactly the same path: the chords become the same input events, mapped with the target window's keyboard layout and sent with scan codes, so the [Input guard](#input-guard) reads them as it reads send_keys' keys.

**The keys.** `keys` is a string or an array of strings:

| `keys` | Presses |
|--------|---------|
| `"ctrl+shift+t"` or `["ctrl", "shift", "t"]` | One chord: Ctrl and Shift go down in that order, then T goes down and up, then Shift and Ctrl come up |
| `"tab*3"` | Tab three times (`*n`: 1 to 100) |
| `"ctrl+a delete"`, `"ctrl+a, delete"` or `["ctrl+a", "delete"]` | Ctrl+A, then Delete: chords separated by spaces or commas, or the items of an array that is not one chord |
| `"alt"` | Alt alone, pressed and released (it shows the menu bar's access keys) |

An array is one chord when every item but the last is a modifier and no item holds `+`, `*`, a comma or a space (`["ctrl", "shift", "t"]`); otherwise each item is a chord (`["tab", "tab"]` presses Tab twice). A chord has modifiers (`ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, `win`, also `windows`, and the left and right forms `lctrl`, `rctrl`, `lshift`, `rshift`, `lalt`, `ralt`, `lwin`, `rwin`) and at most one other key: a [send_keys](#send_keys) key name (`enter`, `tab`, `esc`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `insert`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `home`, `end`, `pgup`, `pgdn`, `f1` to `f24`, `numpad0` to `numpad9`, `apps`, `volume_mute`, ...; case does not matter) or a single character. A letter or digit is its key, A to Z or 0 to 9, with no Shift of its own: `ctrl+t` and `ctrl+T` are the same chord, and `ctrl+1` is the shortcut on any layout, AZERTY included. Any other character is the key the window's keyboard layout types it with, plus the Shift or AltGr it needs (`ctrl+?` is Ctrl+Shift+/ on a US keyboard); a character no key types is sent as Unicode. `+`, `,` and `*` are part of the syntax, so write them `plus`, `comma` and `star`. `repeat` runs the whole sequence again (1 to 100), and one call presses at most 200 chords in all.

**Timing.** Without `holdMs` and `delayBetweenMs` every press goes in one SendInput batch, so no other input comes between them. `delayBetweenMs` (0 to 1000) waits between presses, each its own batch, with the foreground window checked again before each, as send_keys' `delayMs` does. `holdMs` (0 to 5000) keeps each chord's keys down that long before they come up: for an app that reads a long press, or a key repeat. presses × (`holdMs` + `delayBetweenMs`) is at most 10,000 ms; outside any range the call is refused with `InvalidArguments` and nothing is sent.

**Nothing stays held.** A chord's keys come up in the same call that pressed them, and press_keys has no key-down or key-up of its own. When a call stops while a chord is held (the user's [pause hotkey](#pause-hotkey), a cancelled request, a failure), the server releases its keys at once. There are no `key_down` or `mouse_down` tools: a key held across calls could stay down after the agent's turn.

**The same checks as send_keys.** Every chord is read before anything is sent: a chord that closes, quits or locks (`ctrl+w`, `alt+f4`, `ctrl+q`, `win+l`, ...) needs `windowHandle` (`DestructiveChordNeedsTarget`); a chord that hands the keyboard to another window (`alt+tab`, `win`, `win+r`, `alt+space`, a closing chord) must be the last (`KeysAfterFocusChange`); the user's pause hotkey chord is refused (`PauseChordNotAllowed`); and a paste (`ctrl+v`, `shift+insert`) follows the paste rule (`PasteNotAllowed`, see [Clipboard](#clipboard)). Windows never lets injected input press Ctrl+Alt+Del (the secure attention sequence) or lock the session with Win+L, whatever the tool. A key name that is not one is `UnknownKey`, and a chord with two keys (`ctrl+a+b`), an empty name (`ctrl++`) or a bad count (`tab*0`) is `InvalidKeySpecification`; both are reported before anything is checked or sent. The result is send_keys': `keys` echoes the keys (an array joined, `ctrl+shift+t` or `ctrl+a delete`) and `keysSent` counts the presses sent.

<!-- tools:begin params:press_keys -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| keys | string or string[] | Yes | - | A chord (`"ctrl+shift+t"`, or the array `["ctrl", "shift", "t"]`), or a sequence of chords separated by spaces or commas (`"ctrl+a delete"`, or the array `["ctrl+a", "delete"]`), each optionally `*n` (pressed n times, 1-100: `"tab*3"`). Names as above |
| repeat | integer | No | 1 | How often to press the whole sequence, 1 to 100; at most 200 presses in all |
| holdMs | integer | No | 0 | Milliseconds each chord's keys stay down before they come up, 0 to 5000 |
| delayBetweenMs | integer | No | 0 | Milliseconds between presses, 0 to 1000; 0 sends every press in one batch. presses × (`holdMs` + `delayBetweenMs`) is at most 10,000 |
| windowHandle | integer | No | none | The window the keys are for. The server brings it to the front first and sends only while it, or a dialog it owns, is in front (see [Input guard](#input-guard)) |
| window | object | No | - | Alternative to windowHandle: the window as a selector, resolved to exactly one window or refused (WindowNotFound; AmbiguousWindow with candidates), then used as windowHandle. Filters as in find_windows (processName is the whole name); index picks a match in z-order; foreground is the window in front, and alone counts as no windowHandle; handle plus filters must still match (HandleMismatch). |
| allowHostTarget | boolean | No | false | Allow the agent's own host window, only when it is `windowHandle` (or `window.handle`; refused beside a selector without a handle). Set it only when the user explicitly asked |
| releaseHeldModifiers | boolean | No | false | Send modifier keys that are down (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Windows) up first, instead of refusing with `ModifiersHeld`. Only when nobody is pressing them (a stuck key) or the user asked (see [Input guard](#input-guard)) |
| observe | string (one of: `"none"`, `"state"`, `"screenshot"`) | No | "none" | What to return after the action: 'none' (default), 'state' (get_desktop_state's default observation of the window acted on, or of the window in front once that closed, as observed; needs get_desktop_state to be served) or 'screenshot' (as state, plus a capture of that window as image content; needs capture_window too). |
<!-- tools:end params:press_keys -->

**Example:**
> "Reopen the last closed tab in Edge (handle 45678)"

```json
{
  "name": "press_keys",
  "arguments": {
    "keys": ["ctrl", "shift", "t"],
    "windowHandle": 45678
  }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "keys": "ctrl+shift+t",
  "errorCode": "None",
  "keysSent": 1,
  "receivingWindow": { "handle": 45678, "title": "New tab - Microsoft Edge", "processName": "msedge", "processId": 9010 },
  "foregroundAfter": { "handle": 45678, "title": "New tab - Microsoft Edge", "processName": "msedge", "processId": 9010 }
}
```

**Example: move down three rows and open the item**, one key every 50 ms, in File Explorer (handle 23456):

```json
{ "name": "press_keys", "arguments": { "keys": "down*3 enter", "delayBetweenMs": 50, "windowHandle": 23456 } }
```

**Error Response:** a chord with two keys.
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "keys": "ctrl+a+b",
  "error": "'ctrl+a+b' has more than one key besides its modifiers; a chord has one key. To press keys one after another, separate them with spaces ('ctrl+a delete'). Nothing was sent.",
  "errorCode": "InvalidKeySpecification"
}
```

## Input Control

The user's control over the server's input: the [pause hotkey](#pause-hotkey), and tools to read its state ([get_control_status](#get_control_status)), to resume after a pause, only with the user's confirmation ([resume_input](#resume_input)), and to release stuck keys ([release_all_input](#release_all_input)).

### Pause hotkey

The user can stop the agent's input at any moment with a system-wide hotkey, by default **Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Pause**:

- **Press it once to pause.** Every input tool returns `PausedByUser` and sends nothing. So does every tool that changes windows or starts or stops processes: the [Window Control](#window-control) tools ([focus_window](#focus_window) and [close_window](#close_window) among them), the [Batch Operations](#batch-operations), [close_application](#close_application), [apply_layout](#apply_layout), [launch_application](#launch_application), [kill_process](#kill_process), [launch_browser_with_debug](#launch_browser_with_debug), [close_debug_browser](#close_debug_browser), [set_clipboard](#set_clipboard), [element_action](#element_action), [file_dialog](#file_dialog) and a [respond_to_dialog](#respond_to_dialog) that presses a button return an error result (`isError: true`) with `errorCode` `PausedByUser` without running, also when they were already waiting for another call to finish. Tools that only read (window lists, screenshots, UI Automation reads and waits, [get_desktop_state](#get_desktop_state), respond_to_dialog without `button`, browser reading, [get_control_status](#get_control_status)) keep working. A running `type_text` or double click stops between batches and returns `PausedByUser` with what it did so far. A window call that was already running finishes, except an activation ([focus_window](#focus_window), a `focus` placement of [apply_layout](#apply_layout) or of a launch's `placement`, or the input guard bringing a `windowHandle` target to the front), which stops at its next step and reports `PausedByUser`. Keys and mouse buttons the server holds down are released at once; keys the user holds are left alone.
- **Press it again to resume.** The hotkey always toggles, but a press within 2 seconds of the pause is ignored, so pressing it twice to be sure does not resume. The agent can ask to resume with [resume_input](#resume_input), which resumes only when the user confirms.
- **It pauses every server.** Each MCP client session starts its own server, and only one process can register the chord. The pause is shared by all of the user's Windows App Manager servers on the desktop: the chord pauses and resumes every one of them, whichever server registered it, and so does a confirmed [resume_input](#resume_input). A server that finds the chord held by another server reports `hotkey.state` `OtherServer`, and registers the chord itself within 2 seconds after that server stops. A server that starts while input is paused starts paused.
- The agent cannot resume itself: `resume_input` asks the user, and `send_keys` refuses the hotkey's keys (`PauseChordNotAllowed`), which would reach the hotkey like a real key press. While any modifier of the chord is down, no modifier is released for the agent (`releaseHeldModifiers`), not even one outside the chord, since the user may be pressing it.
- Holding the chord down fires it once. On most keyboards Ctrl turns the Pause key into Break; the server registers both, so the chord also works in remote sessions that send Pause.

The chord is set by the user in the server's environment, never by a tool argument:

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `WAM_PAUSE_HOTKEY` | `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Pause` | The pause hotkey: modifiers (`Ctrl`, `Alt`, `Shift`, `Win`) and one key (a letter, a digit, `F1`-`F24`, `Pause` or `Break`, `Esc`, `Space`, `Enter`, `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Insert`, `Delete`, `Home`, `End`, `PgUp`, `PgDn`, the arrows, `ScrollLock`), joined with `+`, in any case, for example `Ctrl+Alt+F12`. It needs a modifier (only `Pause`, `ScrollLock` and `F13`-`F24` may stand alone), and `Shift` alone is not enough for a key that types text. `none` turns the hotkey off. A value that is not a valid chord keeps the default in force, and the reason is shown in [get_control_status](#get_control_status) and logged at start |

For example, in the MCP server configuration: `"env": { "WAM_PAUSE_HOTKEY": "Ctrl+Alt+F12" }`.

If another program already uses the chord, Windows refuses to register it: [get_control_status](#get_control_status) reports `hotkey.state` `Failed` with the reason, and the server logs a warning when it starts. The server tries again every 2 seconds; to use another chord, set `WAM_PAUSE_HOTKEY` and restart the server. If registering fails in another way (Windows refuses the chord for another reason, or the registration throws), the server does not try again, and any key of the chord it had registered is freed, so the hotkey never works while its state says `Failed`. A server that registered the chord marks itself as the chord's holder, so other servers report `OtherServer`; if that mark cannot be made, the hotkey still works and stays `Registered`, and only a server started later reports `Failed` instead of `OtherServer`. Servers configured with different chords each register their own, and every one of those chords pauses all of them. The shared pause is a named event in the user's logon session: a server running as administrator and one that is not may be unable to share it, and then each one keeps its own pause and only its own chord pauses it (`sharedPause: false`, and a warning in its log). A server that cannot read the shared pause once it shares it pauses itself (`pausedBy` `shared_pause_unreadable`; its `PausedByUser` errors say the server paused itself, not that the user pressed the hotkey) and stays paused until the user resumes it: a press of the hotkey then keeps the pause, as the user's own, and the next press resumes.

When the server stops, including when the MCP client closes its standard input, it releases any key or button it still holds. A server process that is killed outright cannot release anything. The hotkey is the way to stop the server; [takeover detection](#takeover-detection), off by default, can also stop its long input operations when the user takes the mouse or keyboard. A hotkey cannot tell an injected key press from the user's, and the shared pause is a named event any program of the user can open: a program the agent started before the pause could press the chord or resume the shared pause. While input is paused the agent cannot start programs (`launch_application` returns `PausedByUser`).

### Takeover detection

Off by default. When the user turns it on, the server watches for the user's own keyboard and mouse input while a long input operation runs, and stops it (or warns about it) instead of typing or dragging on while the user works (roadmap M7.4). It complements the [pause hotkey](#pause-hotkey), which stays the way to stop the server.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `WAM_TAKEOVER_DETECTION` | `off` | `off`: nothing is watched. `warn`: the operation goes on, and its result has a `warning` that the user used the keyboard or mouse meanwhile. `stop` (also `on`, `true`, `1`): the operation stops between two batches or steps with `UserInterrupted`, says how far it got, and releases what it held. Any other value is taken as `stop`, and the reason is shown in [get_control_status](#get_control_status) |

- **What is watched.** [type_text](#type_text)'s typing (not a paste), [drag](#drag) from the press to the drop, and [run_steps](#run_steps) from the moment it holds the input gate (a run stops before its next step, or when a step stops for it; a step that is running is not cut off). Short calls (a click, a key chord) are one batch and are not watched.
- **What counts.** A key, mouse button or wheel going down, or the mouse moving (a burst of at least 4 moves within 300 ms, so a nudge of the desk does not count), when it was not injected. Injected input (SendInput by this server or any other program, the on-screen keyboard among them) never counts. Releasing a key does not count, so letting go of the Enter that sent the prompt does not stop the agent. The pause hotkey's press counts too, but a pause wins: the call returns `PausedByUser`.
- **What is kept.** Only whether the user acted: never which key or button, never where the pointer was. The server installs low-level keyboard and mouse hooks (`WH_KEYBOARD_LL`, `WH_MOUSE_LL`) on a thread of its own only while one of these operations runs, removes them when the last one ends, and passes all input on unchanged. Input in the first moments of an operation, before the hooks are in, can be missed.
- **When it does not work.** If Windows does not install the hooks, a hook fails, or the detection thread stops, [get_control_status](#get_control_status) reports `state` `Unavailable` and why in `error` (until the hooks are next installed). type_text, drag and run_steps then run as with `off`, and the result of each one that detection did not watch for all or part of its time has a `warning` that the user's input was not watched then; a result that reports the user's input all the same (`UserInterrupted`, or the warning of `warn`) does not add it, and an operation that detection watched is not blamed for an earlier failure. Each operation that starts while Windows did not install the hooks tries to install them again. A detection thread that stopped is started again by the next operation, at most three times; after that, detection stays off until the server is restarted.
- **What the agent should do.** After `UserInterrupted`, do not try again at once: the user is using the computer. Ask the user before going on.

### get_control_status

Whether the user has paused the server's input (and how and since when), whether the pause hotkey is registered, which keys and buttons are down, and takeover detection's mode. Reads only.

<!-- tools:begin params:get_control_status -->
**Parameters:** None
<!-- tools:end params:get_control_status -->

**Example:**
> "Is input paused?"

```json
{
  "name": "get_control_status",
  "arguments": {}
}
```

**Response:** paused with the hotkey.
```json
{
  "paused": true,
  "pausedBy": "hotkey",
  "pausedAt": "2026-10-10T12:03:04+00:00",
  "hotkey": { "chord": "Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Pause", "state": "Registered", "source": "default" },
  "sharedPause": true,
  "heldInput": { "serverHeld": [], "modifiersDown": [] },
  "message": "Input is paused by the user (hotkey at 14:03:04). Every input tool and every tool that changes windows or starts or stops processes returns PausedByUser. Stop and ask the user how to continue. Only the user can resume: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Pause again, or by confirming resume_input when you call it at the user's request."
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `paused` | True while the user has paused input |
| `pausedBy`, `pausedAt` | How (`hotkey`; `shared_pause_unreadable` when the pause every server on the desktop shares could not be read, so the server paused itself until the user resumes) and when it was paused; left out while running |
| `resumedBy`, `resumedAt` | How (`hotkey`, `resume_input` after the user confirmed, or `another_server` when another server's hotkey or confirmed `resume_input` resumed the shared pause) and when it was last resumed |
| `hotkey` | `chord`, `state` (`Registered`; `OtherServer` when another Windows App Manager server on the desktop has registered the chord, whose presses pause this server too; `Failed`; `Disabled` when `WAM_PAUSE_HOTKEY` is `none`; `NotStarted`), `source` (`default` or `WAM_PAUSE_HOTKEY`) and `error` (why it is not registered, or why the configured chord was not used) |
| `sharedPause` | `true` when the pause is shared by every Windows App Manager server on the desktop: any server's chord pauses and resumes this one, and so does a confirmed `resume_input` in any of them |
| `heldInput` | `serverHeld`: keys and buttons the server pressed and could not release (normally empty); `modifiersDown`: modifier keys that are down now, the user's or stuck; `lastRelease`: the last release that sent something (`at`, `reason`, `released`, `stillHeld`) |
| `takeover` | [Takeover detection](#takeover-detection): `mode` (`Off`, `Warn` or `Stop`), `state` (`Off`; `Ready`: on, with no operation watched, so no hook is installed; `Watching`: an operation is watched now; `Unavailable`: detection is not working, because Windows did not install the hooks (`error` has its Windows error), a hook failed, or the detection thread stopped, so nothing is detected), `source` (`default` or `WAM_TAKEOVER_DETECTION`) and `error` (why the configured value was not used, or why detection is not working) |
| `message` | What this means for the agent |

---

### resume_input

Ask the user to resume the server's input after they paused it. The server asks the user directly, through the MCP client (elicitation: a question with a "Resume input" checkbox that is off by default), and input resumes only when the user confirms. Call it only when the user has asked you to continue.

<!-- tools:begin params:resume_input -->
**Parameters:** None
<!-- tools:end params:resume_input -->

**Example:**
> "I'm done, you can continue"

```json
{
  "name": "resume_input",
  "arguments": {}
}
```

**Response:** the user confirmed.
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "wasPaused": true,
  "resumedBy": "resume_input",
  "errorCode": "None"
}
```

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|------|---------|------------|
| `ResumeNeedsUser` | The MCP client cannot ask the user (it does not support elicitation), so only the user can resume, with the hotkey | Tell the user and wait |
| `ResumeDeclined` | The user said no, dismissed the question, left the checkbox off, or did not answer within 5 minutes; or the user paused again while the question was open (the answer was for the earlier pause); or another `resume_input` call is already waiting for the user's answer | Input stays paused; ask the user what to do. Do not ask again while a question is open |

When input is not paused, `success` is true and `wasPaused` false, and nobody is asked. When the user presses the hotkey while the question is open, the result reports `resumedBy: "hotkey"`. Only one question is open at a time. With a shared pause (`sharedPause` in [get_control_status](#get_control_status)), resuming resumes every server on the desktop, and the question tells the user so. The confirmation is only as reliable as the client: a client that answered elicitations by itself would defeat it.

---

### release_all_input

Release keys and mouse buttons that are stuck down. Sends the up event of every key and button the server pressed and could not release; normally there are none, because every input call releases its own, also after a failed or interrupted batch, and the server releases them when it stops. With `releaseHeldModifiers: true` it also releases every modifier key (Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Windows) that is down although the server did not press it, for example after an input tool returned `ModifiersHeld` and nobody is pressing the key. Releasing Alt or Windows first sends an unassigned key, so no menu opens. Works while input is paused, except for `releaseHeldModifiers` (`PausedByUser`). While any modifier that is down is one of the pause hotkey's, no modifier the server did not press is released (`ModifiersHeld`), the other keys down included: the user may be pressing the hotkey. The keys and buttons the server pressed are still released.

<!-- tools:begin params:release_all_input -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| releaseHeldModifiers | boolean | No | false | Also release modifier keys that are down although the server did not press them (the user's, or stuck) |
<!-- tools:end params:release_all_input -->

**Example:**
> "Ctrl seems to be stuck"

```json
{
  "name": "release_all_input",
  "arguments": {
    "releaseHeldModifiers": true
  }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "released": ["LeftCtrl"],
  "stillHeld": [],
  "modifiersDown": [],
  "errorCode": "None"
}
```

`stillHeld` lists what could not be released (`SendInputFailed`, for example while a UAC prompt has the input); ask the user to press and release those keys. `modifiersDown` lists the modifier keys still down after the call.

## Step Sequences

Several steps on one window in one call (roadmap M6.2): a form fill, a key sequence, a dialog to wait for and answer. One round trip instead of one per step, and no other call's input or window change lands between two of the steps. [run_steps](#run_steps) is in the `steps` toolset, on by default (`WAM_TOOLSETS=-steps` turns it off). It is not a workflow engine: no loops, no branches, no assertions of its own.

### run_steps

Run 1 to 50 steps, in order, on the run's `window`. A step is `{tool, args, id, optional, return}`: `tool` is one of the tools below and `args` are that tool's own arguments, exactly as a direct call takes them, so each tool's own section documents them. The steps are called through the server's own call pipeline, so each one gets what a direct call gets: its own [audit log](#audit-log) line (request id `<run's id>#<step>`, the first step 1), the refusal of an argument it does not declare, its own error results and its guards ([Input guard](#input-guard), [target policy](#target-policy), the host window). A step tool that the [toolsets](#toolsets), `WAM_EXCLUDE_TOOLS` or `WAM_READ_ONLY` leave out cannot be a step either. run_steps is destructive, audited and not served in read-only mode.

**The step tools.** [focus_window](#focus_window), [find_ui_elements](#find_ui_elements), [element_action](#element_action), [type_text](#type_text), [send_keys](#send_keys), [press_keys](#press_keys), [mouse_click](#mouse_click), [drag](#drag), [mouse_move](#mouse_move), [scroll](#scroll), [wait_for_window](#wait_for_window), [wait_for_element](#wait_for_element), [get_focused_element](#get_focused_element) and [capture_window](#capture_window). Nothing that asks the user, closes a window, ends or starts a process, or writes the clipboard, a file or a layout; no browser tool; not respond_to_dialog and file_dialog (press a dialog's buttons with element_action, and wait for it with wait_for_window); and not run_steps itself. There are no assert steps: [wait_for_window](#wait_for_window) with `condition: "foreground"` and [wait_for_element](#wait_for_element) with `timeoutMs: 0` check a state once, and fail the run when it does not hold (mark the step `optional` when it may not).

**Checked before anything runs.** Every step is checked first, and a wrong one refuses the whole run with `InvalidArguments` ("Nothing was done", naming the step): more than 50 steps or none; a step without `tool` (or with `null`); a step member other than `tool`, `args`, `id`, `optional` and `return` (`arguments` for `args`, for example); an `id` that is not 1-32 letters, digits, `_` or `-`, or that an earlier step has; a tool the server does not serve; an argument its tool does not declare, letter case included (with the name it most likely meant); a `handle`, `windowHandle` or `toWindowHandle` that is no whole number (a JSON number, or a string of its digits); more than 20,000 characters in all the steps' strings together; a reference that is wrong (below); and what a step may not do: `allowHostTarget: true`, type_text's `method` `paste` or `auto` (auto pastes a long text), element_action's `mode: "paste"` and `action: "window_close"`, capture_window's `outputPath`, `saveToFile`, `overwrite` and `output` `file` or `both`, `scope: "desktop"` on element_action, find_ui_elements and wait_for_element (it searches every window), and send_keys' or press_keys' `keys` with a chord that closes, quits or locks: the destructive chords of the [input guard](#input-guard) (Alt+F4, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+F4, Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Win+L by default, and those of `WAM_DESTRUCTIVE_CHORDS`). A step's keyboard tool always gets a window, so its own check, which refuses those chords only without one, would let them through. No argument a step may use writes the clipboard or a file, closes a window or finds one outside the run's window and its dialogs. The keys a step sends act inside the run's window as a direct call's would: `ctrl+s` saves and `ctrl+c` copies, as the app does them. type_text in a step types with `method: "unicode"` unless it says `keys` (also when it says `null`).

**The run's window.** `window` is a selector (or `{"handle": n}`) resolved to exactly one window before the run; `{"foreground": true}` alone is refused, and the agent's own host window is `TargetIsAgentHost`. A step that names no window (none of `handle`, `windowHandle`, `window`, `ref`, `withinRef`, `listRef`) gets the run's window under the name its tool takes: `windowHandle` for the input tools, `handle` for focus_window, find_ui_elements, element_action and capture_window, `window: {"handle": n}` for wait_for_element. An argument that is `null` counts as not given, and an empty selector or `{"foreground": true}` alone names no window, so such a step gets the run's window too, never the one in front. wait_for_window never gets it: its `window` is what it waits for. A step may act only on the run's window, a window it owns (its dialogs, also those of another process) or another window of its process, except for File Explorer's and the packaged apps' frame host's (explorer, ApplicationFrameHost), whose windows are unrelated (the taskbar, other folders, other apps): there only the run's window and the windows it owns count. A step that names any other window, by handle, `toWindowHandle`, selector or element ref, is not run (`InvalidArguments`) and stops the run. A window is read as the step's tool binds it: a handle written as a string of digits (`"1706796"`, also one a reference brings, such as a `captureId`) is that window, and is passed to the tool as the number; a selector's members match in any letter case (`{"Handle": n}`). A step's selector is resolved when the step runs and passed to its tool as `{"handle": n}`, so the tool acts on the window that was checked; a selector that matches no window or several is not run, with its code (`WindowNotFound`, `AmbiguousWindow`). get_focused_element and wait_for_window only read, and may read outside the run's window. Once the run holds the input gate, which it may have waited 30 seconds for, it reads its window again: a window that closed (or whose handle now names another process's window) refuses the run with `InvalidHandle`, and the agent's host with `TargetIsAgentHost`; nothing was done.

**References.** A string argument that is exactly `"$steps.<id>.<path>"` takes a value from the result of the earlier step with that `id`: `"$steps.find.elements[0].ref"`, `"$steps.find.elements[0].clickPoint.x"`, `"$steps.dialog.window.handle"`, `"$steps.shot.captureId"`. The path is property names with optional `[n]` indexes, and it must end with an identifier: `ref`, `handle`, `captureId`, or `clickPoint.x` and `clickPoint.y`. A value keeps its type (a handle stays a number). Text a window shows (a name, a value, a title) is never passed on: untrusted text must not flow into input without the agent reading it. A reference to a step that failed (an optional one) fails its own step.

**One gate, one budget.** The run waits for the input gate (at most 30 seconds, as any input call; `InputBusy`, or `PausedByUser` while input is paused), then holds it for the whole run: its own steps pass it, and every other input or window call waits for the run to end, or gets `InputBusy` after 30 seconds. `maxDurationMs` (default 30000, 1000-60000) bounds how long the run holds it. A wait step's `timeoutMs` is cut to what is left of it (less 250 ms), so with `maxDurationMs` at its default a wait without `timeoutMs` waits at most what is left, not its own default; a step still running when the time runs out is cancelled. `delayBetweenStepsMs` (default 50, at most 2000) waits between two steps.

**When the run stops.** The steps run in order until one fails; the steps after it are `skipped`, and nothing that ran is undone. A step with `optional: true` may fail without stopping the run (a dialog that may not appear). Before each step after the first the run also checks:

| `stoppedBy` | `errorCode` | When |
|-------------|-------------|------|
| `stepFailed` | the failed step's own code | A step that is not optional failed: its tool reported an error, or the run did not call it (a reference to a failed step, a window that is not the run's) |
| `paused` | `PausedByUser` | The user pressed the [pause hotkey](#pause-hotkey) before a step, during the wait between two, or during a step (which then stops as a direct call does). Stop and ask the user; never resume input yourself |
| `timedOut` | `OperationTimedOut` | `maxDurationMs` ran out before a step, or during one (the step is cancelled, or a wait the run cut to the time left ran out) |
| `userInterrupted` | `UserInterrupted` | With [takeover detection](#takeover-detection) set to `stop`: the user used the keyboard or mouse during the run, seen before a step or during the wait between two, or a step stopped for it (or failed while the user was at the controls). Do not try again at once; ask the user. With `warn` the run goes on and the result has a `warning` |
| `foregroundMoved` | `TargetNotForeground` | Once the run's window or one of its windows (above) has been in front, another window is in front before a step: the user (or another program) took the foreground. The run stops instead of taking it back; look at the screen and ask the user. A run whose window never comes to the front (element_action through patterns only, with the agent's terminal in front) is never stopped by this |

A client that cancels the call stops the step that is running; the request gets no result, and what ran stays done. Each step releases the keys and buttons it pressed, as a direct call does, and the run releases anything still held when it ends.

**What it returns.** `success` (true when every step that is not optional ran and succeeded), `ran` and `total`, `elapsedMs`, and `steps`: per step its `tool`, `id`, `status` (`ok`, `failed` or `skipped`), `elapsedMs` and, for a failed one, `errorCode`. A step's whole result (its JSON, as a direct call returns it) is in `result` only for a failed step, the last step that ran, and a step with `return: true`, within 24,000 characters for all of them together: the failed and the last step's come first, then the others in step order, and a step whose result did not fit has `resultOmitted: true` instead. The run returns at most 2 images, of those steps' captures or observations: the last step's first, then in step order. A run that stopped also has `stoppedBy`, `errorCode` and `error`, which names the step and says what to do. A run that did not succeed has `isError: true`. Progress: with a progress token, one notification per step (`step i of n: <tool> ok` or `failed`); a step's own progress is not sent.

<!-- tools:begin params:run_steps -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| window | object | Yes | - | The run's window: a selector with find_windows' filters, or {"handle": n}, resolved to exactly one window before the run; not {"foreground": true} alone |
| steps | object[] | Yes | - | The steps, 1-50, run in order |
| maxDurationMs | integer | No | 30000 | How long the run may hold the input gate, in milliseconds (default: 30000, min: 1000, max: 60000); a wait step's timeoutMs is cut to what is left |
| delayBetweenStepsMs | integer | No | 50 | The pause between two steps, in milliseconds (default: 50, min: 0, max: 2000) |

Each item of `steps` contains:
| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| tool | string (one of: `"focus_window"`, `"find_ui_elements"`, `"element_action"`, `"type_text"`, `"send_keys"`, `"press_keys"`, `"mouse_click"`, `"drag"`, `"mouse_move"`, `"scroll"`, `"wait_for_window"`, `"wait_for_element"`, `"get_focused_element"`, `"capture_window"`) | Yes | - | The tool to call |
| args | object | No | - | The tool's own arguments, as a direct call takes them. A string "$steps.<id>.<path>" is an earlier step's ref, handle, captureId or clickPoint x/y |
| id | string | No | - | A name for the step ([A-Za-z0-9_-], at most 32), unique in the run: later steps refer to its result by it |
| optional | boolean | No | false | True: the run goes on when this step fails (a dialog that may not appear). Default false: a failure stops the run |
| return | boolean | No | false | True: the step's whole result (and its image) is returned, not only its status |
<!-- tools:end params:run_steps -->

**Example:**
> "Fill in the name, accept the terms and save, in the form (handle 1706796)"

```json
{
  "name": "run_steps",
  "arguments": {
    "window": { "handle": 1706796 },
    "steps": [
      { "tool": "focus_window" },
      { "tool": "find_ui_elements", "id": "name", "args": { "automationId": "nameBox" } },
      { "tool": "element_action", "args": { "ref": "$steps.name.elements[0].ref", "action": "set_value", "value": "Ada Lovelace" } },
      { "tool": "element_action", "args": { "automationId": "agree", "action": "toggle", "value": "on" } },
      { "tool": "element_action", "args": { "automationId": "saveButton", "action": "invoke" } },
      { "tool": "wait_for_element", "args": { "automationId": "status", "condition": "name_equals", "expected": "Saved", "timeoutMs": 5000 } }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "ran": 6,
  "total": 6,
  "elapsedMs": 812,
  "steps": [
    { "tool": "focus_window", "status": "ok", "elapsedMs": 64 },
    { "tool": "find_ui_elements", "status": "ok", "id": "name", "elapsedMs": 120 },
    { "tool": "element_action", "status": "ok", "elapsedMs": 98 },
    { "tool": "element_action", "status": "ok", "elapsedMs": 87 },
    { "tool": "element_action", "status": "ok", "elapsedMs": 140 },
    { "tool": "wait_for_element", "status": "ok", "elapsedMs": 210,
      "result": { "success": true, "satisfied": true, "elapsedMs": 205, "polls": 2,
                  "element": { "ref": "w4120035e40", "name": "Saved", "controlType": "Text" } } }
  ]
}
```

**Error Response:** the Save button was not found, so the wait was skipped.
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "ran": 5,
  "total": 6,
  "elapsedMs": 1406,
  "steps": [
    { "tool": "focus_window", "status": "ok", "elapsedMs": 64 },
    { "tool": "find_ui_elements", "status": "ok", "id": "name", "elapsedMs": 120 },
    { "tool": "element_action", "status": "ok", "elapsedMs": 98 },
    { "tool": "element_action", "status": "ok", "elapsedMs": 87 },
    { "tool": "element_action", "status": "failed", "elapsedMs": 1030, "errorCode": "ElementNotFound",
      "result": { "success": false, "action": "invoke", "windowHandle": 1706796, "errorCode": "ElementNotFound", "error": "No element matches the criteria. ..." } },
    { "tool": "wait_for_element", "status": "skipped" }
  ],
  "stoppedBy": "stepFailed",
  "errorCode": "ElementNotFound",
  "error": "Step 5 (element_action) failed with ElementNotFound: No element matches the criteria. ... Step 6 was skipped; the steps before it ran and are not undone."
}
```

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|------|---------|------------|
| `InvalidArguments` | A step is wrong (above), or `maxDurationMs` or `delayBetweenStepsMs` is out of range, or `window` is `{"foreground": true}` alone; nothing was done (a tool error). In a step's result: the run did not call the step | Fix the step it names |
| `TargetIsAgentHost` | `window` is your own terminal or chat window; nothing was done (a tool error) | Name the window you mean |
| `InvalidHandle` | `window` names a window that is gone; nothing was done (a tool error) | Find the window again |
| `PausedByUser`, `InputBusy` | Before the first step, as for any input call; nothing was done (a tool error) | As for any input call |
| A step's code | The step failed (`stoppedBy: "stepFailed"`), as its own section describes | Read the failed step's `result` |
| `PausedByUser`, `OperationTimedOut`, `TargetNotForeground`, `UserInterrupted` | The run stopped (`stoppedBy` above) | See the table above |

---

## App Launch

Tools for launching applications and managing processes.

### launch_application

Launch an application by path, name, installed app (its `appId` or exact name from [list_installed_apps](#list_installed_apps)), or protocol URI, and optionally wait for the window it opens, whichever process owns that window.

<!-- tools:begin params:launch_application -->
**Parameters:**
| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| executable | string | Yes | - | Path, app name, or protocol URI |
| arguments | string[] | No | - | Command line arguments |
| workingDirectory | string | No | - | Working directory for the app |
| waitForWindow | boolean | No | false | Wait for window to appear |
| waitTimeoutMs | integer | No | 5000 | How long to wait for the window, in ms (clamped to 0-30000) |
| expectWindow | object | No | - | With `waitForWindow` (or `placement`): `processName` and/or `titleContains` of the window to expect, for Store apps, URIs and documents whose app the server cannot tell from what was started. `reuseExisting` checks an open window against it too (see [Reusing an open window](#reusing-an-open-window)) |
| placement | object | No | - | Where to put the window once it is found: `snap` or `bounds`, `monitor`, `state`, `focus` (see [Launch and arrange](#launch-and-arrange)); implies waiting for the window |
| reuseExisting | boolean | No | false | Use an open window of the app instead of starting another copy (`launchStatus` `alreadyOpen`; see [Reusing an open window](#reusing-an-open-window)) |
| forceAccessibility | boolean | No | false | Start a Chromium browser, an Electron or a CEF app with `--force-renderer-accessibility`, so its pages are readable from the first UI Automation read (see [Web content accessibility](#web-content-accessibility)) |
| runAsAdmin | boolean | No | false | Start the `.exe` as administrator: Windows asks the user (UAC), or the user is asked through the client where Windows would not (see [Running as administrator](#running-as-administrator)) |
<!-- tools:end params:launch_application -->

**Example 1:** Launch by name
> "Open Notepad"

```json
{
  "name": "launch_application",
  "arguments": {
    "executable": "notepad"
  }
}
```

**Example 2:** Launch with arguments
> "Open the README file in Notepad"

```json
{
  "name": "launch_application",
  "arguments": {
    "executable": "notepad",
    "arguments": ["C:\\Projects\\README.md"]
  }
}
```

**Example 3:** Launch and wait for window
> "Open VS Code in the project folder and wait for it"

```json
{
  "name": "launch_application",
  "arguments": {
    "executable": "code.exe",
    "arguments": ["C:\\Projects\\MyApp"],
    "waitForWindow": true,
    "waitTimeoutMs": 10000
  }
}
```

**Example 4:** Open URL
> "Open GitHub in the browser"

```json
{
  "name": "launch_application",
  "arguments": {
    "executable": "https://github.com"
  }
}
```

**Example 5:** Open a Settings page and wait for its window
> "Open the display settings"

```json
{
  "name": "launch_application",
  "arguments": {
    "executable": "ms-settings:display",
    "waitForWindow": true,
    "expectWindow": { "processName": "SystemSettings" }
  }
}
```

**Example 6:** Start a packaged app by its `appId` (from [list_installed_apps](#list_installed_apps)); `processId` is the app's own process (see [Packaged apps](#packaged-apps))
```json
{
  "name": "launch_application",
  "arguments": {
    "executable": "Microsoft.WindowsCalculator_8wekyb3d8bbwe!App",
    "waitForWindow": true
  }
}
```

**Response** (`calc` handed off to the Calculator app: the window belongs to another process than `processId`, which has exited):
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "processId": 15432,
  "windowHandle": 2884384,
  "launchStatus": "windowObserved",
  "window": {
    "handle": 2884384,
    "title": "Calculator",
    "processName": "CalculatorApp",
    "processId": 16020,
    "bounds": { "x": 120, "y": 80, "width": 336, "height": 545 },
    "state": "normal",
    "isVisible": true,
    "monitorIndex": 0,
    "className": "ApplicationFrameWindow",
    "isCloaked": false,
    "hostProcessName": "ApplicationFrameHost",
    "hostProcessId": 9216,
    "visibleBounds": { "x": 127, "y": 80, "width": 322, "height": 538 }
  },
  "launcherExited": true
}
```

**Launch status** (`launchStatus`): what the launch led to. `success` is `true` for every status: the launch was handed to Windows. Never launch again only because no window was found; that opens a second copy.

| `launchStatus` | Meaning | `window` |
|----------------|---------|----------|
| `started` | A process was started; the call did not wait for a window | - |
| `windowObserved` | A new window of the launch appeared and stayed: of the started process, a process it started, or the running app it handed off to (a browser, `calc` to Calculator, `wt` to Windows Terminal, `code.exe` to the VS Code that is already running) | The window |
| `reusedExistingWindow` | No new window appeared, but a window of the app that was already open came to the front: single-instance apps reuse their window | That window |
| `openedInTab` | No new window appeared, but a window of the app that was already open now shows the launched document (a new tab, in Windows 11 Notepad, Terminal, VS Code, Explorer or a browser) | That window |
| `possibleHandoff` | Windows started no process: the request went to an app that was already running, or a packaged app was started through the shell (from an elevated server, see [Packaged apps](#packaged-apps)) or handed its activation to an instance that was running (`processId` is absent). With `waitForWindow`, no window of it was recognised | - |
| `exitedWithoutWindow` | The started process exited, and no window of it or of an app it may have handed off to was recognised | - |
| `timedOut` | The program is still running, but no window of it appeared within `waitTimeoutMs`; it may still be starting. Also a packaged app whose activation did not return within 15 seconds (`processId` absent) | - |
| `awaitingUserConsent` | The start did not return within 5 seconds: Windows is most likely showing a consent or security prompt (UAC, SmartScreen, a security warning for a downloaded or network file, or "How do you want to open this file?"). Only the user may answer it; do not click or type into it. The program starts only if the user approves; `processId` is absent, and a decline after the 5 seconds is not reported | - |
| `alreadyOpen` | Only with `reuseExisting`: a window of the app was already open (see [Reusing an open window](#reusing-an-open-window)), so nothing was started; `processId` is absent | That window |

`warning` says what to do for the statuses without a window: look for the window with [find_windows](#find_windows), or launch with `expectWindow`. `launcherExited` (after a window wait) is `true` when the started process had exited by then, as launchers and single-instance stubs do after a handoff. `forceAccessibilityApplied` is there only with `forceAccessibility` (see [Web content accessibility](#web-content-accessibility)).

**How the window is found** (with `waitForWindow`): the server records the open windows before the start and then, every 100 ms, looks for a new visible, titled, uncloaked app window that belongs to the launch: a window of the started process or of a process it started (checked by start time, so a reused process ID does not count), of a process with the same program path or name, of the app a launcher hands off to (`calc` to `CalculatorApp`, `wt`, `cmd`, `powershell` and `pwsh` to `WindowsTerminal`, `ms-settings:` to `SystemSettings`, an `http` or `https` address to Edge, Chrome, Firefox, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi or Arc), or one that matches `expectWindow`. A UWP app's window is matched by the app's own process, not `ApplicationFrameHost`. The window must stay for 300 ms (a splash screen does not count), then the server waits up to a second for the app to be ready for input. While no new window is pending, a window of the app that was already open counts once it has come to the front, or once its title changed to show the launched file or folder (as a whole name, and after a path only the launched one, as for [reuseExisting](#reusing-an-open-window)) or to contain `expectWindow.titleContains`, which its title did not show before the start, for a second (`reusedExistingWindow`, `openedInTab`). A host name in a page's title does not count: the page sets it. A packaged app's window is a window of any process of its package (see [Packaged apps](#packaged-apps)). `expectWindow` is needed when the server cannot tell the app from what was started: a desktop app's `shell:AppsFolder` entry, a document opened by whatever app is registered for it, or another browser or URI scheme.

#### Launch and arrange

`placement` launches, places, focuses and confirms in one call, instead of launch, find_windows, snap_window and focus_window. It implies `waitForWindow`; once the window is found (whichever status found it, `alreadyOpen` included), the server places it with the same code as the window tools, watches it until it stays put, places it again each time the app moves it back, as browsers and VS Code do when they restore their saved bounds, and then brings it to the front.

**Apps that move their window back** (roadmap M3.F27). After the placement the server reads the window again after 250 ms, then at intervals that double up to a second, until it has stayed where it was placed for a second, and for at most 3 seconds. Each time the window has moved, been resized or changed state on its own (once or several times, early or late in those 3 seconds), it is placed again, and the reads start over from 250 ms; so a window the app leaves alone costs a second, and one the app moves back costs more, up to the 3 seconds.
