  they do not declare, naming it and, when one is within two edits, the declared name it most likely stands for, where
  they used to ignore it and run. Nothing is done, and the refusal is audited. Every other tool still ignores such an
  argument (see [Undeclared arguments](#undeclared-arguments)).
- **Target policy.** The default deny list adds `CredDialogHost` (a Windows credential prompt), `CHXSmartScreen` and
  `smartscreen` (the SmartScreen prompt "Windows protected your PC") and `SecHealthUI` (the Windows Security app), so
  input, window changes, closes, kills and captures of them now return `TargetDeniedByPolicy`; a `WAM_DENY_PROCESSES`
  value without `default` is unchanged. The policy now also covers the UI Automation reads:
  [get_ui_elements](#get_ui_elements) of a denied app's window (password managers and credential prompts by default), and
  [get_focused_element](#get_focused_element) and [get_element_at_point](#get_element_at_point) of a denied app's window
  or of an element a denied process provides, fail with `TargetDeniedByPolicy` (the new UI element errorCode 24) before
  any warm-up or read, where they used to read it; capture_window and capture_with_elements already refused it. The new
  reads refuse it too, and leave the popups of a denied app, and those of the agent's own host, out of what they list
  and search (see [Target policy](#target-policy)). A window whose process name cannot be read (it exited, or the server
  may not query it) is now refused with `TargetDeniedByPolicy` while the policy denies anything (it does by default),
  where it used to be acted on: by the input tools, focus_window (also for a window it would activate or a restore would
  show), the other window tools and their batches, close_window, close_windows_batch, close_application, apply_layout,
  capture_window and capture_with_elements (also for a window `restoreIfMinimized` would show) and the UI Automation
  reads (get_focused_element and get_element_at_point also for an element whose own process cannot be named); the new
  launch `placement` and `reuseExisting` never place or reuse it, and save_layout no longer saves its title. With
  `WAM_DENY_PROCESSES=none` and no allow list, such a window is still allowed. The window lists
  ([find_windows](#find_windows), get_all_windows, ...) are unchanged.
- **allowHostTarget never reaches the server's own windows.** The input tools refuse a window of this server's own
  process, or a window one owns, with `TargetIsAgentHost` even with `allowHostTarget: true`, and so do element_action,
  respond_to_dialog and file_dialog. The server shows no window of its own, so such a window is a prompt Windows showed
  for it, such as the security warning of a downloaded file that launch_application opens; only the user answers it.
  `allowHostTarget` still lifts the host rule for the agent's own terminal, editor or chat app.
- **Audit log.** element_action, respond_to_dialog and file_dialog are audited. element_action keeps its `ref`, its fixed
  values (`action`, `mode`, `direction`, `amount`, `fallback`, `observe`) and its result's `method` and `status`, and
  records its `value` and its `name` criterion as lengths (`valueLength`, `nameLength`); respond_to_dialog keeps its
  `button`, and file_dialog its `action` and its `path` as `pathLength`; both name the dialog they answered as the line's
  `target`, also when the call named its owner, a selector or no window. A mouse call keeps its `space` and records a
  `captureId` as its length. A launch keeps its `launchStatus` under `result`, a launch batch item's `launchStatus` as
  its `status`, and the placement under `target` or the item. A call refused for an undeclared argument is logged too.
  See [Audit log](#audit-log).
- **UI Automation engine and bounded walks (roadmap M3.1 and M3.2).** The element tools read through the UI Automation
  COM client instead of the managed one (`WAM_UIA_ENGINE=uia2` goes back), with the same fields. AppBar and SemanticZoom
  elements are named from their ids on every display language; with the managed client a non-English Windows gave them
  a localized name. Through the COM client, a UI Automation call gives up on an application that does not connect within
  1 s or answer within 5 s, so a hung provider costs a call seconds instead of holding it until the timeout.
  get_ui_elements reads breadth first and returns at most `maxElements` elements (default 300; it had no limit), so a window with more elements now
  returns `truncated: true` with the new `truncationReason: MaxElements`; pass a larger `maxElements` (up to 5000) to read
  more. A level of more than 200 elements is read one element at a time and can be cut in the middle. When the timeout
  passes, a level of up to 200 elements whose properties were already fetched is returned whole, and a timeout or a hang
  can leave out deeper levels that the depth-first walk used to reach first. A window that Windows reports hung, or that
  does not answer a message within 500 ms, fails at once with `NotResponding` (the new UI element errorCode 10; it used
  to block until the timeout); capture_with_elements then captures the image without overlays and reports it as
  `elementsErrorCode`. New parameter `format` (`tree`, the default and the old shape, `flat` or `text`). get_server_info
  reports `uiAutomation` (the engine in force, where it came from and those two timeouts) and warns about a
  `WAM_UIA_ENGINE` value that is neither `uia3` nor `uia2`.
- **Element refs (roadmap M3.4).** Every element of get_ui_elements, get_focused_element and get_element_at_point, and
  every mark of capture_with_elements, gains `ref` (for example `w4120035e17`) as its first field: a short name for the
  element that later calls take instead of coordinates or a repeated search (element_action, read_element_text,
  read_table, wait_for_element, find_ui_elements' `withinRef`, capture_window's `ref`). A ref names the same element in
  every read of the server session and never silently another one: a ref moved to a re-created element that alone fits
  its description is reported (`refMoved: true` and a `warning`), and element_action refuses it until a read that finds
  or lists elements, such as find_ui_elements, returns that element again. A tool given a ref that no longer names one
  element fails with the new codes `ElementStale` (11) or `AmbiguousElement` (12) (see [Element refs](#ui-automation)).
- **Web content accessibility (roadmap M3.3).** get_ui_elements, capture_with_elements, get_focused_element and
  get_element_at_point now wait up to 1.5 s (at most a third of `timeoutMs`) the first time they read a window with a
  Chromium, Electron or WebView2 page (and a tab shown since), so such a first call can take that much longer, and their
  results carry `accessibilityWarmup` when they waited (see [Web content](#ui-automation)). Elements carry `frameworkId`:
  get_ui_elements reports it at the top and on an element only where it changes (`fw=` in the text format),
  get_focused_element and get_element_at_point on every element, and get_element_at_point's `ancestors` have it too.
  launch_application takes `forceAccessibility` and then returns `forceAccessibilityApplied` (see
  [Web content accessibility](#web-content-accessibility)). All of these are new fields; a call without
  `forceAccessibility` launches as before.
- **captureId and coordinate spaces (roadmap M3.11).** A successful capture result has a new field `captureId` (left out
  when a captured window's rectangle cannot be read, and by capture_with_elements when the window moved while its
  elements were read), and take_screenshot takes `monitorIndex: -1` for the whole virtual screen (it used to fail with
  `InvalidMonitorIndex`). click, right_click, double_click, mouse_move and scroll take `space` (`screen`, `window`,
  `client`, `image`) and `captureId` (see [Coordinate spaces for the mouse tools](#coordinate-spaces-for-the-mouse-tools));
  a call without them is unchanged and its result has no `requested`. With them, `x` and `y` in the result are the
  converted screen point and `requested` echoes the point as given; two new input error codes, `StaleCapture` (46) and
  `CaptureNotFound` (47), refuse a point whose capture changed or is gone.
- **capture_with_elements draws Set-of-Marks, and capture_window crops to an element (roadmap M3.11).**
  [capture_with_elements](#capture_with_elements) changes what it returns by default. Each mark now has a filled tag with
  the element's ref, and the marks are drawn on the returned image after it was scaled (the boxes were drawn before,
  widened by the scale). Without `controlTypes`, only elements with an action pattern are marked (`actionableOnly`, new,
  defaults to true then); labels, panes, groups and other containers are no longer drawn. Pass `actionableOnly: false`
  for the earlier set. The walk stops at `maxElements` (new, default 80; it had no limit) with
  `truncationReason: "MaxElements"`. The metadata has a new `legend`, one line per mark, and leaves `elements` out unless
  `detail: "full"` (new) is passed: a client that reads `elements[].screenBounds` must pass `detail: "full"`, or take the
  legend's `center` with the `captureId`, or act on the ref with element_action. `elementCount` still counts the marks.
  A window that moved while its elements were read is captured without a `captureId` and with a `WindowMoved` warning.
  New `labels` (default true) and `drawOverlays` (default true; false returns the clean image).
  [capture_window](#capture_window) takes `ref` and `padding` (new) to crop the image to one element; without them it is
  unchanged, and its result gains `ref` only with them. New screenshot errorCode `ElementOffscreen` (capture_window with a
  ref); capture_window with a ref can also return the ref errors `ElementStale` and `AmbiguousElement` and the UI
  Automation codes `NotResponding`, `OperationTimedOut`, `WindowNotFound` (UI Automation cannot read the window) and
  `OperationException`.
- **A right click pastes in more apps (M2 follow-up).** A right_click in a window of VS Code (or Code -
  Insiders, VSCodium, Cursor, Windsurf), Hyper, Tabby, WezTerm or Alacritty now counts as a paste, as one in the console
  does: it is refused with `PasteNotAllowed` while the clipboard holds content the agent may not paste.
- **Closing (roadmap M2.F1 and an M2 follow-up).** On a client that cannot ask the user, close_window and
  close_windows_batch no longer close the desktop shell or the agent's own host with `force: true` alone: the call closes
  nothing and fails with `ConfirmationRequired` (close_window in its result, the batch as a tool error, also for 3
  windows or fewer and for its ordinary windows) until it is repeated with `confirm: true` too. close_window gains the
  `confirm` argument for this. `force` on windows that are not protected, and every call on a client with elicitation
  (the user is asked, as in 1.14.0), are unchanged; close_application has no `force`. close_application's
  `otherDesktopWindows` no longer lists suspended or prelaunched Store app frames.
- **Launch and arrange (roadmap M3.13).** launch_application and the items of launch_applications_batch take
  `placement` and `reuseExisting` (see [Launch and arrange](#launch-and-arrange)). A call without them is unchanged. A
  result can carry `placement`, and `launchStatus` has a new value, `alreadyOpen`, only with `reuseExisting`; a client
  that switches over the statuses should treat an unknown one as a success with a window. `reuseExisting` reuses a
  window only when its title shows each launched file or folder as a whole name, never after another path, or contains
  `expectWindow.titleContains` when that is set; a web address or a URI page needs `expectWindow.titleContains`, since a
  page sets its own title, and a window whose title shows only the name is reused with a `warning` to check it (see
  [Reusing an open window](#reusing-an-open-window)).
- **The window a launch reports (M2 follow-up and M3 review).** With `waitForWindow`, launch_application and
  launch_applications_batch take a window that was already open and stayed in the background as the launch's
  (`openedInTab`) only when its title changed to show the launched file or folder as a whole name, after no other path
  than the launched one, and did not show it before the start (one that came to the front counts as before). It used to
  be enough that the title came to contain the name, or a web address's host, anywhere (`app` in `mapper.ts`). A host
  name in a page's title no longer counts, since the page sets it; `expectWindow.titleContains` now does. Such a launch
  can now end `possibleHandoff`, `exitedWithoutWindow` or `timedOut` instead: look for the window with find_windows. In
  a launch_applications_batch, an item whose launcher failed (a non-zero exit code) is no longer given a window of
  another item's instance: it reports `exitedWithoutWindow`.
- **get_desktop_state (roadmap M3.12).** Returns in one call the window in front, the cursor, the modifiers down, Caps
  Lock, the pause, the windows as compact rows, the focused element, the target window's popups and its elements as text
  lines with refs, and optionally a capture (`include` lists every section to read). One `timeoutMs` covers the call: a
  part not read by then is left out and listed in `errors`. It does not read the window in front, or its focus, when that
  is the agent's own host or an app the policy denies (a `target` or `focus` error), and its `scope` takes `window` and
  `windowAndPopups` only. [element_action](#element_action) takes `observe` (`state`, `screenshot`) to return this
  observation after the action as `observed`, and so do click, right_click, double_click, type_text, send_keys and
  respond_to_dialog; `screenshotMarks` draws the elements' refs on the capture (both roadmap M3.F32).
- **find_ui_elements and get_active_popups (roadmap M3.4, M3.5 and M3.10).** [find_ui_elements](#find_ui_elements)
  searches a window by name, automation id, control type and class with the provider evaluating the criteria, and
  returns refs, click points and patterns (at most `maxResults`, default 20). `scope` is `window`, `windowAndPopups`
  (also the window's open menus, dropdowns, flyouts and dialogs, which are windows of their own) or `desktop` (every
  visible window, at most 40); left out, it is `windowAndPopups` when the window, a window it owns or another window of
  its process is in front, else `window`. Denied windows are never searched (a named one is refused) and the agent's
  host windows only when named (`windowsExcluded` counts them). `withinRef` searches below an element, and
  `searchVirtualized` also asks lists for items they have not realized (`virtualized: true`). A search that did not
  finish is truncated (`Timeout`, `SearchLimit`, `PartsSkipped`, `WindowLimit`); a search held up in a provider call can
  end up to about 2 s after `timeoutMs`. [get_active_popups](#get_active_popups) lists an app's open menus, dropdowns,
  flyouts and dialogs with refs; with no window named it does not read the app in front when that is your own host
  (`TargetIsAgentHost`, new UI element errorCode 25) or an app the policy denies.
- **element_action (roadmap M3.6, M3.10, M3.12 and M3.14).** Acts on one element through UI Automation patterns and
  returns its state before and after and `outcomeVerified`. The element is named by its ref, or by a window and element
  criteria with find_ui_elements' `scope`, which must match exactly one element: several are `AmbiguousElement`, and a
  search that did not finish is `OperationTimedOut`. A ref moved to a re-created element is refused (`ElementStale`,
  `refMoved: true`). It runs inside the input gate with the input guard's target checks; `double_click`, `right_click`,
  `fallback: "mouse"` and `mode` `type` or `paste` send guarded input, and a click point is hit-tested first
  (`TargetOccluded` when another element covers it). `realize` makes a virtualized item real and scrolls it into view
  (`maxScrolls`: by scrolling the window's one list); `menu_path` opens a path such as `File>Save As` (`steps`);
  `observe` adds get_desktop_state's observation. New UI element errorCodes `PatternNotSupported` (13),
  `ElementNotEnabled` (14), `ElementOffscreen` (15), `ElementReadOnly` (16), `FocusNotOnElement` (17), `ActionFailed`
  (18), `ActionTimedOut` (19) and `ActionsPending` (20). Under the UIA3 engine the server turns off UI Automation's
  AutoSetFocus, so pattern calls do not move focus; the read tools are unchanged by it.
- **respond_to_dialog and file_dialog (roadmap M3.5 and M3.14).** [respond_to_dialog](#respond_to_dialog) reads a
  dialog's title, text and buttons and presses one through element_action's `invoke`, by standard name in any language;
  without `button` it only reads. A press needs the dialog named by `handle` or `window` (its `dialogHandle`, or
  close_window's `prompt.handle`): only `cancel` goes to the dialog in front, and any other button is refused with
  `InvalidArguments`. A press asked of a named dialog that a modal dialog of its own disables is `BlockedByModal`, and
  `ok` presses a dialog's only button only when it carries the id of Cancel or Close. A dialog drawn inside its window
  has no window of its own: press its button with element_action. [file_dialog](#file_dialog) completes an Open or Save
  As dialog named by `handle` or `window` with a full path. Its `save` is `completed: true` only once a file is seen
  written at `finalPath`; it answers the replace prompt only when the prompt's text names the file, and refuses `open` in
  a Save As dialog (`DialogNotFound`). New UI element errorCodes `DialogNotFound` (21), `DialogNotCompleted` (22) and
  `FileExists` (23, the same name as the captures' code).
- **read_element_text and read_table (roadmap M3.9).** [read_element_text](#read_element_text) reads an element's text a
  page at a time (the Text pattern's document, the value, or the name; at most `maxLength` characters and 60,000 bytes of
  JSON a page), never a password field's. [read_table](#read_table) reads a grid's or list's headers and cells a page of
  rows at a time (at most 40,000 bytes of JSON) and never scrolls: a row a virtualized grid has not realized ends the
  page (`truncationReason: NotRealized`). A criteria search that did not finish is no proof of one match:
  read_element_text, like element_action, refuses it with `OperationTimedOut`, or `AmbiguousElement` when it found
  several. read_table returns `PatternNotSupported` for an element that is no table.
- **wait_for_window and wait_for_element (roadmap M3.7 and M3.8).** [wait_for_window](#wait_for_window) waits on the
  server until a window exists, is gone, is in front, is on screen, has a new title or is ready for input;
  [wait_for_element](#wait_for_element) until an element, named by `ref` or by find_ui_elements' criteria in a `window`
  that is waited for first, exists, is gone, is enabled, visible or focused, or has an expected name, value or toggle
  state. A wait that is not satisfied is a failure (`isError: true`) with the new errorCode `WaitTimedOut` (37), and its
  result still carries `timedOut`, `elapsedMs` and what was last seen; wait_for_element can also end early with
  `WindowNotFound`, `ElementStale`, `AmbiguousElement`, `AmbiguousWindow` or `TargetDeniedByPolicy`. wait_for_window's
  condition must hold for `stableMs` (default 300); wait_for_element has no `stableMs`, and can end up to about 3 s after
  `timeoutMs` when UI Automation is slow.
- **Titles and AutomationIds are cut at 200 characters (roadmap M3.F14).** The window tools, a selector's `candidates`,
  find_ui_elements, wait_for_element, get_active_popups, get_desktop_state and element_action's `openedPopup` used to
  return them whole, however long an application made them. A longer one is now cut to 200 characters ending in `…`, as
  respond_to_dialog's titles were already cut (its cut titles, button names and AutomationIds now end in `…` too). The
  filters and criteria still compare the whole value; a client that passes a cut title to `titleEquals`, or a cut
  AutomationId to `automationId`, finds nothing (see [Untrusted content](#untrusted-content)).
- **Warnings for minimized and elevated windows (roadmap M3.F16).** get_ui_elements gains `warnings` (left out when
  there is nothing to say), and get_desktop_state's `elements` too: `WindowMinimized` when the window's top-level window
  is minimized (its elements are offscreen; the call still succeeds, as before, with `windowState: "Minimized"`), and
  `TargetElevated` when the window's process runs at a higher integrity level than the server, whose tree UI Automation
  cannot read (it used to come back empty without a word). capture_with_elements adds `TargetElevated` to its `warnings`.
  No call that succeeded fails now.
- **Stuck reads per window in multi-window searches (roadmap M3.F13).** A `windowAndPopups` or `desktop` search by
  find_ui_elements' criteria (wait_for_element, read_element_text and element_action included) used to count a UI
  Automation read stuck in any of its windows against the named window's application, so after a popup of another
  process hung, the next searches of the named window failed at once with `OperationTimedOut`. Each window is now read on
  its own and counted against its own application: such a popup is skipped (`truncationReason: "PartsSkipped"`) and the
  named window is still searched. Only a stuck named window fails the call, as before.
- **Commands and scripts are not run (roadmap M3.F8).** launch_application and the items of launch_applications_batch
  used to start `cmd`, PowerShell and other interpreters with any arguments, with only a warning, and to run scripts. A
  command interpreter, script host or other program that runs what its command line names, given any arguments, is now
  refused with `InterpreterWithArguments`, and a script (`.bat`, `.cmd`, `.ps1`, `.vbs`, `.js`, `.hta`, `.py`, `.msi`,
  ...) with `ScriptFile`, with or without arguments; nothing is started (see [Commands and scripts](#commands-and-scripts)).
  apply_layout's `launchMissing` reports a script `launchCommand` as `LaunchFailed`. Started without arguments, an
  interpreter opens as before, without the warning. Batch file shims are scripts too: `code` (VS Code's `bin\code.cmd`)
  and `npm` (`npm.cmd`) are refused, so launch `code.exe` (App Paths resolves it to `Code.exe`) or the program's full path.
- **"Open File - Security Warning" is refused in any process (roadmap M3.F5).** Windows shows this prompt inside
  whichever process opens a downloaded file (explorer.exe when File Explorer opens it), so the deny list could not name
  it, and the agent could answer it. While the deny list includes the default list, the [target policy](#target-policy)
  now recognizes the dialog by its controls and refuses it with `TargetDeniedByPolicy` wherever it refuses a denied
  app's window: input, element_action, respond_to_dialog, file_dialog, the window tools, the captures and the UI
  Automation reads. In the server's own process (after launch_application opens a downloaded file) it used to be refused
  with `TargetIsAgentHost`. No tool, parameter or error code is new.
- **The default deny list adds the sign-in and Windows Security hosts (roadmap M3.F6).** `Microsoft.AAD.BrokerPlugin`
  (the Entra ID and Microsoft account sign-in window, which takes passwords) and `SecurityHealthHost` (Windows
  Security's notifications and prompts) join the default list, so input, window changes, closes, captures and UI
  Automation reads of them return `TargetDeniedByPolicy`. A `WAM_DENY_PROCESSES` value without `default` is unchanged.
- **The default deny list adds `WWAHost` (roadmap M3.F3).** On a real desktop, Settings' "Access work or school >
  Connect" opens its Microsoft account sign-in window in WWAHost.exe, not in Microsoft.AAD.BrokerPlugin, and the policy
  let an agent read and type into it. WWAHost also hosts other web-based system UIs and the rare old JavaScript Store app,
  which are denied with it; a `WAM_DENY_PROCESSES` value without `default` is unchanged.
- **Set-of-Marks tags are shorter and sit beside their elements (roadmap M3.F38).** [capture_with_elements](#capture_with_elements)
  and get_desktop_state's `screenshotMarks` drew every mark's whole ref in its tag, inside the element's top-left corner
  whenever another tag or the image's edge was above it, so on a crowded window (79 marks of File Explorer) the tags
  covered the rows' names and each other. When every mark's ref has the same window part, the tags now show only the
  element part (`e44`), and the result has a new field `markPrefix` with the window part (`w1399829`): the ref is
  `markPrefix` followed by the tag. get_desktop_state reports it as `screenshot.markPrefix`. The legend and the element
  lines still give whole refs, and the tags of refs of more than one window still show whole refs, without `markPrefix`.
  A tag now goes outside its element where nothing else is (above it, left of it or below it), and inside it only when
  there is no room, at the right end of a wide element; it is never drawn over an earlier tag while another of its places
  is free. A client that reads refs off the image must put `markPrefix` before the tag; no parameter or error code changed.
- **searchVirtualized keeps placeholders that do not say what they are (roadmap M3.F37).** find_ui_elements with
  `searchVirtualized: true` (and element_action's criteria search for `realize`) no longer tests `controlType` on an
  item a list returned as a placeholder (it serves only some properties, or has no runtime id) whose control type is
  `Custom` or `Unknown`: File Explorer's are `Custom`, its realized items `ListItem`, so `controlType: "ListItem"` found
  no file it had not realized. Such an item is now returned, with `virtualized: true`, the control type it has, and a
  `note`. Every other item is tested on `controlType` as before.
- **Refs for list items without a runtime id (roadmap M3.F37).** An item find_ui_elements' `searchVirtualized` (or
  element_action's criteria search for `realize`) found through its list without a runtime id (File Explorer's
  placeholder for a file it has not realized) used to come back with `ref: null`, so element_action `realize` by
  criteria failed with `ElementAccessFailed` ("The element has no runtime id"). It now gets a ref that names it by the
  list's answer, `realize` makes it real with every check of an action, and the result reports the realized item under
  that ref. Two items the list matched alike still get no ref.
- **read_table on a virtualizing list (roadmap M3.F36).** A grid read through its realized rows that also has the
  ItemContainer pattern (Explorer's details view) may count only its realized rows in `totalRows` (42 of a folder's 300
  files). Every page of such a grid now carries a `warning` that says so, and a `startRow` at or past `totalRows`, which
  used to return an empty page with `truncated: false` (the end of the list, it seemed), now returns the realized rows
  there or an empty page with `truncationReason: NotRealized` and `nextStartRow` equal to `startRow`. Other grids and
  lists are read as before.
- **read_table reads a WinForms DataGridView (roadmap M3.F39).** A WinForms `DataGridView` read through UI Automation
  has neither the Grid nor the Table pattern, and its rows are `Custom` children ("Top Row", then "Row 0", "Row 1", ...)
  of `Header` and `DataItem` items, so read_table walked its children, found no row and returned `source: "Rows"`,
  `rows: []` and `totalRows: 0`, without an error or warning: the grid looked empty. Its `Custom` children that hold
  `DataItem` cells are now its rows, its "Top Row" gives the headers (without the corner cell above the row headers),
  each cell's text is its value (a cell is named `Amount Row 2`, not for its text), and a `Header` that starts a row is
  its row header, not a column. Paging, `totalRows`, the byte limit and the timeout work as for any list of rows. A
  WinForms row header exposes only a made-up name (`Row 0`), so the rows have no `rowHeaders`. Other grids and lists are
  read as before.
- **file_dialog and UWP file pickers (roadmap M3.F34).** The docs said a UWP app's file picker is `DialogNotFound`.
  Checked on Windows 11 (26200): a UWP app's FileOpenPicker and FileSavePicker are dialog boxes of PickerHost.exe with
  the ids of any Open or Save As dialog, and file_dialog fills them, by the app's window handle or the picker's own.
  Nothing in the tool changed.
- **Every tool refuses an argument it does not declare (roadmap M3.F42).** Only the acting tools (element_action,
  respond_to_dialog, file_dialog, the input, close and kill tools) refused such an argument; every other tool ignored it
  without a word, so take_screenshot with `handle` (it has no such parameter) captured the whole primary monitor, and
  get_window_info with a made-up argument succeeded. Every tool now fails such a call with `InvalidArguments` (a tool
  error) before it runs, keyed on its input schema's properties and matched exactly, letter case included, as the
  arguments are bound. The error names the argument, now lists the tool's parameters, and suggests a near miss more
  often: besides another letter case and two edits, the only parameter that ends with the argument's words or whose
  words end it (`handle` for `windowHandle`, and the reverse). The message starts with `Invalid arguments for tool
  '<tool>'.`, as the other argument errors do. The request's `_meta` is not an argument and is not checked (see
  [Undeclared arguments](#undeclared-arguments)). A client that sent extra arguments to a read, window, capture, launch,
  layout or clipboard tool must leave them out.
- **A WinUI 3 WebView2's page in get_ui_elements, its warm-up, and elements met twice (roadmap M3.F43).** Checked on a
  real desktop (WebView2 runtime 155, Windows App SDK 1.6): a WinUI 3 window lists its WebView2's page twice, below its
  content bridge and below the XAML island's WebView2 pane (which lists the XAML island again), with the page's document
  at level 11, 8 levels below the root of Chromium's views. So get_ui_elements returned the page's wrapper panes twice,
  down to `maxDepth`, and never the page; find_ui_elements returned each page element twice with the same ref; and
  element_action by criteria failed with `AmbiguousElement` ("2 elements match ... (first: w..e25 Button 'Page button',
  w..e25 Button 'Page button')"). The first read also had no `accessibilityWarmup`: the search for the document stopped
  6 levels down. Now a search counts an element it reaches twice (the same runtime id) as one match, in every tool that
  searches by criteria; the walk of a window (get_ui_elements, capture_with_elements, get_desktop_state's `elements`)
  lists an element it meets again only where it met it first, and leaves out the second copy with everything inside it
  (an app's tree that loops back on itself now ends); the warm-up finds the root of Chromium's views (the first element
  whose `frameworkId` is `Chrome`) and looks for the document below it (at most 12 levels and 24 listings), and reports
  `accessibilityWarmup` with `host: "WebView2"` on the first read; and the walk lists the page's document in place of
  that root's children, a level below it (level 4 of a WinUI 3 window). See [WebView2 hosted as a
  visual](#ui-automation). A window without web content is read as before. An element without a runtime id is still
  counted and listed each time.
- **Mouse correctness: one batch per click, swapped buttons, a real double click (roadmap M4.2).** Every mouse
  operation (click, right_click, double_click, mouse_move, scroll and element_action's mouse path) is now one SendInput
  batch built in one place: an absolute move to the pixel across the virtual desktop (`MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK`, spanning
  Windows' own virtual screen, `SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN` to `SM_CYVIRTUALSCREEN`, read for every call, so a monitor left of or
  above the primary one, at a negative coordinate, and monitors at different scales are hit exactly), then the buttons or
  the wheel. The normalized coordinate is chosen to hit the pixel under every mapping Windows may apply, the last column
  and row too. With the mouse buttons swapped in Windows' settings, click and double_click pressed the left button,
  which Windows turned into a right click (and right_click into a left one); they now press the user's primary and
  secondary buttons. double_click sent its clicks in two batches up to 500 ms apart, with the point checked between them,
  so a slow check or a short double-click time could make two single clicks; both clicks now go in the one batch, at
  the same pixel, and its `delayMs` is accepted and ignored. mouse_move used SetCursorPos, which applications that watch
  raw input or a low-level hook do not see; it now sends the same absolute move. New error code `CursorClamped`: right
  after the batch the pointer is not at the point (`actualX`, `actualY` say where it is), because it was confined to a
  window just then, the point is on no monitor, or something moved it at once. Unlike every other input code, the input
  was sent: the result has `success: false` and says so, and the click may have landed where the pointer is. mouse_move
  returns it where it returned `CursorNotAtPoint` (a confined pointer) and `SendInputFailed` where it returned
  `CursorPositionFailed`. No parameter was added or removed.
- **send_keys and type_text: the keyboard engine (roadmap M4.1).** send_keys typed letters and digits by their keys
  without Shift (so `Hello` came out `hello`, and AZERTY digits came out as symbols), sent every other character as
  Unicode (so Ctrl or Alt with punctuation, `^-` or `%.`, never fired a shortcut), and sent no scan codes. Now every
  character is typed with the key of the target window's keyboard layout (VkKeyScanEx), with the Shift or AltGr it
  needs and the key's scan code (MapVirtualKeyEx), allowing for Caps Lock (and a `{CAPSLOCK}` earlier in the keys); AltGr goes
  out as the left Ctrl and the right Alt, which the chord checks read as a character, not a Ctrl+Alt chord; only a character the layout has no key for,
  or only a dead key, is Unicode (see [send_keys](#send_keys)). The grammar gains `#` for the Windows key, `(...)`
  groups, `{NAME n}` repeats (1 to 100), `{NAME down}` and `{NAME up}` within one call (a key still down is released at
  the end), `~` for Enter, the escapes `{+} {^} {%} {#} {~} {(} {)} {{} {}}` (any single character in braces, an emoji too, is that
  character), and the keys F13-F24, NUMPAD0-9, ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE, DECIMAL, SEPARATOR, CLEAR, the OEM keys
  and the browser, volume, media and launch keys; key names may be written with `VK_` and underscores. New `delayMs`
  (0-500) paces the keys, with the window checked again before each, and new `keysSent` in the result says how many
  keys were sent, also when SendInput stops part way (`SendInputFailed`, with what it pressed released again).
  **Breaking:** `#` was an ordinary character and is now the Windows key: send `{#}` for the character; and as any
  chord with the Windows key opens a part of Windows, keys after one are refused (`KeysAfterFocusChange`), so `#tag`
  is refused instead of typing "#tag". `%` was always Alt (`100%{ENTER}` is Alt+Enter): write `100{%}{ENTER}`. A
  modifier with no key after it (`abc^`), a `)` or `}` that closes nothing, an unclosed group and a bad count are now
  `InvalidKeySpecification` (a trailing modifier used to be pressed and released, and a `}` was typed). A tab and a line
  break in `keys` are the Tab and Enter keys (they were Unicode characters). **type_text** stays Unicode, but text with
  a line break or tab now needs `controlChars` (`unicode`, `keys` or `shiftEnter`; see [Line breaks and
  tabs](#line-breaks-and-tabs)) and is refused with `InvalidArguments` without it, because a line break typed as Enter
  sends a chat message or submits a form; `\r\n` and a lone `\r` are typed as one `\n`, which `charactersTyped` counts.
  A client that typed multi-line text must pass `controlChars: "unicode"` for what it did before (without the `\r`).
  element_action's keyboard typing (`mode: "type"`) types line breaks as `unicode` does.
- **mouse_click and drag (roadmap M4.3, mouse_click and drag).** Two new input tools in the `input` toolset, both
  destructive, audited and inside the input gate like click. [mouse_click](#mouse_click) clicks any button (`primary`,
  `secondary`, `middle`, `x1`, `x2`) one to three times (`clickCount`) with modifier keys held (`modifiers`: `ctrl`,
  `shift`, `alt`, `win`): the modifier key-downs, the move, the clicks and the key-ups go in one SendInput batch, with
  every check click makes; its result adds `clickCount` and `modifiers`, and `clickType` is the button. [drag](#drag)
  presses a button at `fromX`, `fromY`, waits `holdBeforeMoveMs` (default 100), moves in `steps` absolute moves (default
  10, the first beyond the drag threshold) with `stepDelayMs` after each (default 20), and releases at `toX`, `toY`,
  with `modifiers` held throughout; both points take `space` and `captureId` (roadmap M3.F28). The to point must be on
  `windowHandle`'s window, or on `toWindowHandle`'s for a drop into another app, and is checked as a click's point
  before the press and again right before the drop. A drag stopped after the press goes back to the from point and
  releases there; the user's pause releases where the pointer is; nothing stays held after the call (`pressed` says
  whether anything was sent); the audit log records its `dropWindow`. The X buttons are now tracked as held input like
  the others, so a partial insert or a pause releases them too, and a held X1 or X2 refuses mouse input (`MouseInUse`).
  A middle click (or press) in a terminal now follows the paste rule as a right click does (`PasteNotAllowed`). click,
  right_click and double_click are unchanged.
- **press_keys (roadmap M4.3, press_keys).** A new input tool in the `input` toolset, destructive, audited and inside
  the input gate: [press_keys](#press_keys) presses keys by name, as a chord (`"ctrl+shift+t"` or `["ctrl", "shift",
  "t"]`) or a sequence (`"tab*3 enter"`, `["ctrl+a", "delete"]`), with `repeat` (1 to 100, at most 200 presses),
  `holdMs` (0 to 5000: the chord's keys stay down that long, within the call) and `delayBetweenMs` (0 to 1000), and
  presses × (holdMs + delayBetweenMs) at most 10,000 ms. Key names are send_keys' (M4.1), a letter or digit is its key
  on any layout, and other characters are mapped with the window's keyboard layout and sent with scan codes. The chords
  become the same input events as send_keys' keys, so the same checks apply: `DestructiveChordNeedsTarget` (`ctrl+w`
  needs `windowHandle`), `KeysAfterFocusChange`, `PauseChordNotAllowed`, `PasteNotAllowed`. The result is send_keys'
  (`keys`, `keysSent`). Nothing stays held after the call; there are no key_down or mouse_down tools.
- **type_text: paste mode and bounded text (roadmap M4.4).** New `method`: `unicode` (what type_text did), `keys` (each
  character with the key of the window's keyboard layout, as send_keys types it, for remote desktops and virtual machines
  that drop Unicode keystrokes; a character the layout has no key for is still Unicode), `paste` (lends the clipboard:
  puts the text there, presses Ctrl+V with scan codes and puts the clipboard's earlier text back about 500 ms later) and
  `auto`, the default, which types text of up to 200 characters as before and pastes longer text when it can (not into
  a terminal, not with `delayMs` or with `controlChars` `keys` or `shiftEnter`, and not multi-line text into VS Code,
  whose focus may be in its terminal), typing it otherwise. A paste goes through the paste rule as Ctrl+V does, lends
  only a clipboard it can put back exactly (empty, or plain text not marked private; otherwise `ClipboardUnavailable`,
  or `auto` types), never pastes into a terminal (`PasteNotAllowed`) and reports `clipboardRestored`, with `warning`
  when the clipboard could not be put back; see [Typing or pasting](#typing-or-pasting). **Breaking:** the result no
  longer echoes `text`: it has `length` (the text's characters) and `method` instead; `charactersTyped` and `length`
  count code points, so an emoji is one character (it was two). Typing more than 5,000 characters is now refused with
  the new `TextTooLong` (pasting takes up to 1,000,000), and a typed batch is 64 characters (it was 32). A client that
  sent long text to type_text and relied on keystrokes (an app that reacts to each key) must pass `method: "unicode"`,
  in parts of at most 5,000 characters. element_action's `mode: "type"` has the same 5,000-character limit.
- **CDP transport, targetId and explicit CDP errors (roadmap M5.2).** [get_browser_url](#get_browser_url) and
  [get_browser_content](#get_browser_content) take a new optional `targetId`: a tab id from an earlier result's
  `targetId` or from a `CdpTargetAmbiguous` error, read instead of the tab the window shows. It needs `cdpPort` (without
  it, or with an id that is not 1-128 letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, the call fails with `InvalidArguments` and reads
  nothing), implies `requireCdp`, and the debug port must belong to the window's process: on this path an owner the
  server cannot read is `CdpPortOwnerMismatch` too. A tab that has closed is `CdpTargetNotFound`.
  get_active_browser_url has no `targetId`. Two new codes: `CdpTargetClosed` when the tab's DevTools connection ends
  during the call (the tab closed, crashed or detached, or the browser exited; it was `CdpProtocolError`), and
  `CdpResponseTooLarge` for a tab list over 16 MB or a page over 64 MB (it was `CdpUnavailable` or `CdpProtocolError`);
  with `textOnly: false` an oversize page returns `CdpResponseTooLarge` instead of `HtmlRequiresCdp`. Without `targetId`
  and `requireCdp`, both fall back to UI Automation and appear in `cdpError` like the other CDP codes. A program on the
  port that answers, but not as a DevTools endpoint does (an HTTP error or redirect status included), is now
  `CdpProtocolError` (it was `CdpUnavailable`, which stays for a port nothing listens on); a tab whose WebSocket URL is
  on another port than `cdpPort`, or on another address than 127.0.0.1 (localhost and `[::1]` included), is refused
  (`CdpProtocolError`), the tab list is read without following redirects, and a WebSocket handshake the browser refuses
  with HTTP 403 is `CdpUnavailable` with the reason. The `CdpTargetAmbiguous` message names get_browser_url and
  get_browser_content as the tools that take `targetId`.
  Once the page reports an open dialog, a read returns `CdpDialogOpen` without sending anything more. The `cdpPort`
  descriptions no longer suggest 9222: pass the port launch_browser_with_debug returns. `ContentAreaNotFound` left the
  get_browser_content error table: no tool returned it.

- **Browser reading through UI Automation (roadmap M5.7).** get_browser_url, get_active_browser_url and
  get_browser_content no longer find anything by its name, which changes with the browser's display language and which
  a page sets. get_browser_url takes the URL from the shown tab's Document (the address the tab committed, with its
  scheme; `urlSource: "document"`), else from the address bar, found as Chromium's omnibox class, Firefox's
  `urlbar-input` id or the first edit box in a toolbar, never inside the page or the tabs (`urlSource: "addressBar"`),
  and returns it only when it is a URL. New result fields: `displayUrl` (the address bar's text, when URL-like),
  `urlSource` and `isEditing`. **Changed:** `url` now has its scheme when the page gives it (it was the address bar's
  text, often without `https://`); a window title, tab, bookmark or page link named like the address bar is no longer
  returned as the URL; a new tab page is the new `NewTabPage` (it was `UrlBarNotFound`); an address bar with the
  keyboard focus, or of a browser that is not the foreground window (whose address bar reports no focus), holding text
  that is not a URL or unreadable, when the page gives no address, is `UrlExtractionFailed` (its text was returned as
  the URL). get_browser_url now waits for a Chromium page's accessibility tree before it reads, as get_browser_content
  does, and its description says where the URL comes from. get_browser_content reads the shown tab's Document, not
  docked DevTools, a side panel, Edge's sidebar or a frame inside the page, returns `ContentAreaNotFound` when there is
  none (it was `ContentExtractionFailed`, or the text of the browser's own panes as the page) and `OperationTimedOut`
  when the browser does not answer the search for it, and takes `url` from the page without reading the address bar. A
  child window's handle, such as a render widget's, is read as its top-level window's. On Chrome and Edge the tab's
  Document is the one beside the render widget's pane ("Chrome Legacy Window", which holds no address), so the page's
  address is read also while the browser is behind another window; a file page's path in the address bar (Chrome and
  Edge leave out `file:///`) is a URL, returned as its `file:///` URL. A browser window that stayed behind other windows
  since its page loaded may have no page to read: the `ContentAreaNotFound` and `UrlExtractionFailed` messages say so
  and point to CDP.

- **launch_browser_with_debug: first-run screens, port 0 and the started browser only (roadmap M5.1).** The browser
  starts with `--no-first-run`, `--no-default-browser-check`, `--disable-search-engine-choice-screen` and
  `--disable-sync`, so a new profile opens `url` instead of a welcome, sign-in or search engine screen. **Breaking:**
  `port` defaults to 0 (it was 9222): the browser picks a free port, the server reads it from the profile's
  `DevToolsActivePort` and returns it as `cdpPort`, which the reading tools need; an explicit port must now be
  1024-65535 (it was 1-65535, and 0 was refused). A client that assumed 9222 must pass `port: 9222` or use `cdpPort`.
  The browser is found through App Paths, Program Files, Program Files (x86) and `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, or the new
  `executablePath`, and no longer through `where.exe` (which searched the server's current directory); `BrowserNotFound`
  lists the places tried. The window wait counts only the started browser's windows, so `windowHandle` is never the
  user's own browser window, and a launch that a browser already running with that `userDataDir` took over now fails
  with `DebugLaunchFailed` instead of reporting a port nobody opened. The result adds `launchStatus` and `warning`, as
  launch_application reports them, and a failure after the start keeps `processId`, `windowHandle` and `userDataDir`
  while the browser runs. A `userDataDir` that a running browser holds (its `lockfile`) is refused with
  `DebugLaunchFailed` before anything is deleted or started, and a relative `userDataDir` with `InvalidArguments`.
  `launchStatus` `awaitingUserConsent` is now a `DebugLaunchFailed` failure (it was a success with the requested port).
  The reading tools' `cdpPort` descriptions and the CDP errors point at the `cdpPort` the launch returned, not 9222.

- **launch_browser_with_debug waits for its DevTools endpoint (roadmap M5.1, readiness).** Once the browser's port
  is known, the server asks `GET /json/version` on `127.0.0.1` and that port, for up to 10 seconds, and connects to
  nothing. The result adds `cdpReady` (true on success), `browserVersion`, `cdpEndpoint` (`http://127.0.0.1:<cdpPort>`)
  and `browserWsEndpoint` (the browser-level WebSocket URL, which must be `ws://` on 127.0.0.1 and that port, under
  `/devtools/browser/`). **Changed:** a launch whose endpoint does not answer in time, answers but not as a DevTools
  endpoint, or whose explicit port another process holds, now fails with `DebugLaunchFailed` and `cdpReady: false`
  (it was a success with a port nobody could read); the browser keeps running and the result still names its
  `processId`, `windowHandle`, `cdpPort` and `userDataDir`. A successful launch can take up to 10 seconds longer while
  the endpoint starts.

- **launch_browser_with_debug: a port that is not the browser's is not returned, and a dead browser ends the wait
  (roadmap M5.1, readiness).** When the port belongs to another process, or its listener cannot be read and the
  browser's `DevToolsActivePort` does not name the port and the `browserWsEndpoint` that answered, the failure's
  `cdpPort` is null (it was that port, and an unreadable listener counted as the browser's, with `cdpReady: true`);
  `processId`, `windowHandle` and `userDataDir` still name a running browser so that it can be closed. A browser that
  exits during the wait fails at once instead of after 10 seconds, and a `webSocketDebuggerUrl` that is not a URL is an
  answer that is not a browser's, refused at once (it was retried for 10 seconds as if nothing listened). The gate
  paragraph under [Window Control](#window-control) now names the two waits launch_browser_with_debug holds the input
  gate for.

- **The reading tools find a debug browser's port and bind its window (roadmap M5.3).** get_browser_url,
  get_active_browser_url and get_browser_content no longer need `cdpPort`: for a Chromium browser whose window's own
  process was started with `--remote-debugging-port` (as launch_browser_with_debug starts it), the port is read from its
  command line, or for port 0 from its profile's `DevToolsActivePort`, and used only when that process is the
  listener on 127.0.0.1; nothing is scanned. **Changed:** such a window is now read through CDP without `cdpPort`
  (`source: "cdp"`, and the result's new `cdpPort` names the port); `textOnly: false` returns its HTML instead of
  `HtmlRequiresCdp`. A browser started without a debug port reads through UI Automation as before. An explicit
  `cdpPort` still wins. `targetId` and `requireCdp` no longer need `cdpPort` (`targetId` without it was
  `InvalidArguments`); without a port of the window's own, they return `CdpUnavailable` (`CdpPortOwnerMismatch` when
  another process holds the port), saying why. **Changed:** with `cdpPort`, a port whose owner cannot be read is now
  `CdpPortOwnerMismatch` (it fell back to the title match alone); without `requireCdp` it falls back to UI Automation
  with that `cdpError`. The window is bound to its browser window (`Browser.getWindowForTarget`'s bounds and state)
  before its title picks the tab, so a tab of another window with the same title is no longer `CdpTargetAmbiguous`.
  New `useCdp` (default true): false reads through UI Automation only. The CdpTimeout and CdpResponseTooLarge messages
  point to `useCdp: false` instead of omitting `cdpPort`. The [target policy](#target-policy) covers the port found:
  a denied browser's command line is not read and it is not read through CDP without `cdpPort`
  (`TargetDeniedByPolicy`, also with `requireCdp` or `textOnly: false`). For port 0 only a profile folder on a local
  drive is read, at most 1 KB of its `DevToolsActivePort`. A `cdpPort` nothing listens on is `CdpUnavailable`.

- **get_browser_content returns pages (roadmap M5.6).** **Breaking:** `maxLength` defaults to 20,000 characters (it
  was the whole page, however large) and is read as at most 50,000; a page also holds at most 60,000 bytes of JSON.
  A client that left `maxLength` out to get a whole long page now gets its first page with `truncated: true`, and must
  call again with `offset: nextOffset` until `truncated` is false. New `offset` (0 or more, else `InvalidArguments`)
  and new result fields `offset`, `totalLength`, `truncated` and `nextOffset`, with read_element_text's paging;
  `contentLength` stays the page's length. Through CDP the page slices its own text, so only the page asked for
  crosses the DevTools connection and the new `totalLength` is the whole text's length, measured before it is cut
  (`contentLength` was the only length before); through UI Automation the Document's Text pattern is read a page at
  a time, `totalLength` comes with the last page, and read_element_text's `textSkipped` marks a page cut inside one of
  the provider's characters. Offsets count in the text of the result's `source`: an `offset` above 0 is read through
  CDP (the port given or found) and returns the CDP error instead of falling back to UI Automation, so a `uia` page
  continues with `useCdp: false` (a first page that fell back and has more says so in `cdpError`). New `selector` (CDP
  only, never falls back; `InvalidArguments` with `useCdp: false`): the text or HTML of each element a CSS selector
  matches, one per line; no match is `ContentExtractionFailed`, a selector that is not valid CSS `CdpEvaluationFailed`.
  Both go through the port lookup, window binding and target policy of the entry above. `CdpResponseTooLarge` no
  longer comes from a large page's content.

- **Debug-browser lifecycle: named profiles, reuse, close and cleanup (roadmap M5.4).** New tool close_debug_browser
  (toolset `browser`, destructive, audited, asks the user like kill_process): it closes a debug browser by its
  `processId` or `cdpPort` with Browser.close, ends what is left, and deletes its temporary profile; it closes only a
  browser this server started or whose command line shows a debug port and a profile in the server's own folders, and
  refuses anything else with the new code `NotADebugBrowser`. launch_browser_with_debug adds `profile` (a named profile
  kept under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\WindowsAppManagerMcp\browser-profiles`), `reuseIfRunning` (the debug browser running with
  the profile is returned with the new `launchStatus` `alreadyRunning` instead of `DebugLaunchFailed`) and `placement`
  (launch_application's), and its result adds `placement`. **Changed:** a new temporary profile is now
  `%TEMP%\WindowsAppManagerMcp\browser-debug\<32 hex digits>` (it was `%TEMP%\browser-debug-<guid>`); it is deleted when
  the browser did not start (the failure's `userDataDir` is then null), and leftovers older than 10 minutes that no
  browser holds are deleted by the next launch with a temporary profile. A call cancelled after the start now ends the
  browser it started and deletes its temporary profile (it kept running with an open port no result named), also when
  it is cancelled during the `placement` or while the start itself still runs (the profile is then deleted only after
  the browser is ended). The description's cleanup advice (find_windows, close_window, list_processes) is replaced by
  close_debug_browser.

- **Browser tabs, navigation and waits (roadmap M5.5).** Four new tools for a browser with a DevTools port, through
  CDP only: [list_tabs](#list_tabs) (a window's or a port's browser: each tab's `targetId`, `title`, `url` and
  `windowId`, the window's tabs marked `inWindow`, and `shownTargetId` when the window's title tells which tab it
  shows) and [wait_for_browser](#wait_for_browser) (until a page's URL, title or text contains a string or a CSS
  selector matches, polled on one connection), in the `browser` toolset; [activate_tab](#activate_tab) and
  [browser_navigate](#browser_navigate) (http, https or about:blank only, in the shown tab, a `targetId` or a new tab,
  waiting for `load`, `domcontentloaded` or nothing, with `httpStatus`, and `NavigationFailed` with the browser's
  `errorText`) in the new `browser-actions` toolset, which is **off by default**: the first toolset that an
  unconfigured server does not serve (`WAM_TOOLSETS=+browser-actions` adds it). They are refused while input is
  paused, take the input gate only to send their command, and are audited. New error code `NavigationFailed`; a load
  or wait that runs out of time is `WaitTimedOut`. Out-of-range `timeoutMs` values are refused, not clamped. The
  target policy applies to these tools also with an explicit `cdpPort`, and with `cdpPort` alone to the process that
  listens on it. The server instructions' wait line names wait_for_browser. A navigation whose server is slow to
  answer is `WaitTimedOut` (`loadState: "loading"`), not `CdpTimeout`, and `waitUntil: "none"` does not wait for the
  server; a page that replaces itself at once is followed; a download is `NavigationFailed` with `loadState:
  "download"`; a 4xx/5xx answer without a body is loaded with its `httpStatus`; a browser's DevTools endpoint on this
  computer is refused; a wait whose page answers no check is `CdpTimeout` (roadmap M5.5).
- **A thin DOM bridge, and Playwright MCP for the rest (roadmap M5.8).** Six new tools for a debug browser's page,
  through CDP only, without the real mouse or keyboard (no foreground change, also in a window behind others):
  [browser_element_rect](#browser_element_rect) (an element's `screenRect` and `clickPoint` in physical screen pixels,
  placed on the tab's Document through UI Automation or its render widget, scaled by `devicePixelRatio`),
  [browser_click](#browser_click), [browser_type](#browser_type), [browser_handle_dialog](#browser_handle_dialog) (also
  a dialog that was open before the call) and [browser_screenshot](#browser_screenshot) in the `browser-actions`
  toolset, and [browser_evaluate](#browser_evaluate) in the new `browser-script` toolset; both toolsets are **off by
  default**, and browser_evaluate needs `WAM_TOOLSETS=+browser-script` (with `+browser-actions` for the other five):
  a script runs with the page's rights and leaves no trace on the screen, so turning on clicks and typing does not turn
  it on. Elements are named by `selector`, `text` or `role`/`name`; several matches need `index`
  (`AmbiguousElement` otherwise). New error codes `ElementObscured` (another element covers the click point) and
  `BrowserInternalPage` (the tab shows one of the browser's own pages, which these tools never read or act on); they
  also return `ElementNotFound`, `AmbiguousElement`, `ElementNotEnabled`, `ElementOffscreen`, `FocusNotOnElement` and
  `DialogNotFound`. The actions are refused while input is paused, take the input gate only to send their commands,
  and are audited with lengths only. [Handing a debug browser to Playwright MCP](#handing-a-debug-browser-to-playwright-mcp)
  shows how to attach Playwright MCP with `--cdp-endpoint` to launch_browser_with_debug's `browserWsEndpoint` for
  anything richer.
- **The DOM bridge's checks (roadmap M5.8).** browser_element_rect refuses (`ContentAreaNotFound`) a tab whose page is
  not shown, a `targetId` that is not the tab its window shows, and a window that shows a Document of another address,
  instead of placing the element on the page the window shows; its `clickPoint` is the middle of the element's first box,
  as browser_click aims. Elements inside frames are measured on the page's own viewport and hit-tested frame by frame (an
  element in a frame whose parent is of another origin is `ElementObscured`). A span inside a disabled button, a control
  inside a disabled `<fieldset>` and anything under `aria-disabled="true"` are `ElementNotEnabled`. browser_click and
  browser_type send their scroll, focus and selection inside the input gate too, and a pause stops them between commands
  (`PausedByUser`, saying what was sent); a press that opens a dialog is still released. browser_type refuses a field the
  page moved the focus away from (`FocusNotOnElement`), and its `AmbiguousElement` no longer suggests `index`.
  `BrowserInternalPage` is an allow list of web pages,
  checked again on the call's connection, so extensions' `blob:` pages and `isolated-app:` pages are refused.
- **The DOM bridge's dialogs (roadmap M5.8, dialogs).** On real Chrome and Edge 155 DevTools never answers a JavaScript
  dialog that was open before its connection ("No dialog is showing", on the page's connection and on every session of
  the browser's alike), so browser_handle_dialog could not answer one, and the advice to use respond_to_dialog was wrong:
  Chromium draws the dialog inside the browser window, where respond_to_dialog finds none. Now
  [browser_click](#browser_click), [browser_type](#browser_type) and [browser_navigate](#browser_navigate) take `dialog`
  (`accept` or `dismiss`) and `promptText`, and answer the first dialog the action opens on their own connection; its
  `dialog` in the result has `answer` (`accepted` or `dismissed`), and browser_navigate's result has `dialog` too.
  Without `dialog` they report the dialog and leave it open, as before. **Breaking:**
  [browser_handle_dialog](#browser_handle_dialog) reads and answers the dialog a Chrome or Edge window shows through UI
  Automation (found by its views' classes and structure in every language, pressed with Invoke, a prompt's text set
  through its Value pattern): it takes the window (`handle` or `window`) and no longer `cdpPort` or `targetId`;
  `accept` is optional (without it the dialog is only read: `dialogType`, `dialogMessage`, `promptValue`); the result
  has `windowHandle`, `accepted` and `dialogClosed` instead of `targetId` and `cdpPort`. A confirm or prompt is accepted
  only once its text was read (new error code `DialogNotRead`). The `CdpDialogOpen` and `CdpTimeout` messages and docs
  point to browser_handle_dialog instead of respond_to_dialog.
- **Token budgets and additive consolidations (roadmap M6.1, budgets and additive consolidations).** Nothing is removed
  or deprecated, and every call that worked still works the same way. [get_monitors](#get_monitors) always returns
  `virtualScreen` (`x`, `y`, `width`, `height`: the bounds of all monitors together, as list_screens
  reports them). [set_window_bounds](#set_window_bounds)' `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` are no longer required: `x` and
  `y` alone move the window as move_window does, `width` and `height` alone resize it as resize_window does
  (`ResizeFailed`), and half a pair or no pair is `InvalidArguments` with nothing changed; its `bringToFront` is now
  optional (`["boolean", "null"]`), and left out it raises the window only when it is moved, so a call with all four
  still raises it. [get_browser_url](#get_browser_url) with `window: {"foreground": true}` and no other filter reads the
  browser in front as get_active_browser_url does, and returns `NoBrowserInForeground` (it returned `NotABrowser` when
  the window in front was not a browser). mouse_click's description now names every check a click gets instead of
  referring to click's. The toolsets table above has a Tokens column, and contract tests hold the default tools/list,
  each toolset and every single tool (at most 2,500 tokens) to a budget.
- **Deprecated tools and the window batches leave the default (roadmap M6.1, deprecations).** **Changed:** a server
  without `WAM_TOOLSETS` serves 58 tools instead of 70, about 51,000 tokens of tools/list instead of about 60,000. Nine
  tools that another tool replaced are in the new `deprecated` toolset, off by default: click, right_click and
  double_click ([mouse_click](#mouse_click)), move_window and resize_window ([set_window_bounds](#set_window_bounds) with
  one pair), get_all_windows ([find_windows](#find_windows)), get_primary_monitor and list_screens
  ([get_monitors](#get_monitors)), and get_active_browser_url ([get_browser_url](#get_browser_url) with
  `window: {"foreground": true}`). Their tool descriptions are one line that names the replacement; their arguments,
  results, input gate and audit lines are unchanged. `WAM_TOOLSETS=+deprecated` brings them back until 3.0.0, which
  removes them; a call to one that is not served is an unknown tool, never forwarded to its replacement.
  set_windows_bounds_batch, snap_windows_batch and set_windows_state_batch are in the new `windows-batch` toolset, off
  by default and not deprecated (`+windows-batch`); close_windows_batch and launch_applications_batch stay in the
  default. A moved tool is served only while the toolset it came from is on too, so `WAM_TOOLSETS=all` (which includes
  both new toolsets) or `+deprecated` never serves a configuration a tool it did not serve before (`all,-input` serves no
  click). A `WAM_TOOLSETS` list that names `windows`, `input`, `monitors` or `browser` no longer gets the moved tools from
  them: add `deprecated` or `windows-batch` to the list, and [get_server_info](#get_server_info)'s new `toolsets.moved`
  says where each tool that is out of reach went, with its replacement. `WAM_EXCLUDE_TOOLS` that names a moved tool is
  no error (it does not fail closed); a toolset's name there also excludes the tools that moved out of it. The server
  instructions name mouse_click instead of click, right_click and double_click, and take_screenshot, the window handle
  parameters, drag and get_control_status point to get_monitors, find_windows and mouse_click. See
  [Removed and moved tools](#removed-and-moved-tools).
- **Runs on .NET 10.** **Breaking:** the server targets .NET 10 (`net10.0-windows`) instead of .NET 8, which reaches
  end of support on 2026-11-10. The exe is still a framework-dependent single file, so the machine now needs the
  .NET 10 Desktop Runtime (x64): `dotnet --list-runtimes` must list `Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App 10.x`. With only the
  .NET 8 Desktop Runtime the exe exits at startup and the client lists none of its tools. The tools, their input
  schemas and their results are unchanged; [get_server_info](#get_server_info)'s `server.runtime` reports
  `.NET 10.0.x`.
- **list_processes: windows, parent, start time, integrity, filters and order (roadmap M6.6).** Every process now has
  `parentProcessId`, `startTime` (UTC, to the second), `integrityLevel` and `elevated`, `windows` (the handle and title
  of up to 10 of its windows, front to back) and, only when true, `aboveServer` (input to it is refused with
  `TargetElevated`); fields that cannot be read are left out. **Changed:** `windowCount` is the real count with
  `includeWindowless: true` too (it was 0 for every process), and the list is sorted by name, then `processId` (it came
  in the system's order). New optional parameters: `processId`, `pathContains`, `sortBy` (`name`, `memory` largest first,
  `startTime` newest first), `limit` (at least 1, no default, so the result is still the whole array; below 1 is
  `InvalidArguments`) and `includeCommandLine`, which returns the command line with secret-looking values masked as
  `***` (`commandLineRedacted: true`), cut to 500 characters, never for a process the user's policy denies, and only
  with `processId`, or `nameFilter` and a `limit` of at most 20 (else `InvalidArguments`). [get_window_info](#get_window_info) with
  `detail: "full"` reports the window's `integrityLevel`, `elevated` and `aboveServer` too; its other details and
  find_windows are unchanged.
- **Resources and prompts (roadmap M6.9).** The server also serves three read-only MCP resources, `wam://monitors`,
  `wam://windows` and `wam://layouts/{name}`, with the JSON of get_monitors, find_windows with no argument and
  get_layout, and four prompts, `automate_app`, `arrange_workspace`, `fill_form` and `diagnose_click`, recipes that
  name only the tools the server serves; see [Resources and Prompts](#resources-and-prompts). The `initialize` (and
  `server/discover`) result now advertises the `resources`, `prompts` and `completions` capabilities (completion offers
  layout names). Each follows the tools it rests on: `WAM_TOOLSETS`, `WAM_EXCLUDE_TOOLS` and `WAM_READ_ONLY` hide it
  with them. [get_server_info](#get_server_info) lists them in `toolsets.resources` and `toolsets.prompts`. tools/list
  is unchanged.
- **Several steps in one call (roadmap M6.2).** A new tool, [run_steps](#run_steps), in a new `steps` toolset that is on
  by default (59 tools by default; `WAM_TOOLSETS=-steps` turns it off). It runs up to 50 steps on one window, each a
  tool of an allow list with that tool's own arguments, under one hold of the input gate, and stops at the first
  failure. Nothing else changes for a client that does not call it, except that while a run holds the input gate (at
  most its `maxDurationMs`, 60 seconds), another input or window call waits for it, or gets `InputBusy` after 30
  seconds, as behind a slow launch. Each step writes its own [audit log](#audit-log) line under the request id
  `<run's id>#<step>`, besides the run's own line.
- **wait_for_visual (roadmap M6.4).** A new read-only tool in the new `visual` toolset, off by default
  (`WAM_TOOLSETS=+visual`): [wait_for_visual](#wait_for_visual) waits until a window, a region or a monitor changes on
  screen (`changed`, against a capture's `captureId` given as `since`, or the wait's first frame) or stops changing
  (`stable`), and returns where as rectangles, never an image. Frames are compared by a hash per 16 x 16 tile, a
  blinking text caret is left out, and over a region or monitor the windows the target policy denies are left out and
  listed in `maskedWindows`. The default surface is unchanged. While the toolset is on, captures (take_screenshot,
  capture_region, capture_window without `ref`, capture_with_elements) also keep a visual signature of their pixels with
  their `captureId`, at most 16 MB together, dropped before any `captureId` is; their results do not change. Read-only
  mode serves it when `visual` is on.
- **Text from pixels: read_screen_text and find_text_on_screen (roadmap M6.3).** Two new read-only tools in the new
  `ocr` toolset, off by default (`WAM_TOOLSETS=+ocr`), so the default surface does not change; tools/list with every
  toolset grows by about 2,100 tokens. They read a window, a region or a monitor with Windows OCR
  (`Windows.Media.Ocr`) for what UI Automation cannot read: [read_screen_text](#read_screen_text) returns lines (and
  with `detail: "words"` words) with screen-pixel `bounds`, [find_text_on_screen](#find_text_on_screen) matches text
  (`contains`, `exact` or `regex`) and returns each match's `clickPoint` and `imagePoint`. Each read is registered as a
  capture 1:1, so [mouse_click](#mouse_click) takes `imagePoint` with the result's `captureId` and refuses it with
  `StaleCapture` once the window moved. Below 150% scale the pixels are read at 2x (`ocrScale`); an image larger than
  OCR takes is read in overlapping tiles (`OcrTiled`). A window of an app the user's policy denies is refused
  (`TargetDeniedByPolicy`, as capture_window does), and in a region or monitor such windows are blacked out before OCR
  (`maskedWindows`). A minimized window is `WindowMinimized`: the tools only read, so nothing is restored and they take
  no input lock. New error codes: `OcrUnavailable` (no OCR language installed, or no Windows OCR) and
  `OcrLanguageNotInstalled` (the `language` asked for), both with `installedLanguages` and how the user adds a language;
  the server never installs one. The exe carries a projection of only the OCR types (CsWinRT, about 0.9 MB more), not
  the Windows SDK projection, so its minimum Windows version is unchanged.
- **Monitors by name, placement in percent, and the z-order (roadmap M6.7).** Every tool that took `monitorIndex`
  (snap_window, move_window_to_monitor, snap_windows_batch's items, take_screenshot, read_screen_text,
  find_text_on_screen, wait_for_visual and the `placement` of launch_application, launch_applications_batch and
  launch_browser_with_debug) has a new `monitor` parameter (`"type": ["integer", "string"]`): an index, `"primary"`,
  `"left"`, `"right"`, `"current"` (the foreground window's monitor), a monitor `id` or device name from
  [get_monitors](#get_monitors), or `"all"` where a capture takes every monitor; see
  [Monitor selectors](#monitor-selectors). New error codes `MonitorNotFound` and `AmbiguousMonitor` (`"left"` with two
  stacked monitors). **Deprecated:** `monitorIndex` keeps working on every one of them until 3.0.0 removes it (owner
  decision D1), and its description now only says to use `monitor`; giving both is `InvalidArguments`.
  **Changed:** move_window_to_monitor's `monitorIndex` is no longer required in the schema (one of `monitor` and
  `monitorIndex` is, else `InvalidArguments`). [set_window_bounds](#set_window_bounds) takes `unit: "percent"` with
  `relativeTo` (`workArea`, the default, or `monitor`) and `monitor`; its `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` are JSON numbers
  now (integers before), and in pixels a value that is not whole is `InvalidArguments`. A new tool in the default
  `windows` toolset, [set_window_zorder](#set_window_zorder) (`top`, `bottom`, `topmost`, `notopmost`, `above`), changes
  a window's place in the z-order without activating it, with the new error code `ZOrderNotApplied`; it takes the input
  gate like the other window changes (60 tools by default). [get_server_info](#get_server_info) lists the windows it
  made topmost in `pinnedWindows`. [get_monitors](#get_monitors) (and `wam://monitors`) report each monitor's `id`,
  `friendlyName`, `dpi`, `isInternal` (only when true) and `relation` to the primary; find_windows rows (and
  `wam://windows`, get_window_info's standard detail) carry `isTopmost: true` for a topmost window and leave it out
  otherwise. The audit log records a launch placement's `monitor` when it is a keyword, an id or a device name, and an
  index as `monitorIndex`. The default tools/list grows by about 1,190 tokens, every tool together by about 1,500.
- **Packaged apps, installed apps and runAsAdmin (roadmap M6.5).** A new read-only tool in the `launch` toolset, on by
  default (61 tools by default): [list_installed_apps](#list_installed_apps) lists the Start menu's apps with `name`
  (localized), `appId`, `packaged` and a desktop app's `path` (`nameFilter`, `limit` 1-200, default 25). **Changed:** a
  packaged app's `appId`, as `shell:AppsFolder\<appId>` or bare, is now activated: the result has the app's own
  `processId` and, with `waitForWindow`, `windowObserved` with its window (it was `possibleHandoff` without a
  `processId`, and needed `expectWindow`); an activation that takes over 15 seconds is `timedOut`. On an elevated server
  it is still started through the shell, without `processId`, with a `warning`. **Changed:** arguments to a packaged app
  or a `shell:AppsFolder` entry are refused with `InterpreterWithArguments` when its program is an interpreter (Windows
  Terminal, PowerShell, Python, a WSL distribution) or cannot be told; they were passed on unchecked. **Changed:** a bare
  name that is no program on disk but an installed app's exact display name now launches that app, with a `warning`
  (it was `ExecutableNotFound`); a name of several apps is the new `AmbiguousApp`. New parameter `runAsAdmin` on
  launch_application and on each launch_applications_batch item starts an `.exe` elevated; where Windows would not show a
  UAC prompt (UAC off or not asking administrators, the built-in Administrator, an elevated server, an unreadable policy)
  the user is asked through the client, shown the resolved program and its masked arguments, and only that launch runs;
  the result's new `elevation` (`confirmed`, `uacPrompt`) says how it was approved, and the audit line records it. A
  `shell:AppsFolder` entry that starts a script is refused (`ScriptFile`). New error codes: `AmbiguousApp`, `ActivationFailed`,
  `ElevationNotConfirmed`, and `ConfirmationDeclined` for launch_application. launch_application now takes the input gate
  itself, after that question, so a question never holds it; its gating is otherwise unchanged.
- **Layouts: schema version 2, layouts an agent writes, and a dry run (roadmap M6.8).** No new tools: the `layouts-v2`
  toolset an earlier version of this document promised is not coming (owner decision D15). **Changed:** save_layout now
  records, per window, its monitor's id and EDID name, a maximized or minimized window's restore rectangle, and what
  `launchMissing` starts (`launch`: the program, or a packaged app's `appId`; never arguments; nothing for a window the
  target policy denies), so apply_layout's `launchMissing` now starts programs for captured layouts, where it started
  nothing before; `launchCommand` holds the same for older versions. Presets are written as schema version 2 and keep
  every version 1 field, so an older plugin version still applies them (and drops the new fields if it saves under the
  same name); files of earlier versions are read as they are and never rewritten. New: save_layout's `includeMinimized`
  and `placements` (agent-written placements with snap positions, monitor names and launches, checked strictly:
  `InvalidPlacement`; get_layout's placements go back in unchanged), apply_layout's `dryRun` (status `dryRun`,
  placements `wouldApply` or `wouldLaunch` with `target`) and `placements` (a subset by index). **Changed:**
  apply_layout finds a saved monitor by its id wherever it is now, then by its name, then by its index, and says which
  in `monitorFallback`; a monitor that fits none is `MonitorNotFound`. A maximized placement is first given its restore
  rectangle, then maximized (a brief move may show; maximize still activates), and one already maximized on its monitor
  is left alone; a minimized window that stays minimized is given its restore rectangle without being shown. Launches go
  through launch_application's plan (packaged apps are activated, scripts refused, the window found whichever process
  opens it). apply_layout now takes the input gate itself, after any question to the user, so a dry run neither waits
  for the gate nor stops while input is paused. Before an agent-written layout starts anything, the user is asked once
  per version of it; without a yes, or on a client that cannot ask, those placements fail with `LaunchNotConfirmed`.
  launch_application's and the batch's `placement` now find a named monitor again by its id when the window appears,
  and fail with `MonitorNotFound` when it is gone. Any `authoredBy` marks a preset as agent-written; the confirmation
  guards against agents with only the MCP tools, not against anything that can write the layouts folder, and older servers
  ignore `authoredBy` and launch without asking. A layout's launches are checked by launch_application's planning, in a dry
  run too; save_layout refuses fields it does not take, rectangles past the work area and more than 8 launches.
- **Partial launch paths are refused.** **Changed:** launch_application, launch_applications_batch and apply_layout's
  launches refuse an `executable` with a folder but no drive and root (`tools\app.exe`, `.\app.exe`, `\tools\app.exe`,
  `C:app.exe`, or a command line such as `cmd.exe /c x`) with `InvalidPath`, and start nothing. Such a path was found
  from the server's current folder or drive, which the client does not choose, with only a warning. Full paths, network
  paths (`\\server\share\app.exe`, still with a warning), bare names, URIs and AppUserModelIDs are unchanged.
- **Workspaces (roadmap M7.5).** A new toolset, `workspaces`, off by default, with [save_workspace](#save_workspace)
  (save_layout's preset plus each File Explorer window's folder and each browser window's pages, cleaned of secret-looking
  values) and [restore_workspace](#restore_workspace) (opens the missing folders and pages, then applies the preset as
  apply_layout with launchMissing; `dryRun`). Layout presets gain an optional `content` per placement, which apply_layout
  and older servers ignore. restore_workspace is audited with what it opened. The default tools/list is unchanged.
- **Takeover detection (roadmap M7.4), opt-in.** New environment variable `WAM_TAKEOVER_DETECTION` (`off` by default,
